drought.details: BIO 9544 is identified as a drought-tolerant or water stress-tolerant variety. It is explicitly recommended as a drought-tolerant choice for maize cultivation and is listed among varieties for 'climate-smart agricultural technologies' in contexts of low-water input management. Evaluation reports also identify it as tolerant to drought stress.

heat.details: The variety is listed in documents discussing 'High-temperature and heat wave stress' in climate-smart agricultural technologies. Field days and evaluations associated with BIO 9544 have also touched upon 'Heat-stress-induced changes'.

salinity.details: BIO 9544 is listed within documents that address 'developing salt-tolerant varieties for coastal salinity'. While not explicitly stated as salt-tolerant, its inclusion in such contexts suggests its potential or evaluation for this trait.

flood.details: Maize, in general, is susceptible to waterlogging. While BIO 9544 has been subject to phenotyping for 'Waterlogging Stress', the provided results do not confirm its tolerance to flood or waterlogging. Some documents state that maize cannot tolerate water logging and requires well-drained soil.

disease_resistance.summary: BIO 9544 was found to be moderately resistant to an unspecified disease, compared to a check variety, Kaveri-50.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: BIO 9544 is characterized as a high-yielding variety and is frequently used as a check variety in yield performance assessments. Reported yields include 12.772 t/ha (for fodder maize) and 63.25 q/ha (6.325 t/ha) and 49.71 q/ha (4.971 t/ha) for grain in different zones and evaluations.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety is used as a 'best check' in heterosis studies for yield across locations and evaluated at multiple locations, suggesting good stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation during the Kharif season and also suitable for the Summer season (February–June) and summer fodder cultivation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Grains are orange-yellow and semi-dent type.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensively evaluated in multi-location trials across various zones (e.g., Zone-I, Zone III) and states including Himachal Pradesh and Delhi, often serving as a check variety for both grain and fodder maize hybrids.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2 or FSCH 75 with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. The only sweet corn stress hits were unrelated hybrids (for example, Sugar 75 and Pusa Super Sweet Corn).

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page named this variety with disease or pest resistance. Results for rust, leaf blight and virus resistance were about other sweet corn hybrids.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No yield, maturity or trial data for VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2 or FSCH 75 was returned. The "Sugar 75" front-line demonstration study (florajournal.com) is a different variety and was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The parentage VSL 26 x VSL 27 appears only in the request record and was not confirmed by any search result. The VPKAS sh2 backcross paper (researchgate.net/publication/332760677) names other parental lines (VLS3, VQL373) and does not name this variety, so it was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/12335
Institution: The VPKAS seed portal lists "VL Sweet Corn 2" under Maize Hybrids -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
Notification: At its 97th Foundation Day (4 July 2020), the Director said the institute had notified "VL Sweetcorn 2" in maize -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/12335
Breeder names: No evidence found. No page named the lead breeder or scientist for this variety. "VL Sweetcorn Hybrid 202" in the same article is a different variety and was not attributed.

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
ICAR-VPKAS, Mall Road, Almora-263601, Uttarakhand (India); phone +91-5962-230208 -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize
Email: No evidence found.
Institute contact page: No evidence found beyond the maize page above.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report or KrishiKosh record naming VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2 or FSCH 75 was returned. The VL Madhurima (isgpb.org) sweet corn paper and the VL VitA paper are different varieties and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
VPKAS seed portal, Maize Hybrids category, lists "VL Sweet Corn 2 / स्वीटकाॅर्न हाईब्रिड 2" (listing only; no price or stock detail in the snippet) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found. The FSCH 75 name returned no seed listing.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Listed on VPKAS seed portal as: Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand (hills), Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya (listing truncated after this point) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
The request's full list (Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura) was not confirmed by a search result.

NAME NOTE
"VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2" and "VL Sweet Corn 2" / "VL Sweetcorn 2" appear to refer to the same variety. No search result contained the Seednet name "FSCH 75 VL Sweet Corn Hybrid 2," so all findings above refer to the CSC-style name.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RECORD CONFLICTS (read first): The input record describes this as a millet with a 2010 release year, but the sources split it into two different hybrids that share the code 86M64. The pearl millet record (MH 1540, notified 7.2.2011, S.O. 283(E)) matches the input's crop, states and parentage-style code. The IIMR maize record (LPCH 3 = IMHP 1540, popcorn, gazette S.O. 3482(E), 7 October 2020) matches the Seednet name and the parentage Dpcl 15-90 x Dpcl 117. Neither matches the 2010-10-10 release date. Evidence for each heading below says which name it refers to. Four searches were used (the maximum), so seed availability got only incidental coverage.

STRESS TOLERANCE
MH 1540 (pearl millet, 86M64): listed as resistant to downy mildew -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
IMHP 1540 (maize): No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance -- searched via https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

DISEASE AND PEST
MH 1540 (pearl millet): downy mildew resistance noted -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
IMHP 1540 (maize): No evidence found for disease or pest resistance -- searched via https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
IMHP 1540 / LPCH 3 (maize): kharif yield 3.5-4.0 t/ha, also suited to rabi, maturity not stated -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
IMHP 1540 / LPCH 3 (maize, secondary blog): kharif yield 3.5-4.0 t/ha; listed for several eastern and northern states -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/exploring-varieties-of-maize-in-india
MH 1540 (pearl millet): late maturing, with conical compact earheads and light grey obovate seeds -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Multi-location trial data for either hybrid: No evidence found in the retrieved AICRP kharif maize 2016 excerpt -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
IMHP 1540 (maize) parentage: Dpcl 15-90 x Dpcl 117 -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
MH 1540 (pearl millet) parent listing is ambiguous in the table: 86M64 appears alongside "M096F x M" and 117R -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
QTL or marker studies for either hybrid: No evidence found. Maize QTL papers returned by the search used unrelated populations and were not listed.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
IMHP 1540 (maize): developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana, PAU Campus; no lead breeder name found -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
MH 1540 (pearl millet): notified under Pioneer Overseas Corp., Hyderabad; no breeder name found -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Unlinked IIMR scientists (not confirmed as breeders of this hybrid): G. K. Chikkappa, N. Sunil, Vinay Mahajan, Bhupender Kumar -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/node/120825

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found in searched sources for disease resistance of J 1009 or J-1006. The Krishi Bazaar handbook recommends fodder maize varieties in general and mentions disease resistance only for hybrids, not for J-1006.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. The Kashmir trial reports that 120 kg N/ha gave the highest green fodder yield, but the digest gives no numeric yield value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data appeared in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Not found in searched sources for agro-climatic fit of J 1009 or J-1006 in the four CSC-listed states (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh). The Kalyani centre page gives a sowing window of May to August. Identity caveat: all search evidence refers to J-1006 (Seednet name). No source names J 1009 or PFM 13, so the link to J 1009 is unconfirmed.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seller copy only (not trial data): the Indiamart listing describes J-1006 as tall (about 7 to 8 feet) with 8 to 11 percent crude protein and a seed rate of 10 to 15 kg/acre. Kalyani centre page: seed rate 50 to 60 kg/ha and spacing 45 x 50 cm.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Identity caveat: these trial and variety results refer to J-1006, not confirmed as J 1009. (1) Kashmir field trial, 2009 and 2010: tested seed rate and nitrogen/zinc on J-1006; 120 kg N/ha gave the highest green fodder yield, crude protein and plant height. (2) Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana study: tested planting methods (zero tillage, conventional tillage, bed planting) and N levels for J-1006 seed yield; no numeric results in digest. (3) Forage-quality trial: lists J-1006 alongside other maize types with green fodder figures; table units unclear, so numbers not used. (4) Kalyani centre variety page: sowing window May to August, seed rate 50 to 60 kg/ha, spacing 45 x 50 cm (agronomic recommendation, not a trial result). (5) Indiamart listing: seller claims of height, crude protein and seed rate; not trial data. No stress-tolerance trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: J 1009 / J-1006 (maize, fodder)

Name note: All four searches returned evidence only for "J-1006", the Seednet name. I found nothing that names "J 1009" or the code "PFM 13". I cannot confirm that J 1009 and J-1006 are the same entry. The findings below refer to J-1006 unless stated otherwise. Searches used: 4 (the maximum).

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of J-1006 or J 1009 in the four searches. -- No URL with relevant content

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for disease or pest resistance of J-1006 or J 1009. The Krishi Bazaar handbook recommends fodder maize varieties generally and mentions disease resistance only for hybrids, not for J-1006. -- https://krishibazaar.in/blog/maize-cultivation-in-india-a-farmers-handbook

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A Kashmir field trial (2009 and 2010) tested seed rate and nitrogen/zinc on J-1006. It reported that 120 kg N/ha gave the highest green fodder yield, crude protein and plant height. -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/4604/4279
- A Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana study tested planting methods and N levels for J-1006 seed yield (zero tillage, conventional tillage, bed planting). -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/Rupinder%20Kaur%20Jassal,%20et%20al.pdf
- A forage-quality trial lists J-1006 alongside other maize types, with green fodder figures. The table units are unclear, so I have not used the numbers. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/forage-quality-of-maize.pdf
- A Kalyani centre variety page lists J-1006 with sowing window May to August, seed rate 50 to 60 kg/ha and spacing 45 x 50 cm. -- https://rsfpdkalyani.com/varietymain.php?id=70&category=Maize+(J-1006)
- The Indiamart listing describes J-1006 as tall (about 7 to 8 feet) with 8 to 11 percent crude protein and a seed rate of 10 to 15 kg/acre. This is seller copy, not trial data. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-maize-j-1006-2856922031312.html

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker or pedigree data for J-1006 or J 1009 were returned. Parentage is not specified in the input, and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist for J 1009 or J-1006.
- The NDDB page lists J-1006 among improved fodder maize varieties, without a developer. -- https://www.nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/fodder/cereals/maize
- The Kalyani centre page lists J-1006 among its varieties, but does not say it was developed there. -- https://rsfpdkalyani.com/varietymain.php?id=70&category=Maize+(J-1006)
- Institution per input only: ICAR-AICRP on Forage Crops, Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. Not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone or postal address for PAU's AICRP on Forage Crops appeared in the results. The Kalyani centre page is a different forage centre and I have not treated its details as PAU contacts. Please check the PAU and AICRP Forage Crops websites directly for an institute contact page.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in the source (year not stated). Evaluation of maize cultivars for herbage yield and silage quality, with a J1006 composite silage comparison. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354947120_Maize_Zea_mays_cultivars_evaluation_for_herbage_yield_and_silage_quality
- Jassal, R. K. et al. (2017, from the issue number in the URL). Growth, phenology and seed yield of fodder maize (J-1006) in relation to planting method and nitrogen level. Int. J. Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences (ijcmas) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/Rupinder%20Kaur%20Jassal,%20et%20al.pdf
- Authors not stated in the source (2012, from the page header). Seed rate and nutrient management in fodder maize (var. J-1006). Indian Journal of Agronomy -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/4604/4279
- Authors not stated in the source (year not stated). Forage quality of maize, with J-1006 yield comparisons. Forage Research -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/forage-quality-of-maize.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Amar Seeds Private Limited (Pune, Maharashtra) lists "Fodder Maize J-1006" as in stock, with a note that it is notified for fodder cultivation. This is a private dealer listing, not an NSC, State Seed Corporation or SAU source. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-maize-j-1006-2856922031312.html
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sale for J 1009 was found. Seednet listings were not reachable in these searches.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found for Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra or Uttar Pradesh for J 1009 or J-1006. The Indiamart seller says J-1006 is recommended across the country, but this is a commercial claim and does not match the four states in the input. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-maize-j-1006-2856922031312.html

RELEASE RECORD
The 2024-08-02 release date and the CSC minutes could not be checked. No search result confirmed a 2024 release for J 1009 or PFM 13. The J-1006 evidence points to an older Punjab fodder variety, so the two records may not describe the same variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Standability/lodging resistance is claimed for the hybrid; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found -- https://kisanshop.in/product/advanta-pac-751-elite-hybrid-maize-seeds (retailer page; also https://agribegri.com/products/advanta-pac-751-elite-f1-hybrid-maize-seeds.php)
Strong standability and good yield potential under varied conditions are claimed; no numbers -- https://rytusevak.com/product/advanta-pac-751-elite-maize-seeds/

DISEASE AND PEST
Pest protection is claimed in marketing text only; no named pests, diseases or resistance scores were found -- https://agribegri.com/products/advanta-pac-751-elite-f1-hybrid-maize-seeds.php
No evidence found for disease resistance ratings in any official or research source.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Medium maturity and high shelling efficiency (up to 84%) are claimed; no trial data -- https://rytusevak.com/product/advanta-pac-751-elite-maize-seeds/ and https://kisanshop.in/product/advanta-pac-751-elite-hybrid-maize-seeds
Seasonal schedule lists Kharif (May–July) and Rabi (September–October) sowing for PAC 751 / 751 ELITE -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/advanta-pac751-elite-corn-seeds
Procurement notice: "Advanta Pac 751" was listed among hybrids supplied to a Tapioca and Castor Research Station, Yethapur; this is a supply brief with no trial results -- https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?id=GALE%7CA765383057&sid=sitemap&v=2.1&it=r&p=AONE&sw=w
No multi-location or AICRP trial results found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage "751F x 751M" was not found in any search result. No QTL or marker studies found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found for a named breeder or developing scientist. The pages name the brand "Advanta" (and in one listing "Bayer"), not UPL Limited, and no page links this variety to UPL Limited. The "Bayer" mention is on a dealer page for other products (DEKALB) and was discarded for attribution.
Brand/marketing reference only: https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/advanta-751-maize-hybrid-seed-2854258362588.html

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for breeder or institute contacts (no official email, phone, address or contact-page URL for UPL Limited or Advanta research units was returned). Retailer contacts are not recorded here because they are not institute contacts.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The research query returned only retailer pages and the Yethapur procurement brief (https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?id=GALE%7CA765383057&sid=sitemap&v=2.1&it=r&p=AONE&sw=w). No KrishiKosh, AICRP, ICAR or journal items were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Multiple private retailers list the hybrid (4 kg packs): https://www.desikheti.com/products/advanta-pac751-elite-corn-seeds ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pac-751-elite-corn-seeds-2853152161112.html ; https://www.indiamart.com/shriram-krishi-udyog/maize-seed.html ; https://rytusevak.com/product/advanta-pac-751-elite-maize-seeds/
One retailer marks it "Currently Unavailable" -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/pac751-corn
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Madhya Pradesh is named as a region of strong performance -- https://kisanshop.in/product/advanta-pac-751-elite-hybrid-maize-seeds ; https://www.indiamart.com/sanjaybrothers/bayer-seeds.html (Ratlam, MP dealer listing for Advanta 751 Maize Hybrid Seed, variety name PAC 751)
This is marketing or dealer information, not an official CSC or state notification. The CSC release record (2019-06-01, Madhya Pradesh) could not be verified from these searches.

NAME CHECK
Variety name (CSC) and Seednet name are both "PAC 751". No Seednet portal page was returned, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Crop fits as maize (hybrid). Searches used: 4 (the maximum).

agronomic_details.yield: Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 (agri news item): average 13.0 t/ha green cob yield, 9.3 t/ha dehusked cob yield (potential 10.2 t/ha) and about 16.2 t/ha green fodder. Original data field 'average_yield' is recorded in Kg/Ha without a value. Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 (IARI page, not confirmed as the Seednet ASKH1 entry): average yield 95.0 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Across-environment stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Agri news item: released for NHZ, NWPZ, NEPZ and PZ zones (conflicts with the CSC zone list of Hill region, North Eastern Hill Region, Plain, Western region, Eastern region, NEPZ and PZ; needs checking against official minutes). IARI page for Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2: recommended for HP, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, TN, Karnataka, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 78 days to maturity for Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 (agri news item). Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 (IARI page): 77 days. The original data field 'maturity_days' is 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 is a shrunken-2 (sh2) based sweet corn hybrid with average sugar of about 15.9 Brix, suited to fresh consumption, processing and the food industry (IARI page). Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 is an sh2 hybrid with 16.4% Brix and kharif sowing. Morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No variety-specific trial report, KrishiKosh thesis, or AICRP/ICAR annual report entry was found. Summaries of available results: (1) Agri news item for Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1: 13.0 t/ha green cob, 9.3 t/ha dehusked cob (potential 10.2 t/ha), about 16.2 t/ha green fodder, about 78 days to maturity, about 15.9 Brix. (2) IARI page for Pusa Super Sweet Corn-1: up to 15.9 Brix; no yield or maturity given. (3) IARI page for Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 (not confirmed as ASKH1): 16.4% Brix, 95.0 q/ha average yield, 77 days maturity. (4) Sowing/harvest-time study of 25 sh2sh2 genotypes: kernel Brix 16.1-25.5%; Pusa lines not named in the snippet.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Microsatellite (SSR) diversity study of sh2, su1 and double-mutant sweet corn inbreds: 39 inbreds from the ICAR-IARI specialty corn programme, 8 from the IIMR Winter Nursery Centre and 1 from CIMMYT; Pusa variety-specific parentage not stated. Functional SNP marker Sh2_rs844805326 identified by GWAS (250 maize lines) for classifying sh2 sweet corn; no chromosomal position given for the SNP in the digest. Marker data specific to Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 or 2 not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL mapping results specific to Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 or 2 found in searched sources. Related (non-QTL) finding: in a sowing/harvest-time study of 25 sh2sh2 genotypes, genotype, sowing time and harvest time explained 33.8%, 9.1% and 3.9% of variation in kernel sweetness, respectively; the paper does not name Pusa lines.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The sh2 (shrunken-2) gene is the basis of the super sweet trait and is located on chromosome 3L. GWAS identified sh2 as the candidate sweetness gene in 250 maize lines. Pathway-level detail: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 / Pusa Super Sweet Corn 2 (ASKH1), maize, ASKH4

Name note: The evidence for "Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1" comes from an agri news item and the IARI ZTM&BPD product page. The IARI page lists "Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2" as a separate hybrid with different data. I found no source that links "ASKH1" or "ASKH4" to either name, so treat the Seednet code mapping as unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance under either name. -- searched in Searches 1 and 3; no stress data in the results.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for disease or pest resistance under either name. -- searched in Search 1; no resistance data in the results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 is a shrunken-2 (sh2) based sweet corn hybrid with average sugar of about 15.9 Brix, released for NHZ, NWPZ, NEPZ and PZ. -- https://agriicarjrf.com/2019/11/25/new-sweet-corn-variety-pusa-super-sweet-corn-1/
- Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 averaged 13.0 t/ha green cob yield, 9.3 t/ha dehusked cob yield (potential 10.2 t/ha), and about 16.2 t/ha green fodder, with about 78 days to maturity. -- https://agriicarjrf.com/2019/11/25/new-sweet-corn-variety-pusa-super-sweet-corn-1/
- Pusa Super Sweet Corn-1 (IARI page): sh2 hybrid, up to 15.9 Brix, suited to fresh consumption, processing and food industry. No yield or maturity given on that page. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/maize/
- Pusa Super Sweet Corn-2 (IARI page, not confirmed as the Seednet ASKH1 entry): sh2 hybrid, 16.4% Brix, average yield 95.0 q/ha, kharif sowing, 77 days maturity, recommended for HP, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, TN, Karnataka, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/maize/
- Sowing/harvest-time study of 25 super sweet (sh2sh2) genotypes: kernel Brix ranged 16.1–25.5%, and genotype, sowing time and harvest time explained 33.8%, 9.1% and 3.9% of variation in sweetness. The paper does not name Pusa lines in the snippet. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-77-3-003
- Sweet corn package-of-practices standardized and popularized in India (review). -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12355-014-0305-6

GENETICS AND QTL
- sh2 (shrunken-2) gene is the basis of the super sweet trait, located on chromosome 3L. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5391363
- Microsatellite diversity study of sh2, su1 and double-mutant sweet corn inbreds: 39 inbreds from ICAR-IARI specialty corn programme, 8 from IIMR Winter Nursery Centre, 1 from CIMMYT. Pusa variety-specific parentage not stated. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5391363
- GWAS on 250 maize lines identified sh2 as the candidate sweetness gene and a functional SNP marker (Sh2_rs844805326) to classify sh2 sweet corn. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8235792/
- Parentage: not specified in any result. Pedigree/parent lines for ASKH1/ASKH4 not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, specialty maize work under the Directorate of Maize Research, Pusa Campus, New Delhi (now ICAR-IIMR lineage). -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/maize/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12355-014-0305-6
- Lead breeder name for Pusa Super Sweet Corn 1 or 2: No evidence found in any result. The sh2 inbred paper credits the ICAR-IARI specialty corn programme without naming a lead breeder. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5391363

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Fodder Maize-1 (maize, fodder)
Name check: The retrieved sources call the variety "Shalimar Fodder Maize-1" or "SFM-1." None of the sources used the Seednet code "KDFM-1," so no evidence was found under that name. The Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1, Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, Shalimar KG Maize-1/-2, Pusa Shalimar, and African Tall results were excluded as different varieties.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance in Shalimar Fodder Maize-1. The searches returned only the entries below.
- SFM-1 is described as moderately resistant to stem borer and aphids -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378775424_Productivity_of_Fodder_Maize_Zea_mays_L_SFM-1_under_Varied_Sowing_Dates_and_Nitrogen_Levels

DISEASE AND PEST
- SFM-1 is described as resistant to turcicum leaf blight and common rust -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378775424_Productivity_of_Fodder_Maize_Zea_mays_L_SFM-1_under_Varied_Sowing_Dates_and_Nitrogen_Levels
- The same source gives moderate resistance to stem borer and aphids, which is listed under Stress Tolerance above.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The variety is reported at a maturity of 75 to 80 days with green fodder yield potential of about 46 t/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378775424_Productivity_of_Fodder_Maize_Zea_mays_L_SFM-1_under_Varied_Sowing_Dates_and_Nitrogen_Levels
- A kharif 2022 sowing-date and nitrogen trial (four sowing dates from 15 April to 15 July; nitrogen 0 to 180 kg/ha) was run at the Crop Research Farm, Division of Agronomy, SKUAST-K, Wadura. Early April sowing gave the highest green fodder yield, and 180 kg N/ha was at par with 120 kg N/ha -- https://doi.org/10.9734/jsrr/2024/v30i82245
- The same trial data appear in the Nisar et al. paper -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/view/5031
- A kharif 2019 Wadura field trial compared SFM-1, PMC-6 and J-1006 as sub-plot treatments. Results were not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378775424_Productivity_of_Fodder_Maize_Zea_mays_L_SFM-1_under_Varied_Sowing_Dates_and_Nitrogen_Levels

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage is recorded as GM-6 x C8 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378775424_Productivity_of_Fodder_Maize_Zea_mays_L_SFM-1_under_Varied_Sowing_Dates_and_Nitrogen_Levels
- No evidence found for marker, QTL, or DNA fingerprinting studies on SFM-1. The DNA fingerprinting results retrieved belong to Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, a different hybrid, and were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The Nisar et al. paper lists authors S. Nisar, Z. Rashid, A. Touseef, R. Kumar, S. U. Nissa, J. Faheem and others. One author's affiliation is the Dryland Agriculture Research Station, Rangreth, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/view/5031. These are paper authors, not confirmed breeders of the variety.
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The retrieved text does not name the breeder.
- Developing institution: the input record gives Dryland Agriculture Research Station, Rangreth with SKUAST-Kashmir. The paper's author affiliation supports the station link. No breeding-origin statement from the institute was retrieved.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No official email, phone number, postal address, or institute contact page for the Dryland Agriculture Research Station, Rangreth, or for SKUAST-K tied to SFM-1 was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Nisar S, Rashid Z, Touseef A, Kumar R, Nissa SU, Faheem J et al. (year not confirmed in retrieved text). Productivity of Fodder Maize (Zea mays L.) SFM-1 under Varied Sowing Dates and Nitrogen Levels. Journal not named in retrieved text (URL path indicates IJBSM) -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/view/5031
- Authors not retrieved (2024). Effect of Sowing Dates and Nitrogen Levels on Growth, Yield, Quality and Economics of Fodder Maize (Zea mays L.) SFM 1. Journal of Scientific Research and Reports -- https://doi.org/10.9734/jsrr/2024/v30i82245
- No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR reports, or conference papers on SFM-1 were found in the results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Shalimar Fodder Maize-1 from NSC, the J&K State Seed Corporation, KVKs, SKUAST seed sales, or private dealers. The results returned only African Tall fodder maize listings (IndiaMART, Pioneer Agro, TNAU), which are a different variety and were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The input record gives UT of Jammu & Kashmir. No CSC release notification or Seednet page confirming this, or the release date of 17 June 2022, was retrieved.
- Supporting context only: the SFM-1 trials were run at Wadura and Sopore in Kashmir -- https://doi.org/10.9734/jsrr/2024/v30i82245

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JK Samriddhi Gold (JKMS-2), mustard, JK Agri Genetics Ltd.

Name note: The search returned evidence under "JK Samriddhi Gold" only. No Seednet page for "JK Smriddhi Gold (JKMS-2)" or the code JKMS-2 appeared in any result, so the Seednet name is unverified. The raw recommended state "Uttar Pradesh" was not confirmed by any source. The company page says "All mustard growing states" instead.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Company product page lists the variety as tolerant of salinity, aphid, frost and shattering (pod shattering). Drought and heat, flood, and submergence were not mentioned. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jk-samriddhi-goldtolerant-for-salinity-aphid-frost-and-shattering/

DISEASE AND PEST -- Company product page gives disease reaction as moderately tolerant of WR (white rust) and DM (downy mildew). Aphid tolerance is listed under stress tolerance above. No resistance data from trials was found. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jk-samriddhi-goldtolerant-for-salinity-aphid-frost-and-shattering/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Company product page gives: maturity 130-140 days (full-duration); sowing 4th week of September to 4th week of October; flowering 50-60 days; medium-tall plant with profuse branching and long main shoot; 17-19 seeds per pod; bold dark-brown seed of 5.5-6.5 g per 1000 seeds (weight as stated); oil content 40-42%. Yield data and multi-location trial results were not found. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jk-samriddhi-goldtolerant-for-salinity-aphid-frost-and-shattering/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage is unspecified in the record, and no pedigree, marker, or QTL source was found for this variety. The searches returned only unrelated results (for example, a Brassica juncea nanoformulation paper and an unrelated hybrid comparison that lists "Kesari Gold" and other entries, not this variety).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developer is JK Agri Genetics Limited (JKAGL), which states it runs breeding facilities for mustard and other crops, with over eighty scientists and several research stations across agro-climatic zones. No named lead breeder or scientist for this variety was found. -- https://jkagri.com/ ; https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder name, email, phone, or postal address for this variety was found. Only the company home page was retrieved, and it contained no address, email, or phone number in the captured text. Company contact page not located. -- https://jkagri.com/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The publication search returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming JK Samriddhi Gold or JKMS-2. Results were about other mustard hybrids, other crops, or unrelated products.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Company mustard category page lists JK Samriddhi Gold as a product for sale. -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/mustard/ ; No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or independent dealer listing specifically for this variety was found. Dealer results for "JK" mustard were for unrelated spices or products. -- https://www.bighaat.com/collections/jk-agri (JK Agri field crop range lists Mustard, but does not confirm this variety)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Company page says "All mustard growing states" for area of adoption. No Uttar Pradesh recommendation or CSC/state notification was found, so the raw "Uttar Pradesh" value is unconfirmed. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jk-samriddhi-goldtolerant-for-salinity-aphid-frost-and-shattering/

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION -- No official CSC release minutes, Seednet notification, or ICAR/SAU record was found in the searches. The 2016-08-12 release date in the record is unverified. Searches were limited to four queries, and Seednet and ICAR/SAU sites were not reached.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches for "MEPH-126 rice variety" and "PHR 126 variety seednet" returned no page naming MEPH-126 or PHR 126 as a rice variety. The results were PR 126, a Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) rice variety, plus unrelated crops and products. PR 126 was discarded as a name resemblance.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The same searches returned nothing on MEPH-126 or PHR 126 disease or pest resistance. The PR 126 pages were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No MEPH-126 or PHR 126 field-trial, maturity or yield data were returned. The PR 126 yield and maturity pages were discarded as a different variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The "MEPH-126 rice research paper trial" search returned no QTL, marker or pedigree study for this variety. It returned unrelated pages, such as Methylobacterium trials, Bt rice in Iran and IRRI platform pages.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. The "MEPH-126 rice breeder developed by institute contact" search returned no breeder name or developing institution for MEPH-126. It returned IRRI platform pages and an unrelated IR8 page. Nothing links those to this variety, so none are attributed. The institution field "MahycoPvt. Ltd." was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute or company contact for MEPH-126 was retrieved. The IRRI contact details that appeared (info@irri.org, +63 2 8580 5600) belong to IRRI and are not linked to this variety, so they are not recorded here.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference item naming MEPH-126 or PHR 126 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The "PHR 126 variety seednet" search returned the Seednet "Newly Notified Varieties" index (https://seednet.gov.in/material/Agriculture_Variety.htm), but the retrieved text showed only mustard and oilseed category headings and no PHR 126 entry. Seed listings for "PR 126 paddy" from private dealers (Flipkart, Agrikendra, TradeIndia) were discarded because they concern PR 126, not MEPH-126 or PHR 126.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The recommended-states list (Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) could not be verified. PR 126 recommendations for Punjab and North India were discarded.

NOTES
1. Searches run (4 of 4): "MEPH-126 rice variety"; "PHR 126 variety seednet"; "MEPH-126 rice breeder developed by institute contact"; "MEPH-126 rice research paper trial". The search budget was used up before the seed-availability query (search 4 in the plan) could be run on its own.
2. Name conflict: the CSC name is MEPH-126 and the Seednet name is PHR 126. Neither name returned evidence.
3. Crop conflict: the input says rice, but the Seednet crop field says Mustard. The Seednet index page retrieved lists mustard and oilseed categories. This needs checking before the record is used.
4. Data-entry issue: the variety code "MRP 5222) (IET 25269" has an unbalanced bracket and should be checked against the source.
5. Unverified inputs: the release date (2020-11-09), the institution (MahycoPvt. Ltd.), the parentage (not specified) and the recommended states all come from the input only. No retrieved source confirms them.
6. Suggested next steps: check the CSC release minutes for the exact name, and query seednet.gov.in directly for the PHR 126 notification entry under Rice, not Mustard. Then check the Mahyco company site or the ICAR/State variety release notifications for MEPH-126.

heat.details: A seedling-stage heat study found most double-zero cultivars susceptible. The tolerant double-zero lines named were JC-21 and JC-33, and PDZ-1 was not among them. No direct PDZ-1 heat evidence was found, so the tolerance level cannot be determined.

agronomic_details.yield: Official average seed yield is 2379 kg/ha. In 16-location AICRP-RM trials over four years in Zone II, the weighted mean yield was 2334 kg/ha, about 5.7% above the low-erucic checks PM-21 and RLC-2. The AVT-I peak was 2766 kg/ha at Navgaon in 2015-16, with oil yield of 958 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: The digest reports a four-year, 16-location Zone II mean with a yield advantage over checks. Stability statistics (for example, GxE or variance measures) are not reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for timely sown irrigated conditions in Zone II (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Jammu, Rajasthan). The IARI NCR recommendation covers the NCR of Delhi plus parts of Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, timely sown irrigated.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Oil content 40.56% in yellow seed. Erucic acid below 2% and glucosinolates below 30 ppm (first double-zero Indian mustard). Described as fairly tolerant of pod shattering in a breeder-style review.
agronomic_details.field_trials: AICRP-RM 16-location trials over four years in Zone II; AVT-I trials under rainfed conditions (drought indication) and AVT-I peak at Navgaon in 2015-16.

YIELD (OFFICIAL): Average seed yield stated as 2379 kg/ha, with about 144 days maturity and 40.56% oil in yellow seed. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/oil-seeds/mustard/

drought.details: SL 979 is identified as one of the most tolerant soybean varieties to drought stress based on RT-PCR analysis. It shows a significantly low value of 5.42 percent under moisture stress, indicating high tolerance. It is also tolerant to the combined stress of drought and salinity. The variety is listed among those considered tolerant to abiotic (drought) stress, especially during summer.

heat.details: SL 979 is listed among varieties that are considered in the context of tolerance to heat and drought stress, particularly in summer conditions. However, specific high tolerance is not explicitly stated as it is for drought or salinity.

salinity.details: SL 979 is tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity. It has been part of analyses to identify tolerant genotypes under salt stress and is listed among varieties suitable for saline/sodic soils.

flood.details: SL 979 is mentioned in the context of yields in flood-prone areas, but its specific level of tolerance to general flood conditions is not explicitly stated.

disease_resistance.summary: SL 979 is resistant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) and Soybean Mosaic Virus (SMV). It was also found to be moderately resistant to an unspecified disease.

pest_resistance.summary: SL 979 is listed among varieties that exhibit resistance or tolerance to abiotic and biotic stresses, including Caterpillar.

seednet_fields.Parentage: TM102 X TM28 TM102 is Interspecific recombinants and TM28 is yellow and Bold seed coat mutant.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated condition during Rabi/winter season of W.B. and also suitable for irrigated eco-system of zone-V (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam, Manipur).
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to lodging and seed shattering. Reponse well to recommended fertilizer @ 140: 70: 70 kg NPK/ha. With 30 cm. X 10cm. spacing: Seed rate: 7kg/ha.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Waxy leaves and bold glossy seeds, Long main fru
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Leaves dark green, flower yellow colour, pods two locules with prominent constriction. Leaf suface rough.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately resistant to alternaria leaf spot up 75 days after sowing.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): N: P2O5:K2O @ 140:70:70, N in three splits (50% as basal, 25% at 30 days after sowing and 25% at 45 days after sowing).

drought.details: No drought tolerance score for TBM-204 was found in the retrieved text. The variety is described as irrigated rabi/winter-season material in the adaptation evidence, which does not establish drought performance. Not found in searched sources.

heat.details: No TBM-204-specific heat trial or heat tolerance score was found. A zenodo heat-stress paper cites the TBM-204 notification but does not name TBM-204 as tested; that source was discarded as evidence for this variety.

salinity.details: Coastal (saline-zone) trials at BCKV Kakdwip with TBM-204 under late sowing were reported in a 2019 paper, but no salinity score was reported in the retrieved text. The backcross mapping population was developed at the RRS Coastal Saline Zone (2018-20) but no salinity result was retrieved.

flood.details: No flood tolerance score or evidence for TBM-204 was found in the retrieved text.

disease_resistance.summary: Field tolerance to Alternaria blight and white rust is reported for TBM-204 in the notification paper. No severity scores or disease levels were given in the retrieved text, so no resistance level is assigned. Note: the digest lists lodging and seed-shattering resistance (not a disease) as stated in the notification paper; the BCKV source records disease_reaction as 'Not Specified' in the original variety data.

pest_resistance.summary: Field tolerance to aphid (insect pest) is reported for TBM-204 in the notification paper. No other pest data was found. No severity scores were given, so no resistance level is assigned.

agronomic_details.yield: Average seed yield of 1336 kg/ha over 4 years of multi-location trials in West Bengal (notification paper), against Kranti (1211 kg/ha), Pusa Bold (1159 kg/ha) and B-9 (948 kg/ha). Attainable yield of 1500-1800 kg/ha under optimum sowing and management (notification paper). BCKV crop-variety table: seed yield 15.0 q/ha (equivalent to 1500 kg/ha). Oil content 41% (notification paper and BCKV table).
agronomic_details.stability: Over three years at 13 BCKV locations (2013-16), TM 204 showed a 10-15% yield advantage over Kranti and Pusa Bold. Coastal Kakdwip trial (2014-16): seed yield statistically at par with the best entry. Multi-location average across 4 years in West Bengal is reported in the notification paper. No formal stability statistic (e.g., AMMI or GGE) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated rabi/winter season in West Bengal (digest adaptation evidence). Tested in the IVT (rabi 2016-17, Zone-V, timely-sown rainfed) and in coastal saline-zone trials at Kakdwip under late sowing. Zone-V state list (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam, Manipur) appears in the ORIGINAL VARIETY DATA only and is not confirmed by the digest's trial evidence. Agronomy: fertilizer at 140:70:70 kg NPK/ha; spacing 30 cm x 10 cm; seed rate 7 kg/ha; resistant to lodging and seed shattering (original variety data and notification paper).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110 To 95Days (duration conflict in the digest: 100 days per ResearchGate figure, 110 days per BCKV table, 115 days per notification paper; all three recorded, not resolved)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Waxy leaves and bold glossy seeds, Long main fru (original text is truncated in the source). BCKV table: plant height 155-160 cm; test weight 4.7 g. Yellow seed coat (notification paper). Resistant to lodging and seed shattering.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Notification paper IVT, rabi 2016-17, Zone-V, timely-sown rainfed: 23% yield gain over national check Kranti. (2) Notification paper, 4-year multi-location trials in West Bengal: mean 1336 kg/ha vs Kranti 1211, Pusa Bold 1159, B-9 948. (3) 2013-16 multi-location trial at 13 BCKV locations: TM 204 gave 10-15% yield advantage over Kranti and Pusa Bold over three years (no authors retrieved). (4) Coastal Kakdwip trial, 2014-16: TM 204 gave the highest siliqua count on the main axis and seed yield statistically at par with the best entry. (5) Coastal West Bengal fertilizer x variety trial included TBM 204 and TBM 143; no result for TBM-204 was retrieved. (6) Coastal late-sowing trials at Kakdwip (2019 paper): no salinity score reported. (7) Backcross mapping population (2018-20) linked to TBM-204; no yield or QTL result retrieved. No heat trial was found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: SSR marker analysis gives distinct alleles for TBM-204 versus Kranti and Pusa Bold. No marker names or positions were reported in the retrieved text. Pedigree: TM102 x TM28. TM102 is an interspecific recombinant; TM28 is a yellow-seeded, bold-seeded mutant.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: A backcross mapping population (2018-20, RRS Coastal Saline Zone) is linked to TBM-204 in the same paper, but no QTL result was retrieved. QTLs and effects: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TBM-204 (CSC release-minute name) / TM-204 (Seednet name), mustard (Brassica juncea)

Name note: The journal paper and BCKV pages use "TBM-204" or "TBM 204". The BARC-BCKV programme page and the coastal trial paper use "TM-204" or "TM 204". The Seednet portal was not reachable through search, so no Seednet record was found. Under each heading below, the evidence refers to the name shown in the source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Field tolerance to aphids, Alternaria blight and white rust is reported for TBM-204 in the notification paper -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- The variety is reported as not lodging or shattering at maturity -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Coastal (saline-zone) trials at BCKV Kakdwip with TBM-204 under late sowing were reported in a 2019 paper -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602 (no salinity score was reported in the retrieved text)
- No drought, flood, submergence or heat tolerance score for TBM-204 was found in the retrieved text. A 2025 seed-priming study on TBM-204 seed quality does not give a stress score -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-09325-z

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerance to aphid (insect pest) and to Alternaria blight and white rust under field conditions -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No other pest or disease data for TBM-204 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notification paper: 23% yield gain over national check Kranti in the IVT (rabi 2016-17, Zone-V, timely-sown rainfed) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Notification paper: average seed yield of 1336 kg/ha over 4 years of multi-location trials in West Bengal, against Kranti (1211), Pusa Bold (1159) and B-9 (948) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Notification paper: attainable yield 1500-1800 kg/ha under optimum sowing and management; harvest about 115 days after sowing; oil content 41% -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- BCKV crop-variety table: duration 110 days, plant height 155-160 cm, test weight 4.7 g, seed yield 15.0 q/ha, oil 41% -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Note the duration conflict: 100 days (ResearchGate figure), 110 days (BCKV table), 115 days (notification paper). Record all three.
- 2013-16 multi-location trial at 13 BCKV locations: TM 204 showed 10-15% yield advantage over Kranti and Pusa Bold over three years -- https://cwss.in/Journal/Complete_jurnal/Vol.13-No.1__22.pdf (the year is 2013-16, the journal volume is 13; no author list was retrieved)
- Coastal Kakdwip trial (2014-16): TM 204 gave the highest siliqua count on the main axis and seed yield statistically at par with the best entry -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/89005
- Fertilizer x variety trial in coastal West Bengal included TBM 204 and TBM 143 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- Heat stress: no TBM-204-specific heat trial was found. A zenodo heat-stress paper cites the TBM-204 notification but does not name TBM-204 as tested -- https://zenodo.org/records/18681400 (discarded as evidence for this variety)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree breeding: TM102 x TM28 cross made at BARC Trombay -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- TM102 is an interspecific recombinant; TM28 is a yellow-seeded, bold-seeded mutant -- same URL
- SSR marker analysis gives distinct alleles for TBM-204 versus Kranti and Pusa Bold -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- A backcross mapping population (2018-20, RRS Coastal Saline Zone) is linked to TBM-204 in the same paper; no QTL result was retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Flow-chart-showing-development-and-evaluation-of-backcross-mapping-population-used-in_fig1_344401463

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead authors (all Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia): Amitava Dutta (first author), Sanjay J Jambhulkar, Archana N Rai, Shankar Bhujbal, H Banerjee, R Das, S Dewanjee, S Sarkar, M Pramanik, S Mandal -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Development was a collaboration between BARC (Trombay, Mumbai) and BCKV -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- BARC affiliation of the paper: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay, Mumbai 400085 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- Applicant on the BCKV variety list: BCKV -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address (BCKV, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, PIN 741252) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf ; same address on the notification paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No breeder email, phone or direct institute contact page was found in the retrieved results. Institute-level contact only: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia 741252, West Bengal.
- BARC-BCKV programme page: https://bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/barc-bckv-programme-en (no contact details on the retrieved text)

PUBLICATIONS
- Dutta A, Jambhulkar SJ, Rai AN, Bhujbal S, Banerjee H, Das R, Dewanjee S, Sarkar S, Pramanik M, Mandal S (2019). Trombay Bidhan Mustard-204 (TBM-204): A high yielding yellow seed coat mustard [Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. & Coss.] variety notified for West Bengal. Journal of Oilseeds Research 36(4): 220-224 -- https://doi.org/10.56739/jor.v36i4.136693 (the ResearchGate page dates it September 2020; the journal volume is 36(4))
- Dutta A, Jambulkar SJ, Rai AN, Bhujbal S, Banerjee H, Das R, Dewanjee S, Sarkar S, Pramanik M, Mandal S (2019). Varietal and Fertilization Effects on Growth and Yield of Mustard under Coastal Environment. Journal of Interdisciplinary Sciences / JISCAR -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- Authors not retrieved (year not stated; journal Vol. 13 No. 1). Performance of yellow coated mustard (Brassica juncea L.) in West Bengal (2013-16 trials) -- https://cwss.in/Journal/Complete_jurnal/Vol.13-No.1__22.pdf
- Authors not retrieved (year not stated). Selection of Rapeseed-mustard Varieties in Coastal Region of West Bengal: A Way Forward to Rice-fallow Intensification. JISCAR -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/89005
- Authors not retrieved (2025). Physiological, biochemical and enzymatic quality parameters of primed seed of rapeseed-mustard genotypes. Scientific Reports -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-09325-z
- Not found: KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entries, or a conference paper naming TBM-204 in the four searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The searches (run once on seed availability) returned only unrelated seed sellers (mustard greens, culinary seed, wheat "TAM 204", Sinapis alba) and a commodity exchange page. None names TBM-204 or TM-204.
- BCKV variety table lists the variety but gives no seed-sale information -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- No NSC, WB State Seed Corporation, KVK, BCKV seed sales or private dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal, notified for cultivation in that state -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Notification reference: S.O. No. 3220(E), 5 September 2019 (the journal says CVRC; the BCKV table says SVRC; check which committee before citing) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal ; https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Release year 2019 is consistent across sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Napier Grass Culture 21

Name note: The CSC name "Napier Grass Culture 21" and the Seednet name "Napier Grass Culture-21" both appeared in the searches, but neither exact string matched any result. Every finding below is about Napier grass (Pennisetum purpureum) in general, or about other named Napier varieties. None of it is confirmed as referring to this variety. Four searches were run, the maximum allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No variety-specific evidence found. A general review says Napier grass growth and nutritive value are limited by low temperatures and drought, and that pearl millet x Napier hybrids were developed partly to improve drought tolerance -- https://gms.ctahr.hawaii.edu/gs/handler/getmedia.ashx?moid=3787&dt=3&g=12
Flood, submergence, salinity: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No variety-specific evidence found. The same Hawaii document describes Napier grass as generally resistant to most pests and diseases, with no variety named -- https://gms.ctahr.hawaii.edu/gs/handler/getmedia.ashx?moid=3787&dt=3&g=12

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No variety-specific evidence found. A 2017 MDPI review gives a general yield figure for Napier cultivars of about 60 t dry matter/ha/year -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/7/2/28 . A 2025 study titled "Growth-Stage dependent nutritional dynamics of super Napier grass" is listed on ResearchGate; it does not name Napier Grass Culture 21 in the retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367817651_Lignocellulosic_Bioethanol_Production_of_Napier_Grass_Using_Trichoderma_reesei_and_Saccharomyces_cerevisiae_Co-Culture_Fermentation (related listing; the specific 2025 item was seen only as a title fragment).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No variety-specific evidence found. General Napier grass QTL and genotyping work exists, for example a 2024 whole-genome resequencing study of a global collection that mentions yield QTL -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12239605/ . Parentage for this variety is not known and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder or developing institution found for Napier Grass Culture 21. A ResearchGate listing of Napier hybrids attributes NB 21, BN 2, CO 1, CO 2 and CO 3 to TNAU; these are other varieties, and no link to this one was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366739789_Hybrid_napier_grass_a_potential_asset_for_livestock_production . Whether this variety was developed by TNAU or another institute is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, scientist, email, phone, address or institute contact page for this variety was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No publication naming this variety was found. Related general items:
Authors not captured in search result (2017). Opportunities for Napier Grass (Pennisetum purpureum) Improvement Using Molecular Genetics. Agronomy 7(2):28. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agronomy7020028
Garg, S.; Meel, M. S.; Gautam, L. (2025). Growth-Stage dependent nutritional dynamics of super Napier grass. Journal not confirmed from the search text (listed on ResearchGate, May 2025). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367817651 (related listing; title and authors are partial)

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No seed source for Napier Grass Culture 21 was found. Retailers found sell generic or differently named Napier seed: Livingstone, Vattappara, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, sells "Super Napier Grass Seeds" -- https://www.indiamart.com/livingstone/lawn-grass-seeds.html ; RK Seeds sells Napier grass seed on IndiaMart -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rk-seeds-napier-grass-seeds-elephant-grass-seeds-pennisetum-purpureum-pack-of-1-kg-21502286688.html ; Farmson Biotech Napier seed on BigHaat -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/farmson-biotech-napier-grass-seeds . No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sale was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found that this variety is recommended for Kerala or any other state. The only Kerala link is the Thiruvananthapuram seed retailer above, which does not establish a recommendation.

RELEASE AND METADATA -- Year of release (NaT) and parentage remain unknown. The crop label "millet" does not match the Seednet entry "Napier grass (elephant grass)"; Napier is a forage grass related to pearl millet, not a millet.

drought.details: Napier grass is described as drought tolerant and persistent, but this is generic to the species and not confirmed for CO-4 or for the Seednet/CSC entry. A Kerala water-stress study names CO-3, CO-5 and Super Napier, not CO-4. No CO-4 specific drought mechanism or trial data were found. The variety name is matched to CO-4 by inference only.

heat.details: No CO-4 specific heat tolerance data were found.

salinity.details: No CO-4 specific salinity tolerance data were found.

flood.details: No CO-4 specific flood tolerance data were found.

disease_resistance.summary: No CO-4 specific disease resistance evidence was found. Napier grass is described generically as vulnerable to disease and pest attacks, not CO-4 specific. The KVK Pathanamthitta page attributes pest and disease resistance to CO-3, not CO-4. No diseases with confirmed resistance in CO-4 are reported in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No CO-4 specific pest resistance evidence was found. Napier grass is described generically as vulnerable to pest attacks. The KVK Pathanamthitta page attributes pest resistance to CO-3, not CO-4. No pests with confirmed resistance in CO-4 are reported in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: CO (CN) 4 gave a mean green fodder yield of 382 t/ha/year (reported in the MASU source), a 33 per cent increase over the check CO 3. The ICAR-IVRI Izatnagar trial of Co 4 recorded a maximum green fodder yield of 307.7 q/ha in 2015-16. Units differ between the two sources (t/ha versus q/ha) and both are reported as given. These are general CO-4 references, not confirmed for the Seednet/CSC entry.
agronomic_details.stability: The ICAR-IVRI trial (2013-14 to 2017-18, irrigated, UP) recorded a yield fall in the fourth year. Ratoon regrowth was good, and the crop was judged productive for 5-6 years. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CO (CN) 4 is described as well adapted to Tamil Nadu. Kerala is listed among major Cumbu Napier growing states. KVK Pathanamthitta (Kerala) offers CO-4 slips, which is use evidence and not an official recommendation. The ICAR-IVRI trial was conducted under irrigated conditions in UP. No Kerala-specific CO-4 trial data were found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified for CO-4. Generic Napier grass takes about 3-4 months after planting for first harvest, with cuts every 6-8 weeks (not CO-4 specific).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CO (CN) 4 is a triploid, so it is sterile and propagated vegetatively. Planting rate for Cumbu Napier seed/slip is 33,333 two-eye stem cuttings per hectare at 60 x 50 cm, and planting can be done year-round under irrigation. Ratoon regrowth was good in the ICAR-IVRI trial. Morphological characteristics were not found in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) MASU/TNAU release paper: mean green fodder yield of 382 t/ha/year, a 33 per cent increase over the check CO 3. (2) ICAR-IVRI Izatnagar trial of Co 4 (2013-14 to 2017-18, irrigated, UP): maximum green fodder yield of 307.7 q/ha in 2015-16, yield fell in the fourth year, ratoon regrowth was good, and the crop was judged productive for 5-6 years. (3) Hybrid CO-3, CO-5 and Super Napier were evaluated under water stress with irrigation in humid tropical Kerala; CO-4 is not named in that study. (4) The North Konkan Zone of Maharashtra study on Bajra Napier hybrid varieties is listed in the digest as a publication only, with no result data in the digest. No Kerala-specific CO-4 trial results were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found for CO-4 in searched sources. A whole-genome resequencing study of a global Napier collection (ILRI-led) and a genetic study of Napier genotypes for biomass, water-use efficiency and feed quality are not CO-4 specific, and the digest gives no marker names or positions. A KAU Vellayani RAPD characterisation of 15 Napier accessions from AICRP centres is also not linked to CO-4 marker data in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not CO-4 specific. The ILRI-led whole-genome resequencing and QTL study reports QTL for yield and feed quality in a global Napier collection. The genetic and QTL study of Napier genotypes reports on biomass, water-use efficiency and feed quality. No QTL effects for CO-4 were found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

commercial_info.private_dealers: A private Namakkal seller lists Cumbu Napier CO-4/CO-5 slips, currently out of stock. Private Super Napier seed listings (Vattappara, Kerala; RK Nursery) are not CO-4.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Napier Grass Culture 4 (variety_name) / Napier Grass Culture-4 (seednet_variety_name), crop: millet (Napier grass / elephant grass), variety code A062216651

Name mapping: No search result mentioned "Napier Grass Culture 4" or "Napier Grass Culture-4" as a named variety. The closest match is the TNAU hybrid CO (CN) 4 / CO-4 (Cumbu Napier), which is cited below. Every finding under the headings below refers to CO-4 by inference from the name, not to a confirmed record for the CSC or Seednet entry. The CSC release minutes, the release year, and the parentage for this exact entry were not found. Parentage is given only for CO-4 as a general reference.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Napier grass is described as drought tolerant and persistent, but this is generic to the species, not CO-4 specific -- https://ekishaan.com/napier-and-its-cultivation/
- Napier grass is described as drought tolerant and vulnerable to disease and pest attacks, again not CO-4 specific -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/igc/23/2-6-1/36
- Hybrid CO-3, CO-5 and Super Napier were evaluated under water stress with irrigation in humid tropical Kerala; CO-4 is not named in that title -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268381528_Hybrid_Napier_Pennisetum_perpureum_X_Pennisetum_americarnum_VAR_CO-3_a_resourceful_fodder_grass_for_dairy_development_in_Sri_Lanka (reference list entry)
- No CO-4 specific heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data were found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The KVK Pathanamthitta page attributes pest and disease resistance to CO-3, not CO-4 -- https://kvkcard.org//products.php
- No CO-4 specific disease or pest resistance evidence was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CO (CN) 4 is a triploid, so it is sterile and propagated vegetatively -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/96-7-12-291-292.pdf
- CO (CN) 4 gave a mean green fodder yield of 382 t/ha/year, a 33 per cent increase over the check CO 3 -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/96-7-12-291-292.pdf
- ICAR-IVRI Izatnagar trial of Co 4 (2013-14 to 2017-18, irrigated, UP): maximum green fodder yield of 307.7 q/ha in 2015-16; yield fell in the fourth year; ratoon regrowth was good and the crop was judged productive for 5-6 years -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=6529&context=igc
- Napier grass generally takes about 3-4 months after planting for first harvest, with cuts every 6-8 weeks -- https://ekishaan.com/napier-and-its-cultivation/
- Cumbu Napier seed/slip planting rate: 33,333 two-eye stem cuttings per hectare at 60 x 50 cm; can be planted year-round under irrigation -- https://kvknamakkalfodder.com/product/cumbu-napier-grass-slips/
- Kerala-specific CO-4 trial data were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- CO (CN) 4 came from a cross of Cumbu CO 8 with Napier FD 461 made in 2001 -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/96-7-12-291-292.pdf
- Another source describes CO-4 as a pearl millet x Napier cross made at TNAU Coimbatore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374536154_A_High_Yielding_Cumbu_Napier_Hybrid_Grass_CO_CN_4
- Whole-genome resequencing and QTL study of a global Napier collection (ILRI-led): QTL for yield and feed quality, not CO-4 specific -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12239605/
- Genetic and QTL study of Napier genotypes for biomass, water-use efficiency and feed quality, not CO-4 specific -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8776657/
- KAU Vellayani RAPD characterisation of 15 Napier accessions from AICRP centres -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7

- Authors of the release paper: G. Vijayakumar, C. Babu, K. Velayudham, T.S. Raveendran -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/96-7-12-291-292.pdf

disease_resistance.summary: Field resistance to Alternaria leaf spot and Cercospora leaf spot is reported in the research source (field conditions). In a natural-epiphytotic leaf spot screen of 21 niger cultivars, GNNIG-4 was among seven entries with a PDI of 12.42%, but the resistance category in the table was not legible in the snippet, so its reaction class is unconfirmed. The same screen classed GNNIG-3 (the Seednet name, a different earlier release) as resistant to Alternaria blight; this does not apply to GNNIG-4.

pest_resistance.summary: Reported resistance under field conditions to leaf-eating caterpillar and semilooper. No other pest reaction data was found. The Pest Reaction field in the original variety data is 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Station trials (2016-18): 543 kg/ha. AICRP trials over three years: 598 kg/ha grain yield. Oil content 37.77%; oil yield 205 kg/ha. Input data lists average_yield as Not Available.
agronomic_details.stability: Results are reported across station trials, three years of AICRP trials and 30 farmers' fields. No explicit stability statistic (for example, a GxE or stability index) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif or late kharif, as sole crop or intercrop; kharif rainfed conditions in Gujarat. No agro-climatic zone details beyond Gujarat were found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Bold seed of 4.08 g per 1000 seeds; greenish-purple stem. Input morphological_characteristics is 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials 2016-18 against checks GN-2, GNNIG-3 and IGPN-2004-1: GNNIG-4 averaged 543 kg/ha, which is 43.65%, 34.07% and 41.40% above those checks respectively. (2) AICRP trials over three years: 598 kg/ha grain yield, 27% above national check IGP-67. (3) Adaptive trials at 30 farmers' fields: the variety was favoured over checks GN-2 and IGPN-2004-1 (no yield figures given in the digest). (4) Leaf spot natural-epiphytotic screen of 21 niger cultivars: GNNIG-4 among seven entries with PDI 12.42%, reaction class unconfirmed. Note: the GNNIG-3 2016 AICRP entry (400-450 kg/ha, 32-35% oil, 110-115 days) refers to a different variety and is not GNNIG-4 data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Name check: the CSC name is GNNIG-4 (NMBP-1907). The Seednet name GNNIG-3 is a different, earlier release, so evidence about GNNIG-3 below does not describe GNNIG-4. I found no Seednet listing for GNNIG-4. Searches used: 4 (variety/release, breeder, research, and a combined contact/seed query).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Notified in 2021 as GNNIG-4 for kharif rainfed conditions in Gujarat (ex-NMBP-1907) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for GNNIG-4 was found in any result. -- No evidence found (searched; see the research and release sources above)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to Alternaria and Cercospora leaf spot and to leaf-eating caterpillar and semilooper under field conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- In a natural-epiphytotic leaf spot screen of 21 niger cultivars, GNNIG-4 was among seven entries with a PDI of 12.42%; the resistance category in the table was not legible in the snippet, so its reaction class is unconfirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393367222_Screening_of_Niger_Cultivars_Genotypes_for_Resistance_to_Leaf_Spot_Disease_Under_Natural_Conditions
- The same screen classed GNNIG-3 (the Seednet name) as resistant to Alternaria blight; this applies to GNNIG-3, not GNNIG-4. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393367222_Screening_of_Niger_Cultivars_Genotypes_for_Resistance_to_Leaf_Spot_Disease_Under_Natural_Conditions

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Medium maturity of 127 days; bold seed of 4.08 g per 1000 seeds; greenish-purple stem; suited to kharif or late kharif as sole or intercrop. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Oil content 37.77% and oil yield 205 kg/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Station trials (2016–18) against GN-2, GNNIG-3 and IGPN-2004-1; the abstract reports 543 kg/ha, which is 43.65%, 34.07% and 41.40% above those checks respectively. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- In AICRP trials over three years, 598 kg/ha grain yield, 27% above national check IGP-67. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382945849_101_Niger_Guizotia_abyssinica_L-_An_Underutilized_Oilseed_Crop_with_High_Value (search result 20-3; the page is the same ResearchGate record: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State)
- Adaptive trials at 30 farmers' fields also favoured it over checks GN-2 and IGPN-2004-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Seednet GNNIG-3 (a different, 2016 release): 400–450 kg/ha, 32–35% oil, 110–115 days, bold shining black seed. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed by mass selection from a mutated population of RCR-317 (15 kr). This conflicts with the input parentage ("selection from local cultivar"). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- No QTL or marker study for GNNIG-4 was found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by Navsari Agricultural University (NAU) through the Niger Research Station, Vanarasi (Tal. Vansda), with the All India Coordinated Research Project on Niger at the same station. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Lead author/scientist: Prashant Jagtap, NRS Vanarasi (listed as author; full author list not confirmed). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- P. M. Mistry is listed on a ResearchGate profile as an NAU, Surat scientist with this paper under Publications; his role in the breeding is not stated. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/P-Mistry
- Seednet GNNIG-3 breeder/institute: no separate source found; the 2016 AICRP entry is the only record. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Jagtap P., Niger Research Station, NAU, Vanarasi-396580, Gujarat; email listed as pacific7@rediffmail.com (a personal-domain address, not an official NAU domain; verify before use). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Niger Research Station Vanarasi, Tal. Vansda, Distt. Navsari-396580, Gujarat (state government directory entry); the listed phone numbers (+91-11-26562122/25/33/44, 26567373, 26962819) are Delhi numbers from a national directory and are not confirmed as the station's. -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/niger-research-station-vanarasi-0
- NAU head office: Eru Char Rasta, Dandi Road, Navsari 396450, Gujarat; phone (02637) 283794; email registrar@nau.in. -- https://nau.in/index
- NAU IT cell contact: itcell@nau.in, 7359445544. -- https://nausagar.nau.in/contact
- NAU administration table (Registrar 02637-282823, registrar@nau.in). -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/navsari-agricultural-university-contact-no

PUBLICATIONS
- Jagtap P. et al. (2023). Development of High Oil Yielding Niger Variety for Gujarat State. Journal of Oilseeds Research 40 (Special issue). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State (DOI not found; full author list not confirmed)
- Authors not confirmed (year not stated; ID suggests c. 2025). Screening of Niger Cultivars/Genotypes for Resistance to Leaf Spot Disease Under Natural Conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393367222_Screening_of_Niger_Cultivars_Genotypes_for_Resistance_to_Leaf_Spot_Disease_Under_Natural_Conditions
- Prashant et al. (year not confirmed). Alternaria and Cercospora Leaf Spot Diseases of Niger (Guizotia abyssinica Cass.) – A Traditional Tribal Crop of South Gujarat, India, with Cost Benefit Ratio in Relation to Different Fungicides. NAU, Navsari. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334730502_Alternaria_and_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot_Diseases_of_Niger_Guizotia_abyssinica_Cass_-_A_Traditional_Tribal_Crop_of_South_Gujarat_India_with_Cost_Benefit_Ratio_in_Relation_to_Different_Fungicides
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report specific to GNNIG-4 was found. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or NAU seed-sale listing for GNNIG-4 was found; the combined contact/seed query returned only institutional contact pages. A dedicated seed-availability search was not run, so this is not a full negative. -- No evidence found
- A Down to Earth article notes that formal seed production has been insufficient for niger generally and that government varieties seldom reach farmers. -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/agriculture/illusive-oilseed-india-s-niger-seed-cultivation-is-declining-here-is-why-84380

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat only, kharif rainfed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State

DISCREPANCIES TO RESOLVE
- Release year: input 2022-10-26; the paper says notified in 2021.
- Parentage: input says a selection from a local cultivar; the paper says mass selection from a mutagenised population of RCR-317 (15 kr).
- Seednet name GNNIG-3 refers to a different 2016 release; no Seednet record for GNNIG-4 was found.
