search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO 3 (tomato)

Name note: the release-minutes name is "CO 3" and the Seednet name is "CO. 3". I did not run a Seednet-specific search, so no finding below comes from seednet.gov.in. Most evidence refers to the open-pollinated "CO 3 (Marutham)". Several TNAU pages also list a separate F1 hybrid named "Tomato Hybrid CO 3" (released 2010). I excluded hybrid-only findings. Crop note: the Seednet crop field says "ONION", which conflicts with the tomato record. No onion evidence was found, and the findings below treat the crop as tomato.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to CO 3. Searches returned only general tomato material, and the one TNAU statement about TLCV resistance applies to the hybrid, so I excluded it. Source checked: https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_tomato_varieties.html

DISEASE AND PEST -- Prevention is the only real solution against bacterial wilt, and resistant varieties such as PKM 1 and CO 3 are recommended. (This is a non-official grower guide, so treat it as secondary.) -- https://growsmartfarm.org/crops/tomato-en
Pest/disease resistance for the open-pollinated CO 3 is otherwise not documented. The "resistant to TLCV / moderately resistant to root knot nematodes" statements on the TNAU variety page refer to the hybrid "TNAU Tomato Hybrid CO 3" and were excluded. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_tomato_varieties.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
- CO 3 (Marutham) is described as a determinate type that can be planted as close as 30 cm x 30 cm, with fruits round, four light grooves, capsicum red. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
- Yield reported for CO 3 as 40 t/ha, compared with 30-35 t/ha for PKM 1 and 30 t/ha for Paiyur. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
- Seed production spacing for CO 3 is 60 x 30 cm. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/seed_veg_tomato.html
- Yield and duration figures from the TNAU variety table (96.2 t/ha, 145 days) belong to the hybrid and were excluded. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_tomato_varieties.html

GENETICS AND QTL -- Origin: CO 3 (Marutham) is described as an induced mutant derived from CO 1, which conflicts with the record's parentage of a clonal selection from CS-450. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
Paiyur-1 was bred by crossing Pusa Ruby with CO 3. This confirms CO 3 as a parent but does not describe CO 3 itself. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
No QTL or marker study specific to CO 3 was found. The QTL and marker results returned in the research search concerned other tomato lines and were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No named breeder for CO 3 was found. The releasing body is the Horticultural College and Research Institute, Coimbatore, TNAU. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/hcri-coimbatore/department-of-vegetable-crops-technologies-developed/
The Department of Vegetable Crops (established 1979 within the institute) runs tomato breeding for yield and stress resistance. This is institute-level only and not specific to CO 3. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/hcri-coimbatore/department-of-vegetable-crops-about-department/
TNAU's release table lists CO 3 (Marutham) with a release year of 1980 (also CO1 1969 and CO2 1974). This conflicts with the 2015-04-07 release date in the record. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/hcri-coimbatore/department-of-vegetable-crops-technologies-developed/

CONTACT DETAILS --
- Dr. L. Pugalendhi, Dean (Horticulture), Horticultural College and Research Institute, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore - 641 003, Tamil Nadu, India. E-mail: nextgenhort2021@tnau.ac.in. This is an institute-level contact taken from a 2021 event page, not a CO 3 breeder contact. -- https://sites.google.com/tnau.ac.in/ihc2021/contact
- A third-party listing gives the address as Lawley Road, Coimbatore - 641003, and names the Dean as Dr. S. Mariappan. This conflicts with the event page and is unverified. -- https://www.collegebatch.com/11967-horticultural-college-and-research-institute-in-coimbatore
- TNAU Seed Centre vegetable stock contact: 0422-6611283 / 6611374; vegetables@tnau.ac.in. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Department of Seed Science & Technology, TNAU, Coimbatore-641003: Phone 0422-6611363; Email seed@tnau.ac.in. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/seed_veg_tomato.html

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research-focused search returned only unrelated tomato papers (cadmium GWAS, Ethiopian germplasm, heat-tolerance trials, fruit-mass genetics) and no CO 3 paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record. No KrishiKosh or journal search was run beyond that query.

SEED AVAILABILITY --
- A TNAU seed stock position dated 13.08.2019 lists CO 3 with a quantity of 35.79, unit not shown in the extracted table. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/pdf/seedavailabilityon13.08.2019.pdf
- A TNAU seed production page says CO 3 is among tomato varieties kept on sale at the Horticultural College and Research Station, Coimbatore (contact 0422 6611283). The page is undated. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/seed%20Centre_Seed%20Productions.html
- The 31.07.2021 TNAU stock list shows PKM 1 and hybrid CO 4 but no visible CO 3 entry. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Papaya "Co 3" and bhendi hybrid "Co 3" appear in TNAU price lists, but those are other crops and were excluded. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/input_source/input_source_tnau_seed.html
- Availability is subject to stock at the time of enquiry. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or private dealer listing for CO 3 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The record's recommended-states field is "Not specified". A grower guide says CO 3 is suited for Coimbatore, Salem & Dharmapuri districts. This is a secondary source and is not an official notification. -- https://growsmartfarm.org/crops/tomato-en
No official Central Sub-Committee notification or recommended-state list was found. Seednet was not checked directly.

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest on drought tolerance or related mechanisms.

heat.details: No evidence of heat tolerance was found. The Sharmila Bharathi and Mohan (2018) source contains agronomic notes on planting dates and temperature responses, but no tolerance rating.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest on salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest on flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance is documented. The variety is moderately susceptible to purple blotch (Alternaria porri).

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance is documented. The variety is susceptible to onion thrips (Thrips tabaci).

agronomic_details.yield: Bulb yield of about 18.9 t/ha in about 90 days, reported as about 18.8% above CO 4 (Saraswathi et al., 2017). The WorldVeg record reports 18.91 t/ha, 18.78% above COA. The comparator varieties differ between sources.
agronomic_details.stability: No evidence found in the digest on performance across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Best suited to January planting for economic yield in fertile loamy irrigated soils. A Coimbatore-area study found December planting gave the highest bulb yield.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 90 days seed-to-bulb; bulb-to-seed 95-100 days (per digest). The input table lists maturity as not available.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Free-flowering and seed-setting type. Produces true seed of roughly 250-300 kg/ha. Pink to light-pink bulbs of about 60-90 g per clump. TSS about 13.2 degrees Brix. Storage life reported over 150 days, although a 2020 TNAU release note describes a short shelf life for CO 5.
agronomic_details.field_trials: A 2015 Journal of Plant Sciences trial in Coimbatore found the lowest post-harvest weight loss and storage rot among CO (On) 5, CO-6 and Aca-15. KVK Namakkal ran a staggered seed nursery of CO (On) 5 for 20 farmers and a demonstration showing improved small onion production. The release year of 2015 is not confirmed by the digest sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No evidence found in the digest on QTL, SNP, or SSR markers.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No evidence found in the digest on genes or pathways. The variety was developed via mass pedigree selection in a seed-propagated aggregatum (multiplier) onion, with parental line AC (SP.l) collected from Gnanamedu village, Cuddalore district.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TOPIC: Identity and breeder: Developed by Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) Horticultural College & Research Institute, Coimbatore, as a seed-propagated aggregatum (multiplier) onion via mass pedigree selection; the input's "Indian Agricultural Research Institute" attribution is not supported by these sources -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf

TOPIC: Release and development: The 2006 WorldVeg record describes the variety's development at TNAU, with the parental line AC (SP.l) collected from Gnanamedu village, Cuddalore district. The input's release year of 2015 is not confirmed by these sources -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Yield: Bulb yield of about 18.9 t/ha in about 90 days, roughly 18.8% above CO 4 (CO 4 is the comparison variety in this source) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/T.%20Saraswathi,%20et%20al.pdf ; also 18.91 t/ha, 18.78% above COA, in https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Seed production and reproduction: Free-flowering and seed-setting type, producing true seed of roughly 250-300 kg/ha; seed-to-bulb about 90 days, bulb-to-seed 95-100 days -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/T.%20Saraswathi,%20et%20al.pdf

TOPIC: Bulb traits and quality: Pink to light-pink bulbs, about 60-90 g per clump; TSS about 13.2 degrees Brix; storage life reported over 150 days -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/T.%20Saraswathi,%20et%20al.pdf

TOPIC: Storage and shelf life: A 2015 Journal of Plant Sciences trial found the lowest post-harvest weight loss and storage rot among CO (On) 5, CO-6 and Aca-15 tested in Coimbatore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370968566_Economics_of_Production_and_Marketing_of_Small_Onion_in_Coimbatore_District ; a 2020 TNAU release note says CO 5 has a short shelf life and was superseded by CO 6 for that trait -- https://www.covaipost.com/coimbatore/13-new-crop-varieties-released-as-pongal-gift-to-farmers-by-tnau-coimbatore/

TOPIC: Disease resistance: Moderately susceptible to purple blotch (Alternaria porri) -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Pest resistance: Susceptible to onion thrips (Thrips tabaci) -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Drought tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Heat tolerance: No evidence found (agronomic notes on planting dates and temperature responses exist, but no tolerance rating) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf

TOPIC: Salinity tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Flood tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Submergence tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: QTL/molecular markers: No evidence found

TOPIC: Recommended planting window: Best suited to January planting for economic yield in fertile loamy irrigated soils; a Coimbatore-area study also found December planting gave the highest bulb yield -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf

TOPIC: Recommended states/regions: Tamil Nadu (named as a preferred variety in TNAU crop notes; crop-growing districts include Perambalur, Trichy, Dindigul, Namakkal, Coimbatore, Erode, Tirunelveli) -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_small%20onion.html

TOPIC: Seed availability (NSC/State Seed Corporations): No evidence found

TOPIC: Seed availability (KVKs and farmer level): KVK Namakkal ran a staggered seed nursery of CO (On) 5 for 20 farmers to supply seed for the next crop and reduce delayed-sowing losses, and a KVK Namakkal demonstration showed improved small onion production using CO 5 seed -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/success_stories/pdf/horti/2014/h_ss12_2014.pdf

TOPIC: Farmer adoption: A study of adoption among farmers in Perambalur district, Tamil Nadu -- https://ageconsearch.umn.edu/record/367061/

disease_resistance.summary: Purple blotch: low disease index relative to the checks GWO-1 and PWF-131 (relative field observation). No formal disease resistance rating was found, so this is not a confirmed resistance classification. Source: release page for Gujarat Anand White Onion 2.

pest_resistance.summary: Thrips: fewer thrips than the checks GWO-1 and PWF-131 (relative field observation). No formal pest resistance rating was found. Source: release page for Gujarat Anand White Onion 2.

agronomic_details.yield: Average bulb yield of 595 q/ha as reported on the release page (name used: Gujarat Anand White Onion 2). The CSC record lists the average_yield unit as Kg/Ha, so the unit should be reconciled before use.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Middle Gujarat, Rabi season, irrigated conditions (release page). The digest treats this as a production condition, not a stress-tolerance finding.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: More long leaves than both checks. Lower percentage of bolting and jointed bulbs than both checks. White skin, globe shape and large bulb size. Higher TSS, pyruvic acid, reducing and non-reducing sugars, and total carbohydrates than the checks (release page, name used: Gujarat Anand White Onion 2).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Release-page comparison with checks: bulb yield 25% higher than GWO-1 and 45% higher than PWF-131 (average 595 q/ha). Thrips and purple blotch were lower than the checks. Bolting and jointed-bulb percentages were lower than the checks. Quality traits (TSS, pyruvic acid, sugars, total carbohydrates) were higher than the checks. (2) Agronomy trial using the name GAWO 2: three consecutive seasons at the College of Horticulture Farm, Anand Agricultural University, testing organic and consortium nutrient treatments (CC + NPK consortium referenced), transplanting in December and harvest in April. This was not a varietal comparison and no yield results were given in the digest. The year of the extended summary could not be verified from the retrieved text.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The searches returned no page on these traits for this variety. -- none

DISEASE AND PEST
- Compared with the checks GWO-1 and PWF-131, the variety had a low purple blotch disease index and fewer thrips (name used: "Gujarat Anand White Onion 2"). -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-white-onion-2

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

- Bulbs have white skin, a globe shape and a large size (name used: "Gujarat Anand White Onion 2"). -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-white-onion-2
- A field experiment on GAWO 2 ran for three consecutive seasons at the College of Horticulture Farm, Anand Agricultural University. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for the variety under both names (Hisar Onion 4 / Hisar Onion 4 on Seednet) returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance records for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Stored-seed study: Hisar Onion-4 (spelled "Hisar Onion-4" in the source) was compared with Hisar Onion-3 and Hisar-2 under natural and artificial ageing, and it kept better seed viability and germination than the other two -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agriculture9080163
Seed-storage highlight: the same study reports the highest germination (65.92%) for Hisar Onion-4 after ageing -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agriculture9080163
Yield listing: a DOGR release table gives Hissar Onion-4 as rose red, rabi season, released 2016, with an average yield of 32.5 t/ha (the table row is misaligned in the PDF text, so this value should be checked against the original) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404114256_Hybrid_Breeding_in_Onion_Innovations_Challenges_and_Future_Prospects_th
Release-year discrepancy: the DOGR table says 2016, while the input record gives 2015-04-07 (CSC release minutes). Both should be verified against the official notification.
Maturity, bulb size and field-trial data for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searches returned no marker, QTL, parentage-confirmation or genetic-study results for Hisar Onion-4. The input parentage ("a selection from local material collected from Bahadurgarh area") was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Hissar Onion-4 is listed under HAU, Hissar (CCS Haryana Agricultural University) in a DOGR release table -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/370/316
Table listing: Hissar Onion-4 appears as rose red, rabi, 2016 in a varieties table -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/370/316
Breeder names: No evidence found for this variety. A 2008 Haryana approval article names a breeding team, but it concerns Hisar Onion-3 (not Onion-4), so it was excluded.
Station: No evidence found for the specific breeding station or division.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for this variety was returned. The institution's name (CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar) is confirmed only as the developing institution; no official contact URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved record (Year not shown; volume 9 suggests 2019, inferred). Assessment of Natural Ageing Related Physio-Biochemical Changes in Onion Seed. Agriculture (MDPI) -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agriculture9080163
Mahajan et al. (2023). Onion: Breeding and Genomics. Indian Journal of Vegetable Science (Indian Society of Vegetable Science) -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/370/316

No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report or conference paper specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale or dealer listing names Hisar Onion 4. A Hisar dealer listing for red onion seed (Super Seeds Private Limited) does not name this variety, so it was excluded -- https://www.exportersindia.com/haryana/onion-seed.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
Haryana -- input record only (CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar). No retrieved source independently confirms the state recommendation or a notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MDU.6 (rice) / MDU-1 (Seednet)

Name note: The evidence below refers to "Rice MDU 6" (variety_name MDU.6, crop rice). No evidence links Seednet's "MDU-1" under ONION to this variety. The only "MDU 1" matches found are a blackgram and a cluster bean variety, so the Seednet record looks mismatched.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to leaffolder, stem borer, green leafhopper and whitebacked planthopper under field conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322734415_Rice_MDU_6_A_high_yielding_long_slender_grain_variety
- Same resistance profile listed in the TNAU varieties page -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/MDU6.html
- Heat stress: a TNAU-linked invertase assay noted that MDU6 was the one genotype that did not show a rise in invertase activity after heat stress, which is an indirect physiological observation, not a field tolerance rating -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322734415_Rice_MDU_6_A_high_yielding_long_slender_grain_variety
- Drought, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for MDU 6 in the searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to the insect pests above is the only pest/disease rating found; no disease ratings (blast, bacterial leaf blight, sheath blight, tungro) were found -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/MDU6.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 110-115 days, semi-dwarf (95-105 cm), high tillering, white long slender grain -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322734415_Rice_MDU_6_A_high_yielding_long_slender_grain_variety
- Mean grain yield 6118 kg/ha, 9.7% above ADT 43 and 10.2% above ADT (R) 45 across yield trials, MLTs and ARTs; over 7000 kg/ha at 29 of 160 ART locations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322734415_Rice_MDU_6_A_high_yielding_long_slender_grain_variety
- Season listing: Sornavari, Kar, Kuruvai and Navarai; parentage MDU 5 / ACM 96136 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/MDU6.html
- Crop management tables list MDU 6 for Kar, Navarai and semi-dry seasons across several zones -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/01_Rice.pdf
- 2022 Rice Scientists Meet proceedings propose that promising cultures be identified to replace MDU 5 and MDU 6 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2022/12/1.-41st-CSM-on-Rice-Proceedings-2022.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage per the journal paper is ACM 01010, a derivative of MDU5 / ACM 96136 -- https://doaj.org/article/108adb860fc746849286ee9b1676fe9a
- Parentage "developed by selection from Sompatti local" (input record): No evidence found in the searches; the published pedigree differs.
- QTL or marker studies for MDU 6: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Agricultural College and Research Institute, Madurai, TNAU, as ACM 01010, released as Rice MDU 6 -- https://doaj.org/article/108adb860fc746849286ee9b1676fe9a
- Institution in the input record (NPRC Vamban) does not match the published developer; NPRC is a pulses centre -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/trri/nprc
- Listed author of the release paper: N. Aananthi (with R.P. Gnanamalar, S. Jebaraj, S.M. Ibrahim, C. Vanniarajan, C.R. Anandakumar) -- https://doaj.org/article/108adb860fc746849286ee9b1676fe9a

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest for drought tolerance in NHRDF Red-4. No mechanisms or trial data were reported.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest for heat tolerance in NHRDF Red-4. No mechanisms or trial data were reported.

salinity.details: A 36-accession Indian short-day onion screening study classed NHRDF Red-4 (L-744) among the salt-tolerant group. Tolerant accessions in the study showed higher relative water content, membrane stability, proline and antioxidant enzyme activity under salt stress. The level is medium because the evidence is a laboratory/screening classification only; no field-level salinity data specific to this variety was found.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance in NHRDF Red-4.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance evidence found for NHRDF Red-4. A Stemphylium blight tolerance statement appears on the NHRDF onion page, but it belongs to a different variety entry (yield 380-400 q/ha, notified for Zone-II and Zone-V) and was not attributed to Red-4. No other diseases were reported.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence found for NHRDF Red-4.

agronomic_details.yield: Sources conflict. Input data gives 22000-25000 kg/ha (approximately 220-250 q/ha). NHRDF extension material gives 350-400 q/ha. The digest does not resolve this discrepancy.
agronomic_details.stability: No cross-environment stability analysis reported beyond the multilocational trial summary, which describes the variety as best-yielding in its trials.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Zone-III (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Manipur/Imphal per the release notice).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: OUTER SCALE THICK AND INNER 2-3 SCALES OF RED COLOUR, MODERATE PUNJGENT, GOOD STORER. Extension material also describes good keeping quality and TSS of 12-14%, while input data gives TSS 13-14% and dry matter 14-15%. Bulbs are dark red, 5-6 cm diameter, size index 18-20 cm square. Extension material gives maturity of 110-120 days after transplanting, which conflicts with the 180-210 day input value and may reflect a different measurement basis.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tested at 5-6 multilocational trial sites with other entries and controls over 2011-12 to 2013-14. Authors report the average yield as the best and superior to all compared varieties. Site-level yield figures were not included in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TOPIC: Identity and release -- The 38th NHRDF annual report (2015-16) says the Central Sub-Committee released one onion variety that year, NHRDF-Red-4 (L-744), for Zone-III (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Imphal). -- https://nhrdf.org/pdf/NHRDF%20Annual%20Report%202015-16.pdf
TOPIC: Breeder/institution -- NHRDF (Nashik, Maharashtra) is the developing institution. Authors R. K. Singh and P. K. Gupta published the variety description in Indian Horticulture (vol. 62, no. 4, 2017; published 2019). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/87634
TOPIC: Recommended states / zone -- The release notice places the variety in Zone-III, which covers Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Imphal. Your input field lists Varanasi, Kanpur, Samastipur, Kalyani and Imphal. These are mostly cities and a research centre, not states, so the field needs correcting; Varanasi, Kanpur, Samastipur and Kalyani fall within the Zone-III states listed above. -- https://nhrdf.org/pdf/NHRDF%20Annual%20Report%202015-16.pdf
TOPIC: Yield and trials -- The variety was tested at 5-6 multilocational trial sites with other entries and controls over 2011-12 to 2013-14. The authors report its average yield as the best and superior to all compared varieties. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/87634
TOPIC: Yield (agronomic profile) -- NHRDF's extension material gives an average yield of 350-400 q/ha and maturity of 110-120 days after transplanting. It also describes good keeping quality and TSS of 12-14%. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/onion-varieties-for-different-seasons/ ; http://www.nhrdf.com/Onion.html
TOPIC: Salinity tolerance -- A 36-accession Indian short-day onion study classed NHRDF Red-4 (L-744) among the salt-tolerant group. Tolerant accessions showed higher relative water content, membrane stability, proline and antioxidant enzyme activity under salt stress. This is a screening study, and no field-level salinity data specific to this variety was found. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9739851/
TOPIC: Drought tolerance -- No evidence found
TOPIC: Heat tolerance -- No evidence found
TOPIC: Flood tolerance -- No evidence found
TOPIC: Submergence tolerance -- No evidence found
TOPIC: Disease resistance -- No evidence found for NHRDF Red-4. A Stemphylium blight tolerance statement appears on the NHRDF onion page, but it sits in the entry for a different variety (yield 380-400 q/ha, notified for Zone-II and Zone-V), so I did not attribute it to Red-4. -- http://www.nhrdf.com/Onion.html
TOPIC: Pest resistance -- No evidence found
TOPIC: QTL/markers -- No evidence found
TOPIC: Seed availability -- NHRDF states it produces and distributes quality seed of its onion varieties, including this one, nationwide. No NSC, State Seed Corporation or KVK stockist data was found for Red-4. -- http://www.nhrdf.org/pVarieties_o.php
TOPIC: Notification/release detail -- NHRDF's annual report says the variety was released by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties of Horticultural Crops, under the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The exact notification date was not confirmed; the input's 2015-04-07 date is not verified. -- https://nhrdf.org/pdf/NHRDF%20Annual%20Report%202015-16.pdf

disease_resistance.summary: Stemphylium blight: incidence recorded at 6.20% in NHRDF Red-2 in NHRDF's 2015-16 onion advance-line disease resistance evaluation (AVT-I). The report does not state whether this is low or high relative to other entries, so no resistance level is assigned. Purple blotch: no variety-specific evidence found in the sources searched.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence on resistance to thrips or other pests specific to NHRDF Red-2 was found across the four queries run.

agronomic_details.yield: Release record (CSC, treated as ground truth): 22000.00 to 25000.00 kg/ha (220-250 q/ha) under normal conditions. Secondary sources in the digest report 350-375 q/ha (global-agriculture.com and nhrdf.org). These figures conflict and have not been reconciled; the CSC value is retained as the reference figure.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location stability (rabi 2023-24, five locations): NHRDF Red-2 showed minimal genotype-by-environment interaction among red genotypes, together with Bhima Kiran and three experimental lines. This comes from a secondary report; the primary paper was not located.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Release record (CSC) recommends release and cultivation in Punjab, Tarai region of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra during the rabi season. The digest's rabi cultivation zones are Zone III (Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Gujarat) and Zone VI (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh). The two state lists differ and are not reconciled in the digest. Fertilizer and trial work has been conducted at Nashik and Karnal.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: OUTER SCALE THICK AND INNER 2-3 SCALES OF RED COLOUR, MODERATE PUNJGENT, GOOD STORER.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Fertilizer trial, rabi 2013-14: 50% recommended NPK plus 50% vermicompost gave the highest yield in cv. NHRDF Red 2; 100% vermicompost gave the best quality (TSS, sugars, lowest pyruvic acid). (2) NHRDF 2015-16 trials at Nashik and Karnal: a combined NPK plus humic acid foliar schedule gave the highest gross and marketable yield and benefit-cost ratio in NHRDF-Red-2 and NHRDF Red; the report recommends it for Nashik and Karnal. (3) NHRDF 2015-16 AVT-I disease evaluation: Stemphylium blight incidence 6.20%. (4) Multi-location stability trial, rabi 2023-24, five locations: minimal genotype-by-environment interaction (secondary report).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NHRDF RED 2 onion evidence digest

Name note: The CSC minutes name is "NHRDF RED 2" (L-355). The Seednet name is "NHRDF RED". Sources usually call this variety "NHRDF-Red-2" or "NHRDF Red-2". Plain "NHRDF Red" or "NHRDF Red (L-28)" is a separate, older variety, so evidence for it is excluded below unless it names Red-2 or L-355.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for NHRDF Red-2 in the sources searched. -- https://nhrdf.org/Onion.php (searched; no stress data)

DISEASE AND PEST
Stemphylium blight incidence was recorded at 6.20% in NHRDF Red-2 in NHRDF's 2015-16 onion advance-line disease resistance evaluation (AVT-I). The report does not state whether this is low or high relative to other entries. -- https://nhrdf.org/pdf/NHRDF%20Annual%20Report%202015-16.pdf
No evidence found on resistance to purple blotch, thrips or other pests specific to NHRDF Red-2. -- searched across the four queries; no variety-specific record found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Bulbs are attractive red, globular, thin-necked, 5.0-6.0 cm in diameter, with good keeping quality; matures 100-120 days after transplanting; average yield 350-375 q/ha. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/big-onion-variety-nhrdf-red-2/ and https://nhrdf.org/Onion.php
TSS 13-14%, dry matter 14-15%, pyruvic acid about 12.0 micromole/g. -- https://nhrdf.org/Onion.php
Notified for rabi cultivation, Zone III and Zone VI, under notification SO-2363(E) dated 01/10/2012. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/onion-varieties-for-different-seasons/
Fertilizer trial (rabi 2013-14): 50% recommended NPK plus 50% vermicompost gave the highest yield in cv. NHRDF Red 2; 100% vermicompost gave the best quality (TSS, sugars, lowest pyruvic acid). -- https://www.worldwidejournals.com/indian-journal-of-applied-research-(IJAR)/article/evaluation-of-the-performance-of-onion-cv-nhrdf-red-2-in-response-to-inorganic-organic-and-bio-fertilizers/NTEyMA==/?is=1&b1=229&k=58
NHRDF 2015-16 trials at Nashik and Karnal: a combined NPK plus humic acid foliar schedule gave the highest gross and marketable yield and benefit-cost ratio in NHRDF-Red-2 and NHRDF Red; the report recommends it for Nashik and Karnal. -- https://nhrdf.org/pdf/NHRDF%20Annual%20Report%202015-16.pdf
Multi-location stability (rabi 2023-24, five locations): NHRDF Red-2 showed minimal genotype-by-environment interaction among red genotypes, with Bhima Kiran and three experimental lines. -- https://bioengineer.org/onion-breeding-breakthrough-scientists-pinpoint-stable-high-yield-genotypes-across-india/ (secondary report; primary paper not located)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genetic-diversity study specific to NHRDF Red-2 was found. -- searched in query 3; no hits

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: National Horticultural Research and Development Foundation (NHRDF), Nashik, Maharashtra. NHRDF was set up in 1977 by NAFED and associate onion shippers; its head office moved to Nashik in 1989; registered office in New Delhi. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nhrdf-red-1849039873.html
NHRDF has five Regional Research Stations, laboratories and 20 extension centres. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nhrdf-red-1849039873.html
Parentage field in the release record says the material was collected from Patiala, Punjab and developed at RRS Karnal. No independent source confirmed the Karnal origin. Karnal RRS does appear as an NHRDF trial site. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12586005/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found in the sources searched.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone or personal contact found for NHRDF Red-2. Official NHRDF email and phone: not found in the sources; verify on the NHRDF site before use.

PUBLICATIONS

disease_resistance.summary: Stemphylium blight: ranked well in a Nashik trial (two seasons, rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24), with 10.93% disease intensity, the lowest among compared entries in that study. This indicates tolerance in a trial context only, not a formal resistance rating. Purple blotch: no variety-specific evidence; NHRDF reports state that no tested onion line was fully free of purple blotch. Other diseases: not specified in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Thrips: no evidence found specific to this variety. The cited source reports thrips tolerance for other NHRDF varieties only. Other pests: not specified in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record (ground truth): 22000.00 to 25000.00 Kg/Ha (220-250 q/ha under normal conditions). Digest reports an average yield of 350-400 q/ha (Krishi Jagran and NHRDF Onion page). The two sources conflict; the CSC value is used as the reference. Digest also reports a Stemphylium trial with gross yield 397.00 q/ha and marketable yield 383.83 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Multilocation trials at 5-6 locations (2011-12 to 2013-14) reported the best average yield across entries. Marketable yield was statistically at par with Arka Lalima and NHRDF-Red-2 in an exotic-hybrid comparison. Two-season Nashik trial (rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24) recorded the highest gross and marketable yields among compared entries. Stability index across environments not reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for release and cultivation in Punjab, Tarai region of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra during the rabi season. Digest release notice lists zone III (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Imphal) for rabi. An older NHRDF page also lists kharif in Cuddapah (Andhra Pradesh) and all three seasons in Karnataka, but the digest states it is unclear whether this refers to the same entry. The CSC list is used as the reference.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: OUTER SCALE THICK AND INNER 2-3 SCALES OF RED COLOUR, MODERATE PUNJGENT, GOOD STORER.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Multilocation trials at 5-6 locations (2011-12 to 2013-14). Exotic-hybrid comparison (NHRDF Annual Report 2015-16). Two-season Stemphylium blight trial at Nashik (rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24). Maturity conflict: digest reports 110-120 days after transplanting, while the CSC record gives 180-210 days; the CSC value is retained above. Digest bulb data: dark red, globular, thin neck, 5.5-6.25 cm diameter, TSS 12-14%, dry matter 13-14%, pyruvic acid about 13 micromol/g. CSC bulb data: 5-6 cm diameter, size index 18-20 cm square, TSS 13-14%, dry matter 14-15%. Keeping quality described as good in both sources.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No search result reports drought tolerance for POH-1. The 'drought' and 'water stress' snippets come from unrelated contexts (cassava, kapok, trehalose and cytokinin trials, and a general onion biochemistry paper).

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The 'heat stress' snippets are generic (a tuberisation statement apparently about potato, a breeding chapter heading, and chemistry texts). None is specific to POH-1.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: The PAU package of practices says only that alkaline, high-salt soils are unsuitable for vegetables in general. There is no POH-1-specific salinity data.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: None documented for POH-1. The ApR1 snippet refers to resistance gene work in onion generally, not to this variety.
disease_resistance.technical_details: No POH-1-specific disease reaction data in the results.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (not demonstrated; evidence absent rather than negative)
key_stress_attributes: A PAU 2025 snippet (result 46) begins a POH-1 description ('Large, round and light red in colour. Tolerance to ...'), but the text is truncated and the tolerance is not stated, so it cannot be used as evidence.

genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Hybrid (F1). PAU states that hybrid seed must be replaced every season. A Springer chapter on accelerated breeding mentions POH-1 developed 'in a time span of 7 years', which suggests a conventional hybrid program, but the snippet is only partial.

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: Kg/Ha (no numeric value in the input). The Springer chapter says POH-1 'gives comparable yield', with no figure given.

agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: A Punjab agroforestry proceedings snippet compared POH-1, PYO-1, PWO-2, PRO-6, PRO-7 and Pb Naroya. PRO-7 transplanted in mid-December gave the highest bulb yield (27.59 t/ha), so POH-1 did not top that trial. No POH-1 yield figure was extracted. The AICRP 2021 report lists POH-1 among six onion varieties.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: No farmer feedback found. PAU recommended POH-1 for Punjab (news dated Jan 2020), and NHRDF is mentioned as a partner for POH-1 and PRO-7.

breeder_and_development_info.development_timeline: Recommended by PAU by Jan 2020. The Springer chapter mentions a 7-year development span. The input record gives a 2022 release year, which conflicts with the 2020 news.
breeder_and_development_info.research_publications: Pyruvic acid and phenol content study (ResearchGate), in which POH-1 had the lowest total phenol content (0.70 mg/g fw). Springer 'Accelerated Plant Breeding Vol. 2'. PAU annual report 2020. AICRP annual report 2021.

However, none of the sources shows POH-1-specific stress tolerance, a yield figure, or any evidence for Gujarat. Most search hits are irrelevant noise (chemistry, dictionaries, and so on). The 60-point tier requires at least one citation, but the citations are weak and carry no stress or yield content. A score of 50 would suit a variety with some climate trait, which POH-1 lacks, so a score of 40-50 is defensible. 50 is given because documentation of the variety is real, but it should be treated as provisional.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No source reports drought tolerance for PRO-7. A hydrogel/FYM study on rabi onion PRO-7 tested soil moisture retention under management, which does not show varietal tolerance. The PAU annual report's drought mention concerns Aegilops-derived wheat synthetics, not onion.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: The PAU package of practices says only that alkaline, high-salt soils are unsuitable for onion in general. This is not a varietal trait of PRO-7. The hydrogel paper's reference to salt and drought tolerance concerns polymers.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The IAUA newsletter's flood-tolerant item is a rice variety.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The submergence snippet in the ResearchGate conference document refers to a different context (probably rice). It also lists PRO-7 yield in a trial, which is not a submergence result.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are credible citations: a peer-reviewed agronomy paper, PAU documents and a release notice. But no source shows stress, disease or pest tolerance for PRO-7. The hydrogel paper concerns moisture management, not varietal tolerance. The yield figure is unverified, and no Gujarat evaluation exists. Roughly 40 of the 50 search results were irrelevant (recipes, manuals and similar). Under the rubric, a citation with weak stress traits falls in the 60 band, while 'only yield info, no stress' falls at 40, so 50 is a compromise leaning toward the lower side. Early maturity is the only climate-relevant trait.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Punjab Tej (CSC name) / PUNJAB WHITE (Seednet name), chilli, code H0102004

Search note: four searches were run. The Seednet-name search for PUNJAB WHITE returned only onion seed retailers, so it has no bearing on this record. The Seednet crop field says ONION, while this variety is a chilli, so that portal entry may be mis-keyed and should be checked. The evidence below refers to Punjab Tej (chilli).

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in Punjab Tej. The searches returned no such data. -- searches: "Punjab Tej chilli variety", "Punjab Tej chilli research paper"

DISEASE AND PEST:
Punjab Tej is described as moderately resistant to leaf curl virus, dieback and root-knot nematode, and as tolerant to aphids, thrips and yellow mites. -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
Punjab Tej is an early-maturing variety whose first picking of red fruit comes about 75 days after transplanting. -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf
Fruits are about 6.80 cm long and thin-skinned, turn light green when immature and deep red when mature. Fruit is highly pungent (1.32% capsaicin) and suits processing and powder making. Vitamin C is reported at 115 mg/100 g. -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf
The PAU sheet gives a red-ripe yield potential of 56 q/acre. -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf
The 2013 PAU paper reports a mean total yield of about 139.7 q/ha for Punjab Tej across local research trials in 2008-09 to 2011-12, and a mean fruit weight of 4.79 g. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
The same paper reports 169 q/ha in multilocation trials, and 140 q/ha in one trial, about 124% above the check Punjab Surkh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli

GENETICS AND QTL:
No evidence found. No parentage, QTL or marker study for Punjab Tej was returned. The parentage field is "Not specified" and remains unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
Punjab Tej was developed by the Department of Vegetable Science, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
The named authors of the 2013 paper are Major S. Dhaliwal, Salesh Kumar Jindal and D. S. Cheema, all PAU. These are publication authors and are not confirmed as the lead breeders. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
The chilli hybrid chapter (CH-27) also covers PAU chilli work but concerns a different variety, so it is not used here. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432487_Advances_in_Horticulture_Chapter_9_Chilli_Production_Challenges_and_Modern_Breeding_Approaches

CONTACT DETAILS:
No breeder email, phone or postal address for Punjab Tej was found. The only institutional detail is the PAU Department of Vegetable Science, Ludhiana. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
A PAU faculty directory PDF appeared in results but its contents were not extracted, so no contact is recorded from it. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/pau_faculty_directory.pdf
Institute site: https://pau.edu (from search results; no phone or email extracted).

PUBLICATIONS:
Dhaliwal, M. S., Jindal, S. K., Cheema, D. S. (2013). Punjab Sindhuri and Punjab Tej: New varieties of chilli. Journal of Research Punjab Agricultural University 50(1&2): 79-81. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
PAU chilli variety sheet (undated, covers Punjab Tej). -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY:
No evidence found for Punjab Tej seed from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, KVK, PAU seed sales or private dealers. The PUNJAB WHITE search returned only onion seed sellers (Amazon.in, exportersindia, bombayseeds and others), which are unrelated and discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
Punjab Tej is recommended for cultivation in Punjab. -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
Record discrepancy: the 2013 paper already describes PAU's recommendation, but the CSC release year on this record is 2015-04-07. Verify the release date against the CSC minutes.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is real and documented in PAU institutional sources and a few trial listings, but no stress or climate-resilience trait is evidenced for it. The attributable information is agronomic only: bulb traits and about 141 days to maturity. Many search hits are irrelevant (the PYO chemistry hits, word dictionaries, Facebook). There is no Gujarat-specific data and no yield figure. By the rubric, 'at least one citation but weak on stress traits' gives 60, but the citations are institutional lists rather than research, so a conservative 50 is assigned. Gujarat suitability is unverified, since the variety is bred for Punjab's rabi conditions.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: PYO-1 is a PAU-developed yellow-bulbed onion with large globular bulbs, recommended for rabi cultivation in Punjab, and tested in poplar agroforestry trials. No variety-specific evidence exists for drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest tolerance, and no genetic or breeder details or yield figures were found. Evidence quality is low, and suitability for Gujarat is unverified.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: PYO-1 is a yellow, large, globular, tight-necked onion with medium-tall upright foliage, grown as transplanted rabi onion in Punjab. Maturity is about 141 days (unconfirmed) and no yield figure is available.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No documented stress tolerance or disease/pest resistance specific to PYO-1. Apparent resistance snippets belong to other crops. The stress profile is unknown, so the variety is not classed as stress tolerant.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
27P27 / 27P22 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: the four searches returned no page that names 27P27 (the CSC release-minute name) with rice. The only page that names 27P22 (the Seednet name) is a 2025 Punjab hybrid-seed news item. That page is the only evidence in this digest for either name, and I have not confirmed that 27P22 and 27P27 refer to the same entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for 27P27 and 27P22 returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for either name. Hits for other Pioneer/PHI varieties (27P39, 27P37) were excluded. -- https://shramikkrishikendra.com/product/pioneer-27p39-paddy-seed/ (excluded, different variety)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page links disease or pest resistance to 27P27 or 27P22. Pages on 27P39 and 27P37 were excluded. -- https://shramikkrishikendra.com/product/pioneer-27p37-paddy-seed/ (excluded, different variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or trial data name 27P27 or 27P22. A Punjab article lists general hybrid yield and duration figures but does not tie them to 27P22, so they are not reported here. -- https://www.insightsonindia.com/2025/04/12/hybrid-paddy-seeds/ (generic, not attributed)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The parentage given in the brief (R834F/RA320) did not appear in any search result. No marker or QTL study was found. -- no URL

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No page names a breeder or scientist for 27P27 or 27P22. -- no URL

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, email, phone, address, or institute contact page was found naming this variety. One search result listed PHI Seeds Pvt. Ltd. at a Hyderabad address, but that page covers other varieties (27P11, 27P61, 25P25, 37P22), so I did not attribute it to this variety. -- https://www.asiafarming.com/high-yield-hybrid-paddy-rice-varieties-in-india-for-rabi-and-kharif-seasons (excluded, other varieties)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The research search returned no paper, AICRP or ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or trial report on 27P27 or 27P22. Results were about other rice cultivars or unrelated topics. -- no URL

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for 27P27 or 27P22 was found. Dealer pages for 27P31, 27P37, and 27P39 were excluded as other varieties. -- https://shramikkrishikendra.com/product/pioneer-27p37-paddy-seed/ (excluded, different variety)

RECOMMENDED STATES
27P22 (Seednet name, paddy/hybrid): listed as a common hybrid in Punjab in a 2025 news article on a Punjab hybrid-seed sale ban. This does not match the release-minute states (Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra), and the page is a news item, not an official source. -- https://www.insightsonindia.com/2025/04/12/hybrid-paddy-seeds/
27P27 (CSC release-minute name): No evidence found.

drought.details: Exhibits drought stress tolerance and is suitable for short duration drought conditions, including direct sown rainfed systems. It is recognized as a drought tolerant variety.

heat.details: Considered heat tolerant in nature, suitable for yield enhancement under heat stress. It exhibits terminal heat tolerance when stress is imposed at the panicle initiation stage.

salinity.details: Exhibits tolerance to salinity and is suitable for salt affected rice growing areas of Gujarat. It is listed among salt tolerant rice varieties.

flood.details: Shows tolerance to water logging conditions and is recommended for lowland deep clay soil.

disease_resistance.summary: In some studies, 27P31 has shown high incidence and severity of sheath blight.

pest_resistance.summary: Unknown

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields range from 5.876 t/ha to 9.0 t/ha. A maximum yield of 8.912 t/ha was recorded under drip irrigation, representing a 25.2% increase over flood irrigated control in a study.
agronomic_details.stability: Unknown
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated and transplanted conditions. It is also suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, semi-deep water, and lowland deep clay soil. It can be cultivated using direct seeding, line planting, or System of Rice Intensification (SRI) methods. Demonstrated performance in aerobic rice cultivation with drip irrigation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Classified as semi-dwarf, with a reported height of 82 cm. However, some studies have also recorded higher plant heights, reaching 137.2 cm and 133 cm. Grains are LS (Long Slender).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensively evaluated in Production Oriented Surveys (e.g., 2019, 2022, 2023) and included in ICAR-IIRR Annual Reports. It has been part of programs like 'Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India' (BGREI) and demonstrated strong performance in aerobic rice cultivation trials using drip irrigation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for 28P09 returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data naming 28P09.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
28P09 was tested for three years in the AICRIP hybrid rice trials (IHRT-MS, 2013-15), and the report calls it promising and yield-superior to the varietal check BPT 5204 in the final year -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf
Zone-wise summary yields for 28P09 in the same report: overall 5834, Zone III 5968, Zone V 6987, Zone VI 5010, Zone VII 5818 (units not labelled in the retrieved text; likely kg/ha) -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf
The report lists 28P09 as an MS-type entry, with a value of 106 in the same row whose column label is not in the retrieved text (possibly days to maturity; unconfirmed) -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf
A kharif 2017 field trial at Port Blair, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, reported 28P09 as a hybrid with the highest grain yield of 3.91 t/ha, about 0.81 t/ha (14-26%) above the local check CARI Dhan-6 (3.10 t/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334450197_Rice_Hybrids_and_High_Yielding_Varieties_for_Augmenting_Public_Distribution_System_Demand_in_Andaman_and_Nicobar_Islands_India
The same Port Blair trial recorded significantly more panicles per square metre (287) and grains per panicle (137) for 28P09, with test weight among the lower values -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334450197_Rice_Hybrids_and_High_Yielding_Varieties_for_Augmenting_Public_Distribution_System_Demand_in_Andaman_and_Nicobar_Islands_India

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker or parentage study for 28P09 was returned. Parentage is "Not specified" in the input and no source supplied it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The AICRIP report lists the entry source for 28P09 as "Pioneer Overseas, Hyderabad" -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf
No individual breeder or scientist name for 28P09 was found. The PHI Seeds name in the input is not confirmed by any page that names 28P09; the PHI Seeds pages returned concern other varieties (27P37, 27P39, 27P11, 27P61, 25P25, 37P22) and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for 28P09 was returned. The only institution named is "Pioneer Overseas, Hyderabad" in the AICRIP report, with no address or contact details given in the retrieved text -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Rice Hybrids and High Yielding Varieties for Augmenting Public Distribution System Demand in Andaman and Nicobar Islands, India. Journal not confirmed in retrieved text; year not confirmed (probably 2019 from the ResearchGate ID) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334450197_Rice_Hybrids_and_High_Yielding_Varieties_for_Augmenting_Public_Distribution_System_Demand_in_Andaman_and_Nicobar_Islands_India
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2015). AICRIP Hybrid Rice Kharif 2015 Report (IHRT-MS trials, Table 10, 28P09). ICAR-IIRR/AICRIP report -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf
No KrishiKosh thesis, Indian journal paper or DOI for 28P09 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed searches returned only other products: a Pioneer 27P37 listing and a Pioneer 27P39 listing (shramikkrishikendra.com), and a RARS Pattambi paddy seed notice (kau.in). None names 28P09. Seednet or NSC/state corporation listings were not returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES

The states listed in the input (Odisha, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh) were not confirmed by any retrieved source. The AICRIP report describes the zones tested, but its zone-to-state mapping is not in the retrieved text.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: 28P67 (rice)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "28P67", so every search and finding below refers to the same name. Seednet's crop label is "PADDY (DHAN)". The searches used four queries, the maximum allowed. Each heading notes where evidence was thin.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in the four searches. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-28p67/ (release notice only)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance in the four searches.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released notice lists 28P67 as an open-pollinated variety for sale in Punjab and Haryana, which conflicts with the hybrid parentage in the record (see Notes). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-28p67/
- Maturity given by a seed retailer as about 125 to 130 days. -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/MlhtoJglp55aOqV7cKdq
- Yield potential of 6.7 t/ha cited for 28P67 in an ICAR-IIRR 56th ARGM draft proceedings, where it was used as an observational hybrid check in IHRT trials. -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- Observational hybrid check trial report (AICRIP hybrid rice 2021): 28P67 and Bio-799 showed no significant yield superiority over the national check. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf
- BCKV field study (West Bengal, summer rice 2015-16 and 2016-17, New Alluvial Zone): 28P67 gave the highest grain yield among the tested hybrids, 7.13 t/ha, with harvest index 49.65%. -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Kajal-Sengupta-2144481990

GENETICS AND QTL
- Grain quality and genetic parameter study clusters 28P67 with 27P31 as the two Indica hybrids, separate from Japonica and other genotypes. No QTL or marker data found. -- https://www.pjoes.com/Quantitative-Characteristics-of-Rice-Grain-Quality-nTraits-and-Genetic-Parameters,208587,0,2.html
- Parentage in the record: hybrid RA401F / RA406 (from the variety record, not independently verified by search).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution in the record: Corteva Agriscience Seeds Private Limited (formerly PHI Seeds Private Limited). Seed is sold under the Pioneer brand. -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/MlhtoJglp55aOqV7cKdq
- Release notice was issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare on 25 September 2023, after consultation with the Central Seed Committee. Signatory named: Pankaj Yadav, Joint Secretary. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-28p67/
- No lead breeder name or station found in the four searches.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No official Corteva India email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL found in the searches. Recommend checking the Corteva India corporate contact page directly, or seednet.gov.in for the company's registered address.

PUBLICATIONS
- Sengupta, K. et al. (year not stated in snippet). Hybrid rice performance study, BCKV New Alluvial Zone, West Bengal, 2015-17 (includes 28P67). -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Kajal-Sengupta-2144481990 (full title, co-authors and journal not confirmed)
- Authors not identified (year not stated). Quantitative characteristics of rice grain quality traits and genetic parameters (includes 28P67 and 27P31). PJOES. -- https://www.pjoes.com/Quantitative-Characteristics-of-Rice-Grain-Quality-nTraits-and-Genetic-Parameters,208587,0,2.html
- ICAR-IIRR 56th ARGM Draft Proceedings (2021). -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- AICRIP Hybrid Rice Progress Report (2021). -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or DOI found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Shramik Krishi Kendra lists "Pioneer 28P67 hybrid Paddy Seed" for sale online (retail listing, price shown ₹1,599). -- https://shramikkrishikendra.com/product-category/paddy/
- Krishdoctor lists Pioneer 28P67 hybrid paddy seed for sale. -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/MlhtoJglp55aOqV7cKdq
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing found in the searches.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab and Haryana. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-28p67/ ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-27-new-varieties-of-paddy-for-farmers/
- A Hindi report from Krishak Jagat repeats the Punjab and Haryana recommendation. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/rice-variety-28p67/

NOTES
- Release year conflict: the record says 2023-05-02, and the national notification was 25 September 2023. The ICAR-IIRR draft says 28P67 was released in 2018 as a hybrid (CVRC). Verify against the official CSC/Gazette record.
- Type conflict: the national notice calls it an open-pollinated variety, while the record and the Pioneer product pages call it a hybrid. Verify the category before using it in a reference record.
- Scope limit: the four searches did not return official Indian sources (seednet.gov.in, ICAR or SAU pages, KrishiKosh). Most evidence is secondary or retailer material.

The digest lists Dholi among normal sali flood-prone-area varieties alongside Ranjit Sub-1, Bahadur Sub-1 and Jalashree, and a recent trial report describes Dholi as among varieties with broad adaptation across Assam's flood-prone landscapes (original trial source not identified). These statements indicate adaptation to flood-prone areas, not a graded flood tolerance level.

submergence.details: Dholi is described as a mid-duration submergence-tolerant variety and is reported to withstand 12 days of complete submergence. The parentage (Ranjit/Swarna Sub1//Ranjit) includes Sub1. The level is based on a single reported duration from a secondary source; no Dholi-specific submergence trial data or physiological mechanism was found. The digest's caveat notes that the RKB page entries (up to 2 weeks submergence, 2018) describe Ranjit-Sub1 and were excluded as Dholi evidence.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Dholi is described as a mid-duration submergence-tolerant variety developed at the station and notified by the government in 2022 -- https://www-aau-ac-in.translate.goog/department/department_details/120?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc
Dholi (AAU-TTB-Dhan-40, Ranjit/Swarna Sub1//Ranjit) is reported to withstand 12 days of complete submergence -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
Dholi is listed among the normal sali flood-prone-area varieties alongside Ranjit Sub-1, Bahadur Sub-1 and Jalashree -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
Caveat: the RKB stress-tolerant page has a heading "AAU-TTB Dhan 40 (Dholi)" but the entries beneath it describe Ranjit-Sub1 (2018, up to 2 weeks submergence, 5-5.5 t/ha). These entries refer to Ranjit-Sub1, not Dholi, and were discarded as Dholi evidence -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties
Drought, heat, salinity and no Dholi-specific tolerance data found -- searched; no evidence found beyond the submergence entries above.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned blast and BPH resistance statements in an AAU rice book, but these were not attributed to Dholi in the retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Dholi was among varieties with broad adaptation across Assam's flood-prone landscapes in a recent trial report (article dated about 49 days before retrieval; original trial source not identified) -- https://bioengineer.org/new-rice-varieties-show-stable-high-yields-across-assams-flood-prone-landscapes/
Dholi-specific yield figures, maturity and plant height: no evidence found. The yield and duration values on the RKB page belong to Ranjit-Sub1 (see STRESS TOLERANCE caveat) -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties
Seed-chain note: the AAU station reports that its foundation and certified seed production runs under a PPP model with FPCs at Golaghat and Jorhat, over 1000 q produced, though these lots are not specifically tied to Dholi in the text -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/120

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: Ranjit/Swarna Sub1//Ranjit -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University ; https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties
QTL or marker study naming Dholi: No evidence found. The Sub1 marker-assisted backcross papers found concern Ranjit-Sub1 and were excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325623708_Flood_proofing_of_Ranjit_a_popular_variety_of_North-Eastern_India_through_transfer_of_Sub1_rice_QTL_by_modified_marker-assisted_backcross_breeding

Lead breeder for Dholi: not identified in the evidence. Janardan Das is listed as involved, not as lead -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Mr-Janardan-Das/323
Developing institution and station: AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute (formerly Rice Experimental Station), Titabar, Assam Agricultural University, with Regional Agricultural Research Station, Titabor named as a station on its page -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/120 ; https://www.facebook.com/RARSTitabor/

seednet_fields.Parentage: The proposed variety has been developed from a cross CN 1216 X CN 1131-4-4-1-4. Both the parents are pre-breeding materials developed under Shuttle Breeding programme of International Rice Research Institute (IRRI).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: The variety may be recommended for Kharif season under rainfed low land condition.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Seed rate is 40 kg/ha (2-3 seedlings per hill)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Disease infection was below the threshold level for the proposed variety AAU-KMJ Dhan-46 (Surma Dhan) at RARS, Karimganj, Assam during kharif 2018 and 2019. Under field screening without artificial inoculation the proposed variety showed Resistant to highly Resistant reaction in respect of False smut and Neck blast diseases, Resistant against Brown spot and Highly Resistant reaction in respect of False smut and Neck blast diseases, Resistant against Brown spot and Highly reaction against BLB
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Under field screening without artificial inoculation the proposed variety, AAU-KMJ Dhan-46 (Surma Dhan) showed White Ear Heads (WEH) to the extent of 0.6-0.8% panicles (Score-)) indicating its Highly Resistant reaction against Stem borer. Similarly, it showed neglible damage (Score-0) in respect of Leaf folder (HR) and very slight injury (Score-1) in respect to BPH and GLH indicating Highly Resistant reactions against these two pests
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha):
60:20:40 kg/ha of N:P2O5:K2O
Basal: ½ N+ Full P2O5+3/4K2O
1st topdressing: ¼ N + ¼ K2O at 30-35 DAT
2nd topdreesing: ¼ N at Panicle initiation stage

The only parentage match is the rice variety ADT 39 (IR 8/IR 20), which is described as drought tolerant. The ADT 39 parentage resemblance suggests the 'IR 8 X IR 20' entry in the source data may be a rice parentage recorded in error for a sesame variety. drought.details: ADT 49 is identified as a drought tolerant variety. It is among the rice varieties listed as drought tolerant in various agricultural surveys and reports.

heat.details: ADT 49 is mentioned as a zonal check in the Southern region during Annual Rice Research Group Meetings where heat tolerance of rice varieties is discussed and screened. While not explicitly stated as 'heat tolerant,' its inclusion in such trials suggests a known performance or relevance in heat stress studies.

salinity.details: The variety grows well in saline soil and is well suited for it. It is also mentioned as a salt tolerant variety and included in evaluations of salt tolerant rice genotypes under saline conditions. It is suggested for YAAS affected saline lands.

flood.details: ADT 49 is tolerant to flood conditions and is recommended for flood-affected areas.

disease_resistance.summary: ADT 49 is reported to be resistant to blast and sheath rot.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety shows resistance to stem borer and brown plant hopper.

agronomic_details.yield: ADT 49 has an average yield of 6170 kg/ha. In comparative trials, another variety, ART (168), showed a yield of 5966 kg/ha, which was 10.5% higher than ADT 49, indicating ADT 49's yield serves as a benchmark.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety is recommended for irrigated conditions and grows well in sandy clay soil. It is considered ideal for the second season.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated conditions in Tamil Nadu. It is suitable as a Thaladi crop and for direct sowing.

drought.details: ADT 55 is a promising short duration rice variety developed through marker-assisted selection for drought tolerance. It possesses two drought-tolerant QTLs (qDTY1). Molecular breeding efforts have focused on developing varieties with inbuilt tolerance to drought. An abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_.Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is relevant to this context, as ADT 55 is listed as a drought tolerant variety. It is also mentioned as tolerant to drought in distribution to farmers.

heat.details: ADT 55 has been screened for high temperature tolerance. Development of abiotic tolerant rice varieties, including those with high temperature tolerance, has been a breeding focus, with ADT 55 listed among them.

salinity.details: ADT 55 is explicitly stated as tolerant to salt. It is also noted that crosses are being attempted involving multiple stress tolerant donors, including those for salt tolerance, and ADT 55 has been used as a parent in such crosses. Salt tolerance has been directly correlated with various rice varieties.

flood.details: While submergence tolerance is noted, general flood tolerance (e.g., flash flood, standing water depth) is not specified beyond its suitability for semi-deep water conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: ADT 55 is resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, sheath rot, grain discoloration, and Rice Tungro Disease (RTD). It is also moderately resistant to blast, sheath rot, and brown spot. It is resistant to bacterial leaf blight (BLB). Its parentage includes IRBB 60, a known source of bacterial blight resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: ADT 55 is moderately resistant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH 10) and moderately resistant to Stem Borer (SB). However, incidence of yellow stem borer has been noticed in ADT 55 paddy varieties in some areas.

agronomic_details.yield: Average reported yield is 59.3 q/ha. Another source indicates a yield of 65 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: ADT 55 is suitable for irrigated, wet conditions and also for semi-deep water, showing one-week submergence tolerance. It is classified as a short/early maturing variety and is non-Basmati type.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in Tamil Nadu under irrigated, wet conditions, including Kar/Kuruvai and Summer seasons. It is an early maturing variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (82 cm) plant height. Grains are Long Slender (LS), with soft gel consistency and good for cooking. It has intermediate amylase content and gelatinization temperature. It is also noted as a protein-rich paddy variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: ADT 55 has been produced and distributed to 74 farmers, indicating farmer acceptance and field performance. It has been screened at multiple centers for submergence and high temperature tolerance.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: ADT 55 was developed through Marker Assisted Selection (MAS). It possesses two drought-tolerant QTLs (qDTY1). A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_.Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is associated with its stress tolerance profile.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: It carries two identified Quantitative Trait Loci (QTLs) for drought tolerance, referred to as qDTY1.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety is a result of molecular breeding for inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast. It is derived from MAS and is involved in new crosses with multiple stress tolerant donors. Its parentage is recorded as ADT 43/IRBB 60.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae): listed as moderately resistant (BPT 2231) in the ANGRAU Bapatla Notable Achievements document. The digest notes that the snippet does not clearly tie this line to Akshaya rather than the neighbouring entry, so the attribution is unconfirmed. A 2014 ISSP South Zonal Seminar abstract (Agricultural College, Bapatla) reports that gamma-ray mutant lines of Akshaya were characterised for blast resistance; the digest gives no resistance level for these mutant lines. No evidence was found for other diseases. Note: the KAU 'Akshaya' (Kerala, released 2018) is a different variety and is excluded from this record.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE --
Akshaya (BPT 2231) is listed as moderately resistant to blast, but the snippet does not clearly tie that line to Akshaya rather than the neighbouring entry -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance -- searched, none in results.

DISEASE AND PEST --
Gamma-ray mutant lines of Akshaya were characterised for blast resistance, per a 2014 ISSP South Zonal Seminar abstract (Agricultural College, Bapatla) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259874628_Biofumigant_Activity_of_Brassica_Spp_Against_Soil_Borne_Plant_Pathogens
Blast reaction as "moderately resistant" -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf
Note: the KAU "Akshaya" (Kerala, released 2018: 130-140 days, moderately resistant to stem borer and leaf folder) is a different variety and must not be merged with this record -- https://kau.in/basic-page/varieties-released

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
Akshaya (BPT 2231) with parentage BPT 4358/IR64 appears in a multi-location/minikit trial table with yield values of 5.4, 2.02 and 2.67 (units not stated in snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287878106_Molecular_screening_for_fertility_restorer_genes_Rf3_Rf4_of_WA_-CMS_and_evaluation_of_F1_hybrids_in_rice_O_sativa_L_Arun_Kumar_Singh_P_Revathi_M_Pavani_R_M_Sundaram_P_Senguttuvel_K_B_KemparajuA_S_Hari_Prasad_C_N_Neeraja_N_Sravan_Raju_P_Kotewara_Rao_P_J_Suryendra_K.Jayaramulu_and_B.C._Viraktamath
Breeder-seed and cultivation-area data in the ARS Bapatla document refer to Sona Mahsuri, not Akshaya -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf
No evidence found for maturity days, yield ranges or season for Akshaya (BPT 2231) from a KVK or SAU source.

GENETICS AND QTL --
Parentage recorded as BPT 4358 / IR64 (matches the release record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287878106_Molecular_screening_for_fertility_restorer_genes_Rf3_Rf4_of_WA_-CMS_and_evaluation_of_F1_hybrids_in_rice_O_sativa_L_Arun_Kumar_Singh_P_Revathi_M_Pavani_R_M_Sundaram_P_Senguttuvel_K_B_KemparajuA_S_Hari_Prasad_C_N_Neeraja_N_Sravan_Raju_P_Kotewara_Rao_P_J_Suryendra_K.Jayaramulu_and_B.C._Viraktamath

Recommended states: No evidence found (the release record says "Not specified"). Regional context only: ANGRAU Bapatla works on Andhra Pradesh conditions, and Akshaya was tested in the Krishna zone minikit trials -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf

variety_name "Akshaya" and seednet_variety_name "AKSHAYA" are the same here; all evidence refers to Akshaya (BPT 2231) of ANGRAU Bapatla. No evidence found on the Seednet portal itself.

LIMITATIONS --
The web_search budget was used up after four queries, so the research was not finished. Breeder names, contacts, seed sources, KrishiKosh/AICRP records, and maturity and yield details remain open and should be checked directly on seednet.gov.in, angrau.ac.in and krishikosh.egranth.ac.in.
