drought.details: DRR Dhan 62 has been developed and released as a drought tolerant variety. It is suitable for irrigated conditions, indicating a general adaptability to controlled water environments, but its development explicitly addresses drought stress mitigation.

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance and is listed among varieties tolerant to heat stress. Research identified candidate genes for heat tolerance in rice, indicating a genetic basis for this trait.

salinity.details: DRR Dhan 62 is described as salinity tolerant and suitable for saline soils and salt-affected rice growing areas, including those in Gujarat.

flood.details: This variety has been developed for multiple stress tolerance, including flood, through Marker Assisted Breeding, specifically demonstrating submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: DRR Dhan 62 is resistant to Bacterial blight (BB) and Blast diseases. This resistance is genetically engineered through the introgression of multiple resistance genes.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields from IIRR, Hyderabad trials include ranges such as 24.20-25.90 t/ha and 44.70-45.00 t/ha. It is generally described as a high-yielding variety, with yield performance evaluated under stress-prone conditions.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety's release for a wide range of states and its multi-stress tolerance traits suggest good adaptability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DRR Dhan 62 is suitable for irrigated and transplanted cultivation systems. It also shows adaptation to areas affected by low soil phosphorus and saline conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: It is a fine-grain type rice variety known for its excellent cooking quality. It is an improved version of Improved Samba Mahsuri.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Performance data for DRR Dhan 62 have been reported in the Draft Proceedings of the 58th and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings (AICRIP-intranet.in), with trials conducted by ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The variety carries multiple resistance genes: Xa21, xa13, and xa5 for Bacterial blight resistance, and Pi2 and Pi54 for Blast resistance. It also contains the Sub1 QTL for seedling stage submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 and qDTY3.1 QTLs for reproductive stage submergence tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs introgressed include qSub1 for submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 + qDTY3.1 for reproductive stage submergence tolerance. These were introduced via Marker Assisted Breeding (MAB) and Marker-Assisted Introgression (MAI).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: DRR Dhan 62 is an improved version of 'Improved Samba Mahsuri', developed through Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) and Marker-Assisted Introgression to incorporate durable resistance genes and abiotic stress tolerance QTLs. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is noted in connection to DRR Dhan 62's development.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: The variety carries multiple resistance genes: Xa21, xa13, and xa5 for Bacterial blight resistance, and Pi2 and Pi54 for Blast resistance. It also contains the Sub1 QTL for seedling stage submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 and qDTY3.1 QTLs for reproductive stage submergence tolerance.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: QTLs introgressed include qSub1 for submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 + qDTY3.1 for reproductive stage submergence tolerance. These were introduced via Marker Assisted Breeding (MAB) and Marker-Assisted Introgression (MAI).
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: DRR Dhan 62 is an improved version of 'Improved Samba Mahsuri', developed through Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) and Marker-Assisted Introgression to incorporate durable resistance genes and abiotic stress tolerance QTLs. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is noted in connection to DRR Dhan 62's development.

agronomic_performance.yield: Reported yields from IIRR, Hyderabad trials include ranges such as 24.20-25.90 t/ha and 44.70-45.00 t/ha. It is generally described as a high-yielding variety, with yield performance evaluated under stress-prone conditions.
agronomic_performance.stability: The variety's release for a wide range of states and its multi-stress tolerance traits suggest good adaptability across different environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: DRR Dhan 62 is suitable for irrigated and transplanted cultivation systems. It also shows adaptation to areas affected by low soil phosphorus and saline conditions.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: It is a fine-grain type rice variety known for its excellent cooking quality. It is an improved version of Improved Samba Mahsuri.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Performance data for DRR Dhan 62 have been reported in the Draft Proceedings of the 58th and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings (AICRIP-intranet.in), with trials conducted by ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad.

drought.details: Dubraj Selection 1 is a short duration drought tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and drought-prone areas. It exhibits tolerance to abiotic stresses including drought. It is listed among SS (Sugarcane Sett) and Drought tolerant varieties.

heat.details: The variety shows tolerance to abiotic stresses, specifically including heat. It has been included in screening trials for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: Dubraj Selection 1 is reported to be tolerant to salinity. Its suitability for areas requiring saline water irrigation has been noted, and it has been a subject in studies related to yield and salinity tolerance in rice.

flood.details: While submergence tolerance is explicitly stated, general flood tolerance beyond submergence is not detailed in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: Dubraj Selection 1 is tolerant to leaf blast and neck blast.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety shows tolerance to White-backed Planthopper (WBPH).

agronomic_details.yield: The average yield for Dubraj Selection 1 is reported as 60-65 Quintals per hectare (Q/ha). Various trial results show varying yield contributions, indicating its performance across different experimental settings.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety's widespread evaluation in Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM) proceedings and IIRR Annual Reports across diverse agro-climatic conditions (irrigated, rainfed, semi-deep water, drought-prone, saline) suggests a degree of adaptability and stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Chhattisgarh, Dubraj Selection 1 is adapted to irrigated, direct sown rainfed conditions, short duration drought-prone areas, semi-deep water, and rainfed uplands. It is also suitable for rainfed lowland rice with medium water depth under anaerobic direct conditions and marginal lands.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dubraj Selection 1 is a Non-Basmati variety. Its grains are described as Long Slender (LS) and aromatic.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensive field trials have been conducted for Dubraj Selection 1, as evidenced by its repeated inclusion and performance data in the draft proceedings of the 55th, 58th, and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings and various annual reports of ICAR-IIRR (Indian Institute of Rice Research). These trials have assessed its performance under various stress conditions (drought, heat, submergence, salinity) and different planting systems.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (QTL, SNP, SSR) are detailed for Dubraj Selection 1 in the provided results. Stress tolerance traits are noted to be highly polygenic.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs or their effects are identified for Dubraj Selection 1.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) is mentioned in the context of research for drought, heat, and submergence stress tolerance, implying its potential application or relevance to this variety. The SUB1A gene, known for submergence tolerance, is also mentioned in proximity to Dubraj Selection 1 in research contexts.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Specific government seed corporations are not named, but the variety is part of the breeder seed multiplication program and varietal induction into the seed chain.
commercial_info.availability_status: Dubraj Selection 1 is part of the formal seed system and is implied to be available through official seed channels due to its inclusion in breeder seed multiplication and varietal induction processes.

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence for Ezhome-2 in the search results. The drought-tolerant entries in the KAU Package of Practices snippet (e.g., PTB 28) are other varieties.

heat.details: No heat tolerance data for Ezhome-2. A KAU 2019 report mentions a crop failure of about 80% when Ezhome 3 was tried under a high-stress condition (truncated snippet), and says nothing specific about Ezhome-2. A KAU 2016 report lists a high-temperature evaluation of 39 traditional genotypes, with no Ezhome-2 result shown.

salinity.details: Ezhome-2 is described as a high-yielding organic rice variety suited to coastal saline and non-saline fields. KAU Package of Practices lists it as suitable for the virippu (first crop) season in saline coastal areas, in the deep ill-drained Kaipad-type tract. Ezhome rice varieties are cited as examples of salt-tolerant cultivars from Kerala, and KAU produced truthfully labelled seed of saline-tolerant Ezhome varieties. The related Ezhome-1 (Jaya x Kuthiru) is reported as tolerant to salt-affected soil. Kuthiru and Orkayama are the traditional saline-tolerant parental landraces conserved by the Malabar Kaipad Farmers' Society, Ezhome, Kannur.

flood.details: The variety is recommended for deep ill-drained coastal tracts, which suggests tolerance of waterlogging. No direct flood tolerance data were found.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction data found for Ezhome-2.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction data found for Ezhome-2.

agronomic_details.yield: Not quantified for Ezhome-2 in the results. Ezhome-1 averages about 3.5 t/ha. Ezhome-3 reached 3.12 t/ha in a CSSRI evaluation.
agronomic_details.stability: Ezhome-2 was among the genotypes evaluated in saline trials (CSSRI Annual Report 2022 mentions Ezhome 3 as an ideal genotype). No stability data specific to Ezhome-2 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Coastal saline and non-saline fields of Kerala, including the Kaipad tracts of Kannur; virippu season; deep ill-drained soils.

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Red kernel, medium bold grain (per KAU Package of Practices snippet). Cooking studies note that Ezhome-2 had the highest water uptake, though cooking time was longer.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Evaluated in KAU quality and cooking studies, and in the CSSRI saline genotype evaluation (Ezhome 3 is the one named there).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CNR-2 (CSC name) / GNR-2 (Seednet name), rice

Search budget: all 4 allowed web_search calls were used (3 for CNR-2, 1 for GNR-2 seed availability). None returned evidence about either name, so most headings below read "No evidence found." The GNR-2 release, breeder, and research topics were not searched, so their "No evidence found" entries mean only that the 4-call cap was reached. A follow-up run is needed for those.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searched "CNR-2 rice variety release recommended states maturity yield"; results were unrelated US and IRRI material.
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Same search as above; no CNR-2 or GNR-2 resistance data returned.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. Same search as above; no maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for CNR-2 or GNR-2.
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The CNR-2 QTL search returned a 2020 Agronomy paper on grain-number QTL (https://doi.org/10.3390/agronomy10020180), but it does not mention CNR-2 or GNR-2, so it is not recorded as evidence.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. Searched "CNR-2 rice breeder developed by institute"; results were a hybrid rice breeding manual and nothing on this variety. No GNR-2 breeder search was run.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or contact page for either name was returned.
PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The CNR-2 research search returned no papers, AICRP reports, or KrishiKosh theses on this variety.
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Searched "GNR-2 paddy variety seed availability"; the only Indian result was a Nuziveedu Seeds generic paddy catalogue page (https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/paddy-variety/), which does not name GNR-2 or CNR-2, so it is not recorded as evidence.
RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. No notification or release record for either name was returned. The input fields "Not specified" for institution, release year, states, and parentage remain unresolved.

Suggested next steps: search seednet.gov.in and the ICAR/CSC release notifications for "GNR-2" and "CNR-2" separately, and check KrishiKosh and the AICRP rice annual reports. Also verify whether "CNR" and "GNR" refer to the same variety, since the two names may be a transcription difference.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The GRH-2 pages returned only general descriptions. Searches also returned Ezhome and Golden Rice pages, which are unrelated. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/61ec6-annual-report-proof-2017-18.pdf (searched; GRH-2 named only as a new variety)

DISEASE AND PEST -- GRH-2 is moderately resistant against bacterial leaf blight, leaf blast, grain discolouration and sheath rot. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- The proposed hybrid is tolerant to insect pest like BPH, WBPH, leaf folder and stem borer. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- GNR-2 (Seednet name): No evidence found. The Main Rice Research Centre page lists GNR-2 only as one of seven improved varieties, with no resistance data. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- Green rice leafhopper (GRH) gene and QTL papers were returned. They concern a different pest and different rice lines, so they are discarded. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00122-006-0270-x

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Mid-late rice hybrid GRH-2 (6129 kg/ha) performed well in Gujarat state, where it exhibited overall 7.1% and 17.9% grain yield superiority over the best hybrid check US 312, and best variety GNR-3, respectively. (season 2017-18, as stated on the page) -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Grain quality: medium slender grain rice hybrid GRH-2 contains intermediate amylose and high head rice recovery. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Release timing conflict: the NAU 2017-18 annual report lists GRH-2 among two rice varieties developed that year, while the CSC release date is 2019-06-01. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/61ec6-annual-report-proof-2017-18.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- GNR-2 agronomy and trial data: No evidence found. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for GRH-2 or GNR-2 marker, QTL or parentage studies. Parentage is not specified in the record, and the searches did not establish it. Search returned only unrelated GRH resistance genes and Golden Rice work. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11769587/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: The NAU has released 105 high yielding good quality varieties of various crops including 18 varieties of cotton, 20 varieties of rice. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Station: the Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari, which is the breeding station named on the GRH-2 information sheet. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Breeder name: No GRH-2-specific breeder name was found. The ResearchGate profile of Vipul P. Patel, Rice Breeder at NAU, does not mention GRH-2, so it is not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Staff at the GRH-2 seed MoU signing: Dr. T. R. Ahlawat (Director of Research), Dr. V. P. Patel (Associate Research Scientist, RRRS Vyara), Dr. P. B. Patel (Associate Research Scientist, MRRC Navsari) and Prof. Sheetal Patel (Assistant Research Scientist, RRRS Vyara). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-3 (rice / PADDY (DHAN))
Variety name (CSC minutes) and Seednet name are both "GNR-3", so one name covers both. Only 4 web_search calls were allowed and all 4 ran, but I could only read ~400 characters of each result, so the findings below are partial. Seednet portal pages were not found.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for GNR-3.
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page on GNR-3 blast, BLB, BPH or other resistance was returned.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for field-trial, yield or maturity data. The one GNR-3 paper located (see PUBLICATIONS) appears to concern processing or value addition, not field performance.
GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage only. A GNR-3 record describes it as derived from the cross IR-28 x GR-4 -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/ohs-2.3.1/index.php/record/view/213880 (the Seednet "Not specified" parentage is therefore contradicted by this record, which should be checked). No QTL or marker study was found.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Navsari Agricultural University is the institution in the input record. No breeder or scientist name was found tied to GNR-3 in the snippets read. The Navsari Main Rice Research Centre document surfaced (https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf) but its visible text did not name GNR-3, so I have not attributed it to this variety. Treat it as an unverified lead.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official email, phone, address or contact page for GNR-3 or its developing division was confirmed.
PUBLICATIONS:
Authors not captured (year not captured). A paddy variety GNR-3 suitable for value addition. ICAR KRISHI record -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/ohs-2.3.1/index.php/record/view/213880
Authors not captured (year not captured). A paddy variety GNR-3 suitable for value addition. ResearchGate (PDF) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374419133_A_paddy_variety_GNR-3_suitable_for_value_addition
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for GNR-3. A Kerala search result (kau.in, Pattambi paddy seed availability) concerns a different station and was discarded.
RECOMMENDED STATES: Gujarat, per the input record only (recommended_states_raw). No search page confirmed this.

Note: the search budget was exhausted during a further attempt to read full page text, so the gaps above are due to the tool limit, not confirmed absence. Next steps: open the two KRISHI/ResearchGate pages for authors, year and full text, and check seednet.gov.in directly for release notification and parentage.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to GNR-4. The searches returned only unrelated rice papers.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to GNR-4. The searches returned only unrelated rice papers.

salinity.details: No GNR-4-specific evidence found. The only salinity source retrieved is a generic meta-analysis that the digest marks as not GNR-4-specific, so it is not used as evidence.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to GNR-4.

disease_resistance.summary: No blast, brown planthopper (BPH) or bacterial blight reaction for GNR-4 was found in searched sources. Not found in searched sources for any disease resistance rating.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer: GNR-4 showed a moderately susceptible reaction under natural field conditions at the Main Rice Research Centre (MRRC), Navsari, alongside GR-4 and varieties 6, 9 and 103. This is a susceptibility rating, not resistance. A Mistry and Patel paper includes a table on GNR-4's reaction to major insect pests at MRRC Navsari, but the retrieved text does not show the scores. No other pest reactions found.

agronomic_details.yield: Under irrigated transplanted conditions in South Gujarat, GNR-4 averaged 4409 kg/ha, which is 103% above Lal Kada and 11.2% above GR-11.
agronomic_details.stability: A location-wise comparison table (PET Kharif 2009, Navsari and other South Gujarat sites) against Lal Kada and GR-11 exists, but the values are not in the retrieved text. Stability across environments: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for transplanted rice in South Gujarat's heavy-rainfall zone (AES-III), according to the NAU Main Rice Research Centre. Adaptation outside South Gujarat: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources for plant morphology. Grain nutritional profile: iron about 91 ppm, dietary fibre about 2.87%, beta-carotene about 0.53 ppm. The NAU document advises spraying a 1% iron solution for bio-fortification.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Tested in kharif seasons 2009 to 2012 through the preliminary evaluation trial, small-scale and large-scale varietal trials, and district trials under transplanted conditions. (2) Under irrigated transplanted conditions in South Gujarat, mean yield of 4409 kg/ha, 103% above Lal Kada and 11.2% above GR-11. (3) Location-wise comparison in PET Kharif 2009 at Navsari and other South Gujarat sites against Lal Kada and GR-11 (table values not retrieved). (4) Stem borer natural-field screening at MRRC Navsari: moderately susceptible.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-4 (rice, paddy)

Name note: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "GNR-4", so one search set covered both. No Seednet portal page for GNR-4 was retrieved. All evidence below refers to the name GNR-4 (Gujarat Navsari Rice-4).

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GNR-4. The searches returned only a generic salinity meta-analysis and unrelated rice papers. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11003983/ (not GNR-4-specific)

DISEASE AND PEST
GNR-4 showed a moderately susceptible reaction to stem borer under natural field conditions at the Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari, alongside GR-4 and varieties 6, 9 and 103. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
The Mistry and Patel paper includes a table on GNR-4's reaction to major insect pests at MRRC Navsari, but the retrieved text does not show the scores. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
No blast, BPH or bacterial blight reaction for GNR-4 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Derived from NAUR-1 x Lal Kada, crossed at the Main Paddy Research Station, Navsari, in kharif 2005. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Bulked to F5 in summer 2009. Tested in the kharif seasons 2009 to 2012 through the preliminary evaluation trial, small-scale and large-scale varietal trials, and district trials under transplanted conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Under irrigated transplanted conditions in South Gujarat it averaged 4409 kg/ha, which is 103% above Lal Kada and 11.2% above GR-11. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Location-wise comparison table (PET Kharif 2009, Navsari and other South Gujarat sites) against Lal Kada and GR-11. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Nutritional profile: iron about 91 ppm, dietary fibre about 2.87%, beta-carotene about 0.53 ppm. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Maturity duration: not found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies on GNR-4. The GNS4/DWARF11 and gsnl4 papers concern other rice lines and were excluded. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12284-017-0171-4 (excluded, different variety)
Pedigree information is in the AGRONOMY section above. Parentage field "Not specified" should be updated to NAUR-1 x Lal Kada. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by Navsari Agricultural University. The authors listed on the GNR-4 paper are Pramodkumar Mistry and Pathik Patel, both at Navsari Agricultural University, with Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari, given as the affiliation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
The NAU crop-improvement listing names GNR-4 among the NAU-developed rice varieties. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
Vipul P. Patel (rice breeder, Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara) and P. B. Patel (Main Rice Research Centre) were excluded. Neither page links them to GNR-4.

CONTACT DETAILS
Names and roles as found: Pramodkumar Mistry (author, Navsari Agricultural University); Pathik Patel (author, Navsari Agricultural University; the paper identifies P. B. Patel as corresponding author). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Institution: Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari 396 450, Gujarat, India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Institute page URL: https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676 (no email or phone retrieved).
Official email: not found. Phone: not found. Postal address of the MRRC division: not found beyond the city and postal code above.

PUBLICATIONS
Mistry, P. M. and Patel, P. B. (2014). Bio-fortified rice variety Gujarat Navsari Rice-4 (GNR-4). Journal not identified (ResearchGate listing dated January 2014) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4 (DOI not found)
Excluded: "A paddy variety GNR-3 suitable for value addition" (Mistry et al.). Its title and main cross concern GNR-3, although its abstract text mentions GNR-4. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374419133_A_paddy_variety_GNR-3_suitable_for_value_addition
No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or peer-reviewed paper specific to GNR-4 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The searches returned seed listings for other varieties and firms: the Gujarat State Seeds Corporation (Gurabini) crop page lists GR4, GR11, GNR-3 and NAUR-1 for paddy, not GNR-4 (http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=1). The IFFDC and Nuziveedu paddy lists do not include GNR-4 (https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed; https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/paddy-variety/). The GSFC seeds page names paddy but no GNR-4 variety (https://www.gsfclimited.com/seeds).

RECOMMENDED STATES
Recommended for South Gujarat: the NAU Main Rice Research Centre advises transplanted-rice growers in South Gujarat's heavy-rainfall zone (AES-III) to grow GNR-4 for its higher net returns, and to spray a 1% iron solution for bio-fortification. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
Registration: the same NAU document says GNR-4 was registered with PPV&FRA, but it gives no registration number or date. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
Release notification date for 2016-08-12 (CSC minutes): not confirmed by any retrieved source.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GJ-103 (Seednet name GR-103), sorghum, NAU Main Sorghum Research Station, Surat

Searches run (4): "GJ-103 sorghum variety"; "GJ-103 sorghum breeder Navsari Agricultural University"; "GJ-103 sorghum GR-11 x Mahsuri research"; "GR-103 sorghum seed availability Gujarat". Neither GJ-103 nor GR-103 appeared in any result that names this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The variety search returned only pages on other sorghum lines, such as GDJ 1 (Banas Surya), which is a different variety, and foreign or unrelated products.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) page reports disease and borer scores for that other variety, so it was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. Excluded as other varieties or crops: GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) multi-location yield data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat ; CoFS 29 fodder trial, Kheda -- https://www.gjoee.org/papers/1266.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The parentage GR-11 x Mahsuri did not appear in any result. Excluded: a sorghum GWAS and an unrelated Ma/Dw gene paper, neither about this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No breeder name found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The NAU "About" page is institution-level and says The Navsari Zone of erstwhile GAU had attained the status of independent State Agricultural University (SAU) with the promulgation of Gujarat Agricultural Universities Act 2004; it does not name this variety. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676
Excluded: a 2025 AGRESCO proceedings page lists NAU's endorsed sorghum variety GNJ-1, which is a different variety -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//18th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_773.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder or station contact found under GJ-103 or GR-103. Institute-level fallback only (this page does not name the variety): Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari – 396450, as printed on a KVK Navsari Scientific Advisory Committee report -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/d9016-14-th-sac-21-final-reoprt.pdf
No email or phone for the Main Sorghum Research Station, Athwa Farm, Surat was found.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or journal paper naming this variety appeared.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The results were general sorghum grain dealers in Ahmedabad (for example, https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sorghum-22836423391.html) and a state-wise seed supplier list that names the Gujarat State Seeds Corporation generically, not for this variety (https://nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/state-wise-list-of-seeds-producer-supplier). None are variety-specific, so none are recorded as seed sources.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103 in the search results. The only statement of Gujarat as the recommended state comes from the supplied variety record, not from a web source.

Gaps to close next: the CSC release minutes for GJ-103 (2025), the Seednet entry for GR-103, and the NAU Main Sorghum Research Station page. These were not reachable with the four searches allowed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Search 1 ("GR-20 (Navsari Kamod) NVSR-407 rice variety") returned no page naming this variety. The top hit was a NAU variety page about NVSR-2528, a different rice variety, so it was discarded. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found. https://nau.in/nauvariety

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Search 1 returned no page naming GR-20, Navsari Kamod, NVSR-407 or IET-27797 with blast, BLB, BPH or other disease/pest reaction data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Search 3 ("GR-20 Navsari Kamod rice research paper trial") returned the ICAR-IIRR Annual Report 2022, which is general national rice reporting and does not mention this variety. Search 1 also returned the NAU page for NVSR-2528, which is a different variety. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for this variety was found. https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Searches 1 and 3 returned no QTL, marker or parentage information. Parentage is still unspecified in the record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for this variety. Search 2 ("GR-20 Navsari Kamod rice breeder Navsari Agricultural University") returned a ResearchGate profile for Vipul Patel, listed as a rice breeder at Navsari Agricultural University. The page does not name GR-20, Navsari Kamod or NVSR-407, so it is not attributed to this variety. https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact or NAU/Regional Rice Research Station contact page was returned for this variety. The Vipul Patel profile above is the only contact-related hit and is not linked to this variety, so no name, email, phone or address is recorded.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report or KrishiKosh item naming GR-20, Navsari Kamod, NVSR-407 or IET-27797 was returned. The only items seen were the ICAR-IIRR Annual Report 2022, which does not mention this variety, and the NAU page for NVSR-2528.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Search 4 ("NVSR-407 IET-27797 paddy seed availability Gujarat") returned an IFFDC seed availability page listing Gujarat Cumin-1. That is a different crop and variety and was discarded. No Seednet, NSC, Gujarat State Seed Corporation, KVK, NAU seed sales or dealer listing was found. https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record field says "Gujarat", but no page in the results confirmed this recommendation for GR-20, Navsari Kamod, NVSR-407 or IET-27797.

NAME NOTE -- Searches used "GR-20 (Navsari Kamod) NVSR-407" for the CSC release name and "NVSR-407 IET-27797" for the Seednet name, but no result matched either name. The search budget of four queries is now used up, so the gaps above need follow-up on the NAU rice programme site, the Seednet portal, KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Rice reports.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to GNR-6. The ICAR Annual Report 2019-20 lists GNR-6 as suitable for rainfed transplanted conditions in Gujarat, which describes adaptation to rainfed cultivation and does not establish drought tolerance. The NAU Main Rice Research Centre page lists GNR-6 among released varieties but gives no stress data for it.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to GNR-6.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to GNR-6. A salt-affected-area statement near GNR-6 on the NAU page is fragmented and cannot be safely attributed to GNR-6, so it is not used.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to GNR-6.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The NAU Main Rice Research Centre page contains reaction descriptions (moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight, grain discoloration and sheath rot; tolerance to BPH). The text is fragmented and the row layout does not confirm that these apply to GNR-6, so they are treated as unverified and are not recorded as confirmed resistance for GNR-6.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The same NAU page describes moderate resistance to stem borer, leaf folder and sheath mite, but the text is fragmented and does not confirm these apply to GNR-6. Treated as unverified.

agronomic_details.yield: 4500.00 to 5500.00 Kg/Ha (from the variety data record). No yield value for GNR-6 was confirmed in the evidence digest. The 65 to 70 q/ha entry in the ICAR Annual Report 2019-20 sits between the GNR-6 and GNR-7 rows and is not attributed to GNR-6.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The NAU page states GNR-6 performed well across Gujarat, but the surrounding text is fragmented and no multi-environment stability data was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in South Gujarat under transplanted conditions (variety data record). The ICAR Annual Report 2019-20 lists GNR-6 as suitable for rainfed transplanted conditions in Gujarat.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Vyara trial, 2018 to 2020, Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara: GNR 6 was compared with Purna, GR 5 and IR 28 under 100% and 50% recommended nitrogen with FYM. The results are truncated and no yield values are recorded. (2) Heterosis evaluation, kharif 2018, Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari: the cross NVSR-398 x GNR-6 was among the top three heterotic hybrids for grain yield per plant (reported in the GNR-4 study; no yield values given in the digest). (3) The Scribd RRRS variety list names GNR-6 among notable varieties released since 2014, with no agronomic data in the excerpt. No other trial results for GNR-6 were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL or marker study for GNR-6 found. Parentage per variety data: a derivative of the cross (GR 3 x PUSA-33).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL study for GNR-6 found. A heterosis study on GNR-4 reports the cross NVSR-398 x GNR-6 among the top three heterotic hybrids for grain yield per plant (evaluated at Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari, kharif 2018). This shows GNR-6 used as a parent; it is not a QTL study and reports no QTL effects.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GNR-6 / GR-6 (rice, Navsari Agricultural University) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: the search results name this variety as GNR-6 (variety code NVSR-2031). No result for the Seednet name GR-6 was relevant, so every finding below refers to GNR-6 unless marked otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GNR-6. A NAU Main Rice Research Centre page lists GNR-6 among its released varieties but gives no stress data for it -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- The same NAU page has a row for GNR-6 that says it performed well across Gujarat. The surrounding text is fragmented, so the salt-affected-area statement nearby cannot be safely attributed to GNR-6 -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The NAU Main Rice Research Centre page contains reaction descriptions (moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight, grain discoloration and sheath rot; tolerance to BPH; moderate resistance to stem borer, leaf folder and sheath mite). The text is fragmented and the row layout does not confirm these apply to GNR-6, so treat them as unverified -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- GNR-6 is listed in the ICAR Annual Report 2019-20 as suitable for rainfed transplanted conditions in Gujarat -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- A yield (65 to 70 q/ha) and maturity (120 to 125 days) entry appears in the same ICAR report, but the excerpt sits between the GNR-6 and GNR-7 rows and cannot be confidently assigned to GNR-6. Not recorded as a GNR-6 finding -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- A field experiment at the Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara (2018 to 2020) compared GNR 6 with Purna, GR 5 and IR 28 under 100% and 50% recommended nitrogen with FYM. The results are truncated, so no yield values are recorded -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- The Scribd copy of an RRRS variety list names GNR-6 among notable varieties released since 2014, but gives no agronomic data in the excerpt. Its original source is unverified -- https://www.scribd.com/document/867808197/6c31c-Varities-English

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker study for GNR-6 found.
- A heterosis study on GNR-4 (Mistry and Patel, NAU) reports that the cross NVSR-398 x GNR-6 was among the top three heterotic hybrids for grain yield per plant, evaluated at Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari in kharif 2018. This shows GNR-6 used as a parent; it is not a QTL study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Navsari Agricultural University. The NAU Main Rice Research Centre lists GNR-6 among its seven released varieties, and the centre is in SWMRU, Navsari -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Station: Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari (NAU) is named as the centre for paddy improvement, and the Regional Rice Research Station at Vyara is also a rice-breeding station -- https://nau.in/unithome/Regional%20Rice%20Research%20Station%20Vyara
- Breeder name: No evidence found that names the lead breeder of GNR-6. Vipul P. Patel's ResearchGate profile identifies him as a rice breeder at NAU's Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, but no page links him to GNR-6's development. He is not attributed as breeder -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- No evidence found for the breeder or developer named on an NAU variety page for GNR-6.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Navsari Agricultural University. No official email or phone number for the rice programme was found in the results. Address details found: Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari (from the centre information page) -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara (Tapi district): the page gives the location (about 4 km from Gandevi town) but no postal address or phone -- https://nau.in/unithome/Regional%20Rice%20Research%20Station%20Vyara
- Institute contact page: No evidence found for an NAU contact-page URL in the results. The NAU about page is at https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676 but contains no contact details.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Patel, V. P., and co-authors (years not shown in results). Field experiment at Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, 2018 to 2020, comparing GNR 6 with Purna, GR 5 and IR 28. Journal/report not identified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- Mistry, P., and Patel, P. (year not shown in results). Bio-fortified rice variety Gujarat Navsari Rice-4 (GNR-4). Journal not identified. The paper names GNR-6 as a parent in a top heterotic cross. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to GNR-6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The Gujarat State Seeds Corporation crop-details page lists GNR-6 in a kharif paddy table with a price per 25 kg. The page is undated, so current availability is unconfirmed -- http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=1
- The Gujcomasol page lists paddy varieties GR-13, Gurjary, GNR-3 and Mahisagar but not GNR-6 -- https://www.gujcomasol.com/seeds.php
- No evidence found for GNR-6 at Seednet, KVKs, or private dealers. The GSFC and Nuziveedu paddy pages do not name GNR-6.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat. The ICAR Annual Report 2019-20 lists GNR-6 with Gujarat as its state -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- The NAU Main Rice Research Centre page says GNR-6 performed well across Gujarat -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

Searches run: 4 (release and traits; breeder and institution; research and trials; seed availability). The Seednet portal was not reached directly, and the GR-6 name returned nothing relevant.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned only pages on other NAU rice varieties: GNR-3 (IR-28 x GR-4), reported as similar to Gurjari for pest and disease reaction, and GNR-4 (NAUR-1 x Lal Kada). Neither is this variety. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/OIJR/article/view/71223 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The search returned an NAU earhead-bug screening paper covering IR-28 and Jaya, not GR 16 or GR-6. -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0003914

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. A Vyara field study (2018-2020) names GR 5 and GNR 6, not GR 16 or GR-6; it is discarded. A 2022 Navsari KVK frontline demonstration names GNR-6, also discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27 ; https://nau.in/assets/uploads/1c2d5-15-th-sac-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The only genetics hit is a salinity meta-analysis correction from NAU and Vyara authors, which does not name this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11003983/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution-level only; no breeder named for this variety.
- NAU was established under Gujarat Act No. 5 of 2004 and is headquartered at Navsari. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676
- NAU runs 25 research centres at 15 locations for mandate crops including paddy. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676
- A Regional Rice Research Station at Vyara is listed as an NAU unit in a 2024 affiliation. This station is named in the release record, but no page ties it to GR 16 or GR-6. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11003983/
- Breeder name: none found for this variety. Breeders named on NAU paddy pages (P. B. Patel, Main Rice Research Centre; V. P. Patel, Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara) appear only in unrelated thesis listings. They are not attributed here. -- https://old.nau.in/alloprtitle.php

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No official NAU or Regional Rice Research Station email, phone, or postal address was found in the results. The only institutional URL retrieved is the NAU about page; verify contacts there or via the NAU main site.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. None of the retrieved papers or theses names GR 16 or GR-6. Papers found were about GNR-3, GNR-4, and unrelated rice studies; they are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The Gujarat State Seeds Corporation (Gurabini) paddy listing names IR-28, Masuri, Jaya, Gurjari and Dandi, not GR 16 or GR-6. Retailer pages (Nuziveedu, BigHaat, Bombay Super Seeds) list other varieties only. No Seednet portal page was returned. -- http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=1 ; https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/paddy-variety/ ; https://www.bighaat.com/collections/paddy-seeds

No evidence found. "Gujarat" is taken only from the input record. The IRRI-NARES release list and the ICAR-IIRR release page mention Gujarat for other varieties, not this one. -- https://www.irri.org/news-and-events/news/31-high-impact-irri-nares-developed-rice-varieties-now-available-across-india

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-7 (release/evidence name) / GR-7 (Seednet name), NVSR-6128, rice, Navsari Agricultural University

Search note: four web_search queries were run (variety, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability). Most results were about other crops or varieties (for example Gamagora 7, Ratnagiri 7, Ghd7 gene papers) and were discarded. Unless stated otherwise, the findings below refer to GNR-7 (NVSR-6128), which the source names directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The variety search returned only unrelated pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
- GNR-7 is moderately resistant against bacterial leaf blight, grain discoloration and sheath rot. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- It showed tolerant to pest like BPH and moderate (the sentence is cut off in the source) -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Trial result: GNR-7 (5740 kg/ha) performed very well in South Gujarat, where it exhibited overall 13.0 %, 22.8% and 12.4 % grain yield superiority with easy threshability over the checks GNR-2, GR-11 and GAR-13, respectively. The source dates the trial to 2016-17. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Plant type: It has short slender grain, high productive tillers and number of grains per panicle with good quality characters. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Maturity, duration and parentage (GR-3 x Basmati-370): No evidence found in the search results.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The QTL and gene results returned were for Ghd7, GL7 and other genes in unrelated rice germplasm.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is listed among the seven improved varieties released by the Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University. Seven improved varieties (NAUR-1, GNR-2, GNR-3, GNR-4, Purna, GNR-5, GNR-6, GNR-7 and GR-15) and two hybrids (GNRH-1 and GRH-2) of rice have been developed there. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- The same document links the code and name directly: Rice variety NVSR-6128 (GNR-7) recommended for normal rice growing areas of South Gujarat. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. A ResearchGate profile for Vipul P. Patel lists a rice breeder at NAU's Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara. That page does not mention GNR-7, so it is not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- Release year: the 2018-08-10 date from the input could not be confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level address (from a publication address for the same centre, not a GNR-7 page): Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari 396 450, Gujarat, India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
- Also listed as the Main Rice Research Centre in the centre information sheet: "SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari." -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Breeder email, phone and personal contact: No evidence found. A phone number found in the results (9426960246) belongs to a soil scientist at a different NAU unit and was discarded.

PUBLICATIONS
- No GNR-7-specific paper found.
- Ambiguous, not attributed to GNR-7: a paper on GNR-3 uses a check labelled "GR-7" (the Seednet name). It is unclear whether that check is the same variety. Authors and year not shown in the result. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374419133_A_paddy_variety_GNR-3_suitable_for_value_addition
- AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses and DOIs: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Gujarat State Seeds Corporation (GURABIN) lists "GR-7" among its kharif paddy varieties, with no price shown and only "Place Demand" as the availability note. The listing does not state that GR-7 is the same variety as GNR-7. -- http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=1
- NAU Mega Seed Project production figures, and any NSC, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing for GNR-7: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat only. The source recommends the variety for normal rice growing areas of South Gujarat. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

drought.details: GR-8 is described as a drought-tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and showing tolerance to moisture stress. It was evaluated in trials focusing on drought-tolerant varieties.

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat tolerance, with studies examining water use efficiency and heat tolerance traits in relation to grain yield. It is noted in the context of breeding for climate change focusing on genes with large effects on heat tolerance.

salinity.details: GR-8 is identified as a salt-tolerant variety, performing well under coastal saline eco-systems and showing tolerance to soil salinity.

flood.details: GR-8 shows tolerance to waterlogging and is suitable for semi-deep water conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: GR-8 exhibits resistance to White Backed Plant Hopper (WBPH), Stem Borer (SB), Leaf Folder (LF), and Leaf Blight (LB).

pest_resistance.summary: The variety is tolerant to root-knot nematodes.

agronomic_details.yield: Grain yield for GR-8 is reported to be 45-50 quintals per hectare (4.5-5.0 t/ha). Seed yield figures from trials were lower, ranging from 704 kg/ha to 0.94 t/ha (940 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: The widespread mention and evaluation of GR-8 across various agricultural reports (AICRIP, CRIDA, AAU) suggest a degree of environmental stability and adaptability, though explicit stability data is not provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: GR-8 is well-adapted to direct sown rainfed conditions, semi-deep water areas, rainfed uplands, and coastal saline ecosystems. It shows adaptability to regions experiencing drought, moisture stress, soil crusting, cracking, and soil salinity.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 75-80 days, with some reports indicating 45-50 days. It is characterized as an extra early maturity genotype.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: An extra early, erect, semi tall, non-loding genotype with strong culm, well exerted and lax panicles with purple apiculus, awnless spikelets and very coarse grains. It is also noted as non-shattering and semi-dwarf (82 cm).
agronomic_details.field_trials: GR-8 has been part of national agricultural research programs, including the All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) and trials conducted by ICAR-CRIDA and Anand Agricultural University (AAU), where its performance, particularly seed yield, was recorded.

drought.details: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results due to matching parentage) is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, recognized as a short-duration drought-tolerant rice variety, and exhibits inbuilt tolerance to drought and moisture stress. It has been identified as a drought-tolerant variety in various trials.

heat.details: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) is considered an efficient genotype for heat tolerance and has been studied for its response to heat and water stress. It exhibits tolerance to terminal heat stress, particularly when heat stress is imposed at the panicle initiation stage. It is also used as a check variety in studies evaluating potential heat stress.

salinity.details: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) is explicitly listed as a salt-tolerant variety. It is included in international soil stress tolerance nurseries and has been mentioned in the context of tolerance to soil crusting, cracking, soil salinity, and low saline phases. It is also described as a tolerant rice variety for coastal saline ecosystems.

flood.details: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) exhibits tolerance to water logging and is suitable for semi-deep water conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) exhibits inbuilt tolerance to biotic stresses. Specific resistance levels for individual diseases are not detailed in the provided results.

pest_resistance.summary: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) is moderately resistant to Stem Borer (SB).

agronomic_details.stability: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) is frequently used as a 'best check' variety in various trials, indicating its consistent performance and reliability as a benchmark for comparison.
agronomic_details.adaptation: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) is adapted for rainfed, direct sown conditions. It is specifically recommended for and grown in Gujarat, and also performs well in semi-deep and deep water areas and rainfed uplands.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) is a semi-tall variety, classified as early and medium coarse grain type. Morphological characteristics include a compact and well-exerted panicle, green apiculus, and awnless spikelets.
agronomic_details.field_trials: GR 19 (identified as GR-9 in search results) has been extensively tested under the All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP), included in Soil Stress Tolerant Trials, and evaluated in International Rice Soil Stress Tolerance Nurseries (IRSSTN). It has also been part of evaluations related to hybrid rice experiments and nutrient management under high and low input conditions.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-9 (Seednet name GR-9; variety code Lalkada Gold), rice/paddy, Gujarat

Search budget note: I ran four web_search queries, one per required topic plus the optional seed-availability query. A further batch of name-check queries was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so no additional evidence was gathered.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The four searches returned no page naming GNR-9, GR-9 or Lalkada Gold with stress-tolerance data. The results were a general rice-types nutrition article, a BPH-resistant hybrid restorer-line paper (PMC5461369), a glutaredoxin review in rice (PMC10707574), and a rice seed supply article (farmprogress.com).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The same search results apply; none named this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No page with maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The parentage (SATHI 34-36 x CR-544-1-2) did not appear in any result. The PMC5461369 hit concerns other restorer lines and is not attributed to this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page named a breeder or scientist for GNR-9/GR-9. The institution (Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, Navsari Agricultural University) did not appear in any result.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official NAU, Vyara station, or ICAR contact page was returned.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No Seednet listing, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer page for GNR-9, GR-9 or Lalkada Gold was returned. The seed-related hit (farmprogress.com) concerns a US rice seed market and is unrelated.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. Gujarat is the state given in the release record, but no retrieved page confirmed it.

Recommended next steps: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) directly for "GR-9" under PADDY (DHAN), check the CSC/ICAR release notification for the 17 June 2022 release, and query the Navsari Agricultural University Vyara rice station site and KrishiKosh for "GNR-9" or "Lalkada Gold". These sources were not reachable within this search budget.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The searches returned two different names. The evidence for "Gujarat Anand Rice 22 (Swagat)" comes from AAU pages. The Seednet name "GUJARAT ANAND RICE-2 (IET-21614)" is attached to a different AAU variety, GAR-2 (released 2011). Pages about GAR-2 are therefore not attributed to GAR 22 below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to white-backed planthopper, yellow stem borer and leaf folder, and resistant to leaf blast and neck blast. Moderately resistant to bacterial leaf blight, sheath rot and grain discoloration -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The search returned no pages on these traits for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Insect resistance (planthopper, stem borer, leaf folder), blast resistance (leaf and neck), and moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight, sheath rot and grain discoloration are as listed above -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average grain yield of 5613 kg/ha, reported as 22.6% above check GR 7 and 15.1% above check GAR 3 -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- Milling recovery of 72.08% and head rice recovery of 62.80%, at or above the checks -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- Medium maturity, medium plant height, more productive tillers, long slender kernel -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- No multi-location trial, AICRP or on-farm trial results found specifically for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage (GURJARI IET-10750 x IET-14714/1-1-4-1-3-2) or for any QTL or marker study. The searches did not return any page naming this parentage.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Anand Agricultural University, Anand (listed as the source of the variety on the AAU site) -- https://aau.in/variety_released
- The AAU variety page lists the variety under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education and the Main Rice Research Station context, but no named breeder or scientist was found -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- No evidence found for a lead breeder's name.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or personal contact for this variety.
- Institute-level page only: AAU main website -- https://www.aau.in (the search did not return a verified AAU contact page; the Main Vegetable Research Station contact found belongs to a different station and was discarded).

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming GAR 22 (Swagat) was returned. Pages on GAR-13, GAR-14, GAR-2, Gujarat Rice 21 and Gujarat Aerobic Rice 201 were discarded as other varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales pages for this variety. The searches returned only unrelated rice traders and mill listings in Anand, which were discarded.
- Institute variety listing (not a seed-sales page) -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-29/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for the transplanted rice areas of middle Gujarat -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- The input record says "Gujarat". The AAU page is narrower (middle Gujarat), so the record should be checked.

RELEASE AND REGISTRATION (discrepancies to resolve)
- Year of release: AAU pages give 2021 (53rd SSSC) -- https://aau.in/variety_released. The input record gives 2022-06-17. These do not agree.
- Seednet name: No page found links "GUJARAT ANAND RICE-2 (IET-21614)" to GAR 22. The PPV&FR and Bihar notified-variety lists tie that name to GAR-2 (2011). The Seednet name in the input record should be checked against the portal. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumforextantnotified-nov-2021.pdf ; https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Variety code "GAR 22: Swagat": the AAU listing uses "Gujarat Anand Rice 22 (Swagat)", which supports the common name. No separate code source was found.

flood.details: Hasanta recorded a maximum reduction in agro-morphological and physiological traits under seven days of submergence stress, indicating low tolerance to submergence (a form of flood stress). Efforts are underway to pyramid submergence tolerance genes into this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Research is being conducted to pyramid three bacterial blight resistance genes into Hasanta through marker-assisted backcross breeding, suggesting the original variety may not possess sufficient resistance to bacterial blight.

pest_resistance.summary: Hasanta is mentioned as a paddy cultivar in studies evaluating resistance and susceptibility to rice root-knot nematode, but its specific reaction is not detailed.

agronomic_details.yield: Quantitative yield data for Hasanta is not specified, but it is studied in the context of optimizing resource use efficiency and weed management to mitigate yield loss.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield stability across environments using AMMI and GGE biplot tools has been evaluated for other lowland rice genotypes, but specific data for Hasanta is not provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Odisha. Hasanta has been a test variety in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, in studies evaluating optimum transplanting dates and thermal requirements, suggesting adaptability to different planting windows and regions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Hasanta's agro-morphological and physiological traits have been assessed under submergence stress. It is also subject to biochemical characterization for straw lignocellulose.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Hasanta has been used in field trials concerning integrated nutrient management (INM) practices (e.g., Green Manure + 50% STBNR through inorganics), weed dynamics and management under resource-conserving planting modules (e.g., direct-seeded rice, wet-direct seeded rice), and evaluation of thermal requirements across different transplanting windows.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Genetic markers are actively utilized in marker-assisted backcross breeding for pyramiding submergence tolerance and three bacterial blight resistance genes into the Hasanta variety. Additionally, Hasanta is an elite rice variety characterized using SSR (Simple Sequence Repeat) markers for lignocellulose and genetic diversity assessment.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specified directly for Hasanta's inherent traits, but QTLs for submergence tolerance (e.g., Sub1 gene mentioned in context of other varieties like CR Dhan 801) are being introgressed.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Gene pyramiding for submergence tolerance and bacterial blight resistance.

drought.details: Identified as a rice variety recommended for areas prone to drought stress. It is listed among multiple stress tolerant varieties and has been screened for drought stress tolerance in AICRIP trials.

heat.details: Screened for high temperature tolerance. Included in agro-advisories for cultivation where managing terminal heat stress at the time of maturity is relevant.

salinity.details: Explicitly identified as a salt-tolerant variety. Recommended for cultivation in saline lands, including areas affected by events like YAAS.

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance was found in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: Reported as 'triple disease resistant' against bacterial wilt, early blight, and leaf curl virus. It has also been screened for resistance to Rice Tungro Disease.

pest_resistance.summary: No direct evidence of specific pest resistance was found for Hiranmayee in the provided results. It is mentioned in general advisories regarding pest management in rice.

Digest (AICRIP centre report): semi-dwarf, high-yielding, medium-duration variety with long flag leaf and long slender grain. Digest maturity figure of 145 days differs from the release record range of 135 to 140 days; both are reported here.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Transplanting date trial (academia.edu source, which names HKR-128): under late transplanting, HKR-128 showed about a 31% yield reduction compared with early transplanting on June 15, and it was statistically at par with HKR-127 in yield. (2) Hybrid rice IET/AICRIP-style trial table: HKR-128 appears only as a local check variety across Kaul (KUL) and other centres; check-variety role only, trial yield values not extracted. No other trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
HKR 128 rice: evidence digest

Name note: the CSC/variety_name is HKR 128. The Seednet name is HKR-126, which is a different, separately released Kaul variety. Every search result that names HKR-126 was therefore discarded for HKR 128. The findings below refer to HKR 128 unless marked otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for HKR 128. The only stress-tolerance statements retrieved (10-day water-stress tolerance, salinity responses) concern HKR-126 or other genotypes and were excluded. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for HKR 128. The Kaul AICRIP centre report describes HKR 126 as resistant to stem rot and WBPH and moderately resistant to bacterial blight, but this is not attributed to HKR 128. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
Discarded: "HKR 95-128" is a separate bacterial-blight-resistant genetic stock maintained by NBPGR, not this variety. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- HKR 128 is a semi-dwarf, high-yielding medium-duration variety with long flag leaf and long slender grain, maturing in 145 days, and was described as tested in farmers' fields and likely for general cultivation in Haryana. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
Under late transplanting, HKR-128 showed about a 31% yield reduction versus early transplanting (June 15), and it was statistically at par with HKR-127 in yield. -- https://www.academia.edu/35376988/Effects_of_different_dates_of_transplanting_on_yield_attributes_yields_and_quality_of_non_scented_varieties_of_rice_Oryza_sativa
HKR-128 appears as a local check variety in an IET/AICRIP-style hybrid rice trial table, with yield data across Kaul (KUL) and other centres. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf (check-variety role only; trial yield values not extracted)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for HKR 128. Parentage in the release record (NAMSAGNI 19 / IR-4215 / IR 5953 derived from IRRI F4 material, selected under artificial bacterial blight inoculation) was not corroborated by any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- HKR 128 was developed at Rice Research Station, Kaul (district Kaithal, Haryana), under Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
The Hisar university page lists HKR 128 among seven non-scented varieties released by the Kaul station. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
Lead breeder name for HKR 128: No evidence found. The retrieved pages name a "Rice Breeder & Head, RRS Kaul" without a name, and the names of other Kaul staff appear only in unrelated acknowledgments; none are attributed to HKR 128.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No individual breeder contact found. Institute-level information only:
Rice Research Station, Kaul, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Kaul 132021, India (address as printed on the Kaul station credit line). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8402606_Genetic_analysis_of_Indian_aromatic_and_quality_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_germplasm_using_panels_of_fluorescently-labeled_microsatellite_markers
Institute home page: https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
Station information PDF (infrastructure, campus details): https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1716344337.pdf
Email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Lavanya, A. and Pinky, B. (2019). Physical and Nutritional Quality Evaluation of Different Rice varieties (includes HKR-128 from RRS Kaul). International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences, 8(6) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-6-2019/A.%20Lavanya%20and%20Boora%20Pinky.pdf
Author(s) not retrieved (year not retrieved). Effects of different dates of transplanting on yield attributes, yields and quality of non-scented varieties of rice (Oryza sativa L.). Journal not retrieved -- https://www.academia.edu/35376988/Effects_of_different_dates_of_transplanting_on_yield_attributes_yields_and_quality_of_non_scented_varieties_of_rice_Oryza_sativa
Author(s) not retrieved (year not retrieved). Kaul Rice Research Station centre report, AICRIP (HKR 128 release description). -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
Excluded: the HKR-126 callus regeneration paper (Callus induction and efficient regeneration from recalcitrant of indica rice varieties) concerns HKR-126 and HKR-120, not HKR 128. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316503793_Callus_induction_and_efficient_regeneration_from_recalcitrant_of_indica_rice_varieties

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for HKR 128 or HKR-126 from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or Seednet. The retrieved listings are for PR 126 (a PAU variety, different crop variety) or Hasco/Hari branded products and were discarded. Searched once with the HKR-126 and Haryana terms. Recommend checking the CCSHAU Rice Research Station seed sales and the Seednet portal directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Haryana, with an HAU statement that HKR 128 occupied substantial area in Haryana and other North Indian states. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
Release status is unclear: the AICRIP centre report says HKR 128 was likely to be released for general cultivation in the state, and the release year in the record (2019) was not confirmed by any retrieved source. HKR-126 appears in a Haryana notified-paddy list (2022), but HKR 128 was not seen on that list. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-haryana/
