search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: CSC release name HKR 127 (variety code HKR 95-222). Seednet name HKR-126. The evidence below for HKR 127 refers to HKR 127. HKR-126 is a separate Kaul release, so its records apply only to HKR-126. I did not find evidence that the Seednet entry "HKR-126" refers to HKR 127.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- HKR 127 is reported to show weak endurance against bacterial blight, though farmers value its yield and cooking quality in Haryana -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343049563_Evaluation_of_resistance_of_rice_genotypes_derived_from_the_cross_be-_tween_HKR-127_and_IRBB-60_against_bacterial_blight_caused_by_Xanthomonas_oryzae_pv_oryzae
- In a salinity biplot analysis, HKR 127 was among the genotypes favoured for salt tolerance (MP, GMP, STI and yield). The text does not give a salinity score. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361442656_Development_of_Salt-Tolerant_Rice_Varieties_to_Enhancing_Productivity_in_Salt-Affected_Environments
- No drought, heat, flood or submergence data for HKR 127 found in the searches. The "10 days of water stress" result refers to HKR 126, not HKR 127 -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf (not applicable to HKR 127)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight: HKR 127 has less endurance to BB. Breeding lines from an HKR-127 x IRBB-60 cross carrying Xa21, xa13 and xa5 showed lower lesion length, with the three-gene lines most resistant -- https://sajeb.org/index.php/sajeb/article/view/352
- Blast, brown planthopper, stem rot and stem borer ratings for HKR 127 were not found. Stem rot and WBPH resistance in the Kaul station notes apply to HKR 126 -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf (HKR 126 only)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration: mid-early, 135-139 days, with long slender super-fine grain, stiff straw and disease resistance claimed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316503793_Callus_induction_and_efficient_regeneration_from_recalcitrant_of_indica_rice_varieties
- Morphology: semi-dwarf, high yielding, golden yellow grains, high milling recovery -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- Early maturity was presented as a way to shorten the gap before wheat sowing and reduce straw burning -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/comment/the-paddy-straw-challenge-613982
- No yield figures (t/ha) for HKR 127 found in the searches. No multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from the record supplied, not confirmed by search): NAMSAGNI 19/IR-4215-301-2-2-6 x IR 5953-162-1-2-3, selected from an F4 IRRI segregating population under artificial BB inoculation. No independent source found.
- Marker-assisted pyramiding of Xa21, xa13 and xa5 in HKR-127 backgrounds was reported at CCS HAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343049563_Evaluation_of_resistance_of_rice_genotypes_derived_from_the_cross_be-_tween_HKR-127_and_IRBB-60_against_bacterial_blight_caused_by_Xanthomonas_oryzae_pv_oryzae
- No QTL or marker-mapping study specific to HKR 127 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: KAUL Rice Research Station, Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Kaul, Kaithal, Haryana. The station was established in 1974 -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- A GK source credits HKR 127 to the KAUL Rice Research Station, Haryana Agricultural University -- https://www.gktoday.in/question/terms-mtu1010-swarna-naveen-hkr127-pertain-to
- The HAU page lists HKR 127 among seven non-scented varieties released by the Haryana rice station -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
- Lead breeder name(s): not found in any retrieved source.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23 (no email, phone or street address in the retrieved text)
- KAUL Rice Research Station, district Kaithal, Haryana. No email, phone or postal address found in the retrieved text -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Mehta K (2019). Evaluation of resistance of rice genotypes (derived from the cross between HKR-127 and IRBB-60) against bacterial blight caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. South Asian Journal of Experimental Biology 9(4):142-147 -- DOI 10.38150/sajeb.9(4).p142-147; https://sajeb.org/index.php/sajeb/article/view/352 (only first author visible in retrieved record)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Callus induction and efficient regeneration from recalcitrant indica rice varieties, including HKR-127 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316503793_Callus_induction_and_efficient_regeneration_from_recalcitrant_of_indica_rice_varieties
- Prasad, G.S.V. et al. (2022). Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India. Journal not confirmed in retrieved record -- DOI 10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2; https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2 (HKR 127 listed among inbred cultivars; only one author confirmed)
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found (not searched directly; the search tool did not return KrishiKosh records).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Notified in the list of notified rice varieties: HKR-127 (HKR-95-222), year 2009, notification 29/01/2010, S.O. 211(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Breeder seed multiplication for HKR 127 is covered in the national seed distribution study above. No current seed dealer, NSC, SSC or KVK listing for HKR 127 found. The Indiamart results are for PR 126 (a Punjab PAU variety), not HKR 127 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pr-126-paddy-seed-20406304873.html (not HKR 127)
- Seednet portal listing: not retrieved. Check seednet.gov.in directly under "HKR-126" and "HKR-127" to confirm.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Haryana (recorded in the input). HKR 127 is widely grown in Haryana, per the Mehta 2019 abstract above -- https://sajeb.org/index.php/sajeb/article/view/352
- Recommendation for other states: No evidence found.
- Release year in the input is NaT. The notification list gives 2009 (notification 29/01/2010) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

agronomic_details.adaptation: HKR 49: Suitable for direct-seeded aerobic conditions in the Kaul trial (2019 and 2020), where it was early duration. Recommended states per release data: Odisha, Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat. HKR-47 (not HKR-49): suitable for early and late planting (Kaul source); suitable for parboiling (PAU event page); among the most suitable genotypes under alternate wetting and drying in puddled direct-sown conditions (Kaul source); popular in Haryana for high yield and medium slender grains with excellent cooking and eating qualities.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: HKR 49: Not specified in the digest, though it is described as an early-duration cultivar under direct-seeded aerobic conditions. HKR-47 (not HKR-49): about 104 days to maturity after transplanting.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: HKR 49: Not specified in the digest, other than early duration. HKR-47 (not HKR-49): average plant height of 117 cm; medium slender grains; prone to lodging (PAU source).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) HKR 49, direct-seeded aerobic conditions at Kaul, 2019 and 2020: highest water use efficiency of 7.74 kg/ha/mm; early-duration cultivar; highest net returns of Rs 84,963/ha. (2) HKR-47, transplanting-date trial at Kaul: 63.82 q/ha, ranked behind HKR-128 and HKR-127; the source gives no HKR-49 data. (3) HKR-47, Kaul plant pathology reports: minimum yield loss of 22.62% when inoculated at 30 DAT (pathogen not named). (4) HKR-47, evaluation of duration genotypes under alternate wetting and drying in puddled direct-sown conditions: HKR 47 among the most suitable genotypes, along with hybrid HKR 1094 and hybrid Haryana Shankar Dhan 1.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- HKR-47 (Seednet name): It is tolerant to false smut and suitable for early and late planting. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- HKR-47: It is susceptible to all the ten presently prevalent pathotypes of bacterial blight pathogen in the Punjab state and is prone to lodging. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- HKR-49 (variety_name): The highest water use efficiency (7.74 kg/ha/mm) was achieved with HKR 49. Tested under direct-seeded aerobic conditions at Kaul in 2019 and 2020 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/149739
- HKR-49: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance beyond the water-use result above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- HKR-47: Kaul plant pathology reports the minimum yield loss of HKR 47 (22.62%) when inoculated at 30 DAT, with the pathogen not named in the retrieved text -- https://hau.academia.edu/Departments/Plant_Pathology_Rice_Research_Station_Kaul_136021_Haryana/Documents
- HKR-47: popular amongst rice farmers and consumers in Haryana because of its high yield, medium slender grains, and excellent cooking and eating qualities, though the source notes a weakness that the snippet does not state -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336317940_Evaluation_of_Resistance_of_Rice_Genotypes_Derived_from_the_Cross_between_HKR-47_and_IRBB-60_against_Bacterial_Blight_caused_by_Xanthomonas_oryzae_pv_oryzae
- HKR-49: No evidence found for disease or pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- HKR-49: Under direct-seeded aerobic conditions HKR 49 was an early-duration cultivar, and HKR 49 fetching the highest net returns (₹84,963/ha) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/149739
- HKR-47: HKR-47 (63.82 q/ha) ranked behind HKR-128 and HKR-127 in a transplanting-date trial at Kaul; the source gives no HKR-49 data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326605987_Effects_of_different_dates_of_transplanting_on_yield_attributes_yields_and_quality_of_non-scented_varieties_of_rice_Oryza_sativa
- HKR-47: It takes about 104 days to mature after transplanting with an average plant height of 117 cm. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- HKR-47: Its' average paddy yield is 29.5 quintals per acre. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- HKR-47: It is suitable for parboiling. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5025
- HKR-47: Evaluation of different duration genotypes under alternate wetting and drying in puddled direct sown conditions revealed that hybrid HKR 1094; inbred HKR 47 and hybrid Haryana Shankar Dhan 1 were found most suitable. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- HKR-47 (Seednet name): HKR47, a low-land high yielding indica rice variety unadapted to cultivation in aerobic conditions (used as female) and MAS26, an aerobic rice variety (used as male) were selected as parents to develop mapping populations -- https://d-nb.info/1218930675/34

drought.details: The krishdoctor product page reports partial water-stress tolerance and good performance under moisture stress for Arize Tej Gold. The level is set to medium because the tolerance is described as partial and no trial data was found. A seller page (sandia-agric.com) makes drought claims only for 'Arize hybrids' in general; these are not variety-specific and were not used to set the level.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183.

salinity.details: No variety-specific salinity evidence found. A seller page lists 'moderate salinity' tolerance only as a generic claim about Arize hybrids, not trial data for this variety. No formal salinity screening data was found for HRI-180 or HRI-183.

flood.details: Bayer's brochure makes a brand-level flash-flood tolerance claim that is not specific to Tej Gold. A seller page makes a generic flash-flood claim for Arize hybrids. Neither is variety-specific, so no level is assigned.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB): the krishdoctor page describes Arize Tej Gold as 'resistant to BLB' in one place and 'tolerant' in its description, so the strength of resistance is unclear. Bayer's brochure lists BLB tolerance for Tej Gold and Swift Gold (Swift Gold is the Seednet name HRI-183). No evidence found for blast or sheath blight resistance specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence found for brown planthopper or other pest resistance specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183. The brown planthopper-tolerant hybrid mentioned in Bayer's brochure is Arize AZ 8433 DT, a different product, and was excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Sources conflict and none is a verified trial figure. A seller page gives 8-9 t/ha as a marketing figure. The Krishak Jagat hybrid list gives an unlabelled figure of 7.0 in the same row as the duration entry, which is likely yield in t/ha but is not confirmed. The input record lists average_yield as 'Kg/Ha' with no value.

agronomic_details.field_trials: One trial found: a Nepal multi-hybrid evaluation (Lumbini Province) under irrigated transplanting that includes Arize Tej Gold among compared hybrids. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) resistance is listed for Arize Tej Gold, and the page also reports partial water-stress tolerance and good performance under moisture stress -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold / HRI-180)
- Bayer's Arize brand document lists Tej Gold among varieties with BLB tolerance, and says many Arize varieties tolerate biotic stress and suit direct seeding. Bayer's brand-level claim about flash-flood tolerance is not specific to Tej Gold -- https://www.bayer.in/sites/bayer_in/files/Bayer_25_Years_of_Arize_English_2019_0.pdf (name searched: Arize Tej Gold; the same brochure also lists Swift Gold, i.e. the Seednet name HRI-183)
- Drought, salinity and flood claims on a seller page are generic statements about "Arize hybrids", not trial data for this variety: temporary drought, moderate salinity, flash floods -- https://sandia-agric.com/product-818-1.html (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- No evidence found for heat, submergence, or formal drought/salinity screening data specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183.

DISEASE AND PEST
- BLB tolerance/resistance: the krishdoctor page calls it "resistant to BLB" in one place and "tolerant" in its description, so the strength of resistance is unclear -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- BLB tolerance listed in Bayer's brochure for Tej Gold and Swift Gold -- https://www.bayer.in/sites/bayer_in/files/Bayer_25_Years_of_Arize_English_2019_0.pdf (name searched: Arize Tej Gold / Swift Gold)
- Bayer's brochure also mentions a brown planthopper-tolerant hybrid, but that is Arize AZ 8433 DT, not this variety -- excluded.
- No evidence found for blast, sheath blight, brown planthopper or other pest resistance specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 125-130 days -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Duration 125-130 days, with an unlabelled figure of 7.0 in the same row. The figure is likely yield in t/ha, but the column is not labelled -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/ (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- A seller page gives maturity of 110-120 days and yield of 8-9 t/ha. This is a marketing figure and conflicts with the 125-130 day figure above -- https://sandia-agric.com/product-818-1.html (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Bayer product page lists long slender grain, high yield, more productive tillers and fine grain with good eating quality -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/seed-products/arize-tej-gold/212799 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Milling recovery above 70% and long slender grain -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Nepal multi-hybrid trial (Lumbini Province) includes Arize tej Gold among hybrids compared under irrigated transplanting. The numeric columns are unlabelled in the snippet, so no yield is attributed here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387415927_Evaluation_of_hybrid_rice_varieties_for_growth_and_yield_traits_under_irrigated_transplanted_conditions_in_Lumbini_Province_Nepal (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- No evidence found for AICRP/ICAR multi-location trial results or Indian yield data for HRI-180 or HRI-183.
- Excluded: a retailer page (mtolori.com) describing "Arize Tej Gold" as semi-dwarf and lodging-resistant, because its product title and listing refer to Arize 6444 Gold.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage was not stated in the sources (matches the input "Not specified"). No QTL, marker, or CMS/restorer details were found for HRI-180 or HRI-183.
- Excluded: the IntechOpen rice-breeding chapter gives development details for Arize Tej (HRI 169), a different variety -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Notified by Government of India and marketed by Bayer Crop Science -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Bayer Crop Science listed as the company for the Tej Gold row in the hybrid list -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/ (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Bayer introduced hybrid rice in India in 1995 under the Arize brand. This is brand-level background, not variety-specific -- https://www.bayer.in/sites/bayer_in/files/Bayer_25_Years_of_Arize_English_2019_0.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name for HRI-180 or HRI-183 was found in any result. Excluded: a LinkedIn profile of a hybrid-rice consultant lists Arize products generically, not as breeder of this variety -- https://www.linkedin.com/in/ish-kumar-82449b16a/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- No email, phone or postal address for Bayer's rice seed division was found in the search results.
- Only institute-level product page found (not a contact page): Bayer Crop Science India, Arize Tej Gold product page -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/seed-products/arize-tej-gold/212799 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Seednet (seednet.gov.in) was not returned by any search, so no Seednet contact or variety record was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183 was found.
- Only item found: Nepal hybrid evaluation that names Arize tej Gold. Authors and year were not captured from the snippet, and no journal is confirmed -- Authors not captured (Year not captured). Evaluation of hybrid rice varieties for growth and yield traits under irrigated transplanted conditions in Lumbini Province, Nepal. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387415927_Evaluation_of_hybrid_rice_varieties_for_growth_and_yield_traits_under_irrigated_transplanted_conditions_in_Lumbini_Province_Nepal
- Excluded: Golden Rice and Arize Bigante papers (different varieties/products).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Bayer product page lists Arize Tej Gold in 1 kg and 3 kg packs -

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for HRI-183 or Arize Swift Gold. The only retrieved rice pages on stress tolerance concerned other varieties, such as the IIRR entries IET-27530 and CR Dhan 411, and were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page named HRI-183 or Arize Swift Gold together with disease or pest resistance. Results about bacterial blight and blast referred to other entries and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for maturity, yield, or multi-location trials for HRI-183. The retailer pages (seedlelo, IndiaMart, Amazon, R K Traders) describe Arize 6444 Gold, Arize 6129 Gold, or unnamed "Arize" hybrids, so they were discarded as different products. Only the seedlelo page for "Arize Swift Gold" mentions yield in general terms (see SEED AVAILABILITY), and it gives no figures.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker, or QTL information was retrieved. The variety's parentage is recorded as "Not specified" in the input, and no source filled that gap.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found for a named breeder or scientist for HRI-183. The only institutional link retrieved is the input's "Bayer Bio Science Pvt Ltd" as the institution. The notification entry (below) does not name a breeder, and the Seednet portal and CSC minutes were not reached.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, Bayer division, postal address, email, phone, or institute contact page for HRI-183 was returned. The Bayer-branded pages that appeared (Amazon, IndiaMart) list product or dealer details for other Arize products, not for the developing division, so they were not used.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming HRI-183 or Arize Swift Gold was retrieved. The IIRR Annual Report 2023 (https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf) and the ICAR-CRRI variety list (https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf) were returned, but neither names HRI-183.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Bayer Arize Swift Gold Hybrid Rice Seed, 3 kg, listed at ₹1,200 with "Availability: 1", described as a hybrid paddy seed for kharif season -- https://www.seedlelo.com/index.php?route=product%2Fproduct&product_id=1675
This is a private retailer listing under the seednet_variety_name alias "Arize Swift Gold". It does not give the code HRI-183, so it is weak evidence of identity. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or Seednet availability record was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
HRI-183 ((Arize Swift Gold) (IET24082), notified by S.O. 1007(E) dated 30.03.2017: Haryana, Uttrakhand, Uttar Pradesh & Gujrat -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Note: this notification is dated 2017, whereas the input's year_of_release is 2016-08-12. The page is a state-level notified-varieties list, not the CSC release minutes, so the discrepancy is unresolved. The list also spells "Uttrakhand" and "Gujrat" as shown above.

drought.details: HUR-1304 is described as a short duration drought tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Furthermore, it has been utilized as a parental line (IR97443-11-2-1-1-1-1-B * HUR-1304) in Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) breeding programs to develop varieties with multiple abiotic stress tolerance, including drought tolerance.

heat.details: No direct information available regarding HUR-1304's specific tolerance to heat stress.

salinity.details: HUR-1304 (Malviya Dhaan 1304) is listed among varieties described as salt tolerant in proceedings of the Annual Rice Research Group Meeting.

flood.details: No direct information available regarding HUR-1304's specific tolerance to general flood conditions, though it contributes to submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: HUR-1304 is moderately resistant to rice blast, neck blast, and bacterial leaf blight disease. It is generally described as a disease-resistant paddy variety.

pest_resistance.summary: While not explicitly stated for HUR-1304 itself, a breeding product using HUR-1304 as a parent (IR97443-11-2-1-1-1-1-B * HUR-1304) is reported to be resistant/tolerant against brown plant hopper, stem borer, and leaf folder, suggesting HUR-1304 contributes to these resistances.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: IGKVR-1 (rice, IET 19569)**

**Search status:** Three web searches completed. The tool limit was reached before the fourth (seed availability) search ran, and a follow-up search was blocked, so coverage is partial. Only search snippets were reviewed, not full documents. Variety name and Seednet name are both "IGKVR-1", so all evidence refers to the same name. No Seednet portal record was retrieved.

**STRESS TOLERANCE:** The ICAR Crop Improvement report (2011-12) lists IGKVR-1 among six varieties in a group, but the snippet does not show its tolerance profile. Stress claims are unverified. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf

**DISEASE AND PEST:** No evidence found in the retrieved results (search limit reached; not verified).

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:** The same ICAR 2011-12 report mentions IGKVR-1 alongside other entries in a varietal group, which suggests it was part of a trial or notification listing. The snippet gives no yield, maturity, or location data. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf

**GENETICS AND QTL:** No evidence found in the retrieved results (search limit reached; not verified).

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:** The AICRIP centre profile for Raipur Rice Research Station, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), describes the station's germplasm evaluation work. The snippet does not name IGKVR-1 or its breeder, so the link to IGKV is inferred from the variety prefix, not confirmed. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
A 2023 IGKV breeding-modernization paper was returned, but its snippet does not mention IGKVR-1. -- https://zenodo.org/records/10398607

**CONTACT DETAILS:** No breeder name, email, phone, or address was found. Institute-level contact should be taken from the IGKV website (not retrieved in this session). No official contact page URL was verified.

**PUBLICATIONS:**
- ICAR Crop Improvement Annual Report 2011-12 (Crop Improvement chapter). Mentions IGKVR-1 in a varietal listing. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Authors not stated (n.d.). AICRIP Raipur Rice Research Station centre profile. Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
- IGKV breeding modernization paper (2023), International Rice Congress 2023. Authors not verified. -- https://zenodo.org/records/10398607

**SEED AVAILABILITY:** Not searched because the tool limit was reached. No evidence found.

**RECOMMENDED STATES:** The ICAR report snippet does not confirm the release states. The record's listing of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, and Orissa (Odisha) is unverified against an official notification. Note that the IGKV Raipur station is in Chhattisgarh, which is consistent with the listing but does not confirm it.

**Gaps to close:** Release year (2010, from the record) is unverified. Parentage is unknown. Recommend re-running the stress, research, and seed searches, and checking the Seednet portal and the CSC release minutes directly.

drought.details: Described as 'drought tolerant' and suitable for 'direct sown rainfed condition'. It is noted to be capable of 'escaping terminal drought'. However, under severe stress, it may require 'protective life saving'.

heat.details: Exhibits 'heat stress tolerance' and is 'tolerant to terminal heat stress', capable of 'escaping terminal heat stresses'.

salinity.details: Improved Chinnor has been identified as tolerant to salinity and included in screening for 'Salinity Tolerance in Rice'.

flood.details: Described as a 'flood tolerant rice variety' with 150 days duration.

disease_resistance.summary: Improved Chinnor exhibited tolerance to bacterial blight and false smut. It is also resistant to neck blast disease and rice tungro rice disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Improved Chinnor exhibited tolerance to Gall midge and is resistant to stem borer.

agronomic_details.yield: Various yield values have been reported in different trials, including: 2.40, 9.00, 6.60; 1.00, 9.52, 8.52; 7.60, 13.50, 5.90; and 2.75, 46.71, 43.96.
agronomic_details.stability: Its documented tolerance to multiple abiotic and biotic stresses (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, gall midge, blast, bacterial blight, false smut, stem borer, tungro) suggests a degree of adaptability and stability across varying environmental conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Primarily suitable for irrigated conditions, but also mentioned as suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions due to its drought tolerance. It is classified as a Non-Basmati type.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: The variety is semi-dwarf, reaching a height of approximately 82 cm. It produces medium slender, aromatic grains (LS).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Agronomic performance data has been presented in Draft Proceedings of the Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM) and through Frontline Demonstrations (FLD).

EVIDENCE DIGEST: JGL 11118 (Anjana), rice

Name note: The CSC name is "JGL 11118" and the Seednet name is "JGL-11118". My searches returned evidence under the JGL-11118 / Anjana form in most sources. The Seednet portal itself was not reachable through search, so no Seednet record was retrieved. The release year in the input (2013-01-18) conflicts with the 2012 year in the ICAR-IIRR newsletter. I did not resolve that conflict.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The ICAR-IIRR newsletter lists Anjana (JGL 11118) with salient features of gall midge resistance and tolerance to bacterial leaf blight and cold -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to this variety was found in the searches -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST -- Gall midge resistance and BLB tolerance are listed in the IIRR newsletter (above) -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- In a rice weevil (Sitophilus oryzae) preference study, JGL 11118 recorded high adult emergence (index 17.33), which indicates susceptibility to this stored-grain pest -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346675746_Varietal_preference_of_different_rice_genotypes_by_rice_weevil_Sitophilus_oryzae_L

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Duration is listed as 115-135 days in the IIRR newsletter -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Sensory and organoleptic evaluation found Anjana (JGL-11118) scored high on all sensory attributes relative to Pradhyumna (JGL-17004) -- https://www.academia.edu/37083436/ORGANOLEPTIC_PROPERTIES_OF_SELECTED_NEWLY_RELEASED_RICE_VARIETIES_OF_NORTHERN_TELANGANA_REGION
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Milling quality and glycemic index were assessed for Anjana (JGL-11118) and Pradhyumna (JGL-17004) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=3420&vol=6-7-2017&SNo=446 and https://www.ijcmas.com/6-9-2017/R.%20Anitha2,%20et%20al.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield data for this variety: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL -- JGL 11118 is listed among early-maturing genotypes in a diversity and maternal-lineage study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301588915_Genetic_diversity_and_maternal_lineage_among_early_maturing_genotypes_of_Indica_and_Japonica
GENETICS AND QTL -- JGL 11118 appears as a parent in MTU 7029/JGL 11118 crosses in a 2016 breeding and genetic divergence study -- http://www.sciencewebpublishing.net/jacr/archive/2016/December/pdf/Tejaswini%20et%20al.pdf
GENETICS AND QTL -- JGL 11118 is one of the varieties used for SSR/DUS DNA fingerprinting -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/13102818.2021.1987324

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance. The only related result is an aerobic-condition trial on Alfisols, in which JGL 11727 had the highest grain yield (3477 kg/ha) and the highest agronomic performance and stability among 10 genotypes. This shows performance under aerobic conditions but does not establish drought tolerance mechanisms.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: No resistance evidence found for blast, bacterial leaf blight (BLB) or brown spot for JGL 11727 itself. BLB work used a cross involving this line as a parent, which does not establish resistance in JGL 11727. A collaborative breeding study describes the variety as highly susceptible to lodging, pests and diseases, with lower germination, despite good grain quality. Overall disease reaction is therefore reported as susceptible in one source and otherwise unestablished.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge resistance, biotype 3, is recorded for JGL 11727 at the Rice Research Scheme, RARS Jagtial, and the variety is listed as 'resistant to gall midge' in an IIRR newsletter release table. The same collaborative breeding study describes high susceptibility to pests, which conflicts with the gall midge record and is not resolved in the digest. No evidence found for brown planthopper (BPH) or whitebacked planthopper (WBPH) reaction.

agronomic_details.yield: Aerobic trial on Alfisols (10 genotypes): 3477 kg/ha, the highest among entries. N-response trial (pre-release cultures): 5347 kg/ha, superior with JGL 13595 (5345 kg/ha). The release record's average_yield field gives the unit only (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Highest agronomic performance and stability among 10 genotypes in the aerobic trial. Heritability and genetic advance for grain yield and 1000-grain weight were reported as high in the same trial. Multi-location AICRP yield data: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Tested under aerobic conditions on Alfisols. Developed at RARS Jagtial (Polasa) and associated with northern Telangana through a socioeconomic adoption study. The CSC record lists Andhra Pradesh as the recommended state; the digest does not state recommended states directly.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Fine grain (release-table traits). Good grain quality (collaborative breeding study). Plant height, tiller number: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Aerobic trial on Alfisols, 10 genotypes: JGL 11727 gave the highest grain yield (3477 kg/ha) and the highest agronomic performance and stability. (2) N-response trial on pre-release cultures: JGL 11727 and JGL 13595 were superior, with yields of 5347 and 5345 kg/ha respectively. (3) Release-table traits: duration 135-140 days and fine grain. (4) Socioeconomic adoption study in northern Telangana (see publications). Plant height, tiller and maturity figures from the official release description: Not found in searched sources. Multi-location AICRP yield data: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JGL 11727 / JGL-11727 (Pranahitha), rice

Name note: The evidence uses "JGL 11727", "JGL-11727" and "Pranahitha" interchangeably. No result came from the Seednet portal itself, so the Seednet name is unverified. Everything below refers to the same variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Gall midge resistance, biotype 3, is recorded for JGL 11727 at the Rice Research Scheme, RARS Jagtial -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sreedhar-Siddi/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre/links/62fe0727ceb9764f7204ea59/Telangana-State-506-007-India-3-Rice-Research-Centre-7-Administrative-Office-8-Seed-Research-and-Technology-Centre.pdf
- Listed as "resistant to gall midge" in IIRR newsletter release table -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Susceptibility: described as highly susceptible to lodging, pests and diseases, with lower germination, despite good grain quality -- https://researchgate.net/publication/229364604_Collaborative_breeding_with_farmers_can_be_effective
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found (aerobic-condition trial only, see AGRONOMY)
- Disease resistance beyond gall midge (blast, BLB, BPH): No evidence found for JGL 11727 itself (BLB work used a cross involving it as a parent -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boddupalli-Srinivas)

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Gall midge resistance (see above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/401068001_KNM_1638_-_A_High_Yielding_Gall_Midge_Resistant_Early_Duration_PJTSAU_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L_Variety_Suitable_for_Telangana_State
- Lodging, pest and disease susceptibility (see STRESS TOLERANCE) -- https://researchgate.net/publication/229364604_Collaborative_breeding_with_farmers_can_be_effective
- Brown spot / blast reaction of JGL 11727: No evidence found
- BPH / WBPH reaction: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Release-table traits: duration 135-140 days, fine grain -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Aerobic trial on Alfisols, 10 genotypes: JGL 11727 had the highest grain yield (3477 kg/ha) and the highest agronomic performance and stability -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols
- N-response trial (pre-release cultures): JGL 11727 and JGL 13595 were superior, with yields of 5347 and 5345 kg/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Leaf-area-index-LAI-at-different-growth-stages-of-rice-cultivars-as-affected-by_tbl1_259972800
- Plant height, tiller and maturity figures from the official release description: No evidence found
- Multi-location AICRP yield data: No evidence found in retrieved text
- Socioeconomic adoption study (northern Telangana): see PUBLICATIONS

GENETICS AND QTL:
- Parent of KNM 1638 (cross JGL 11727 x JGL 17004, female parent, pedigree method) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/401068001_KNM_1638_-_A_High_Yielding_Gall_Midge_Resistant_Early_Duration_PJTSAU_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L_Variety_Suitable_for_Telangana_State
- Used as a parent in a 50-line breeding population (Pranahitha//ISM/MTU1010) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boddupalli-Srinivas
- Heritability and genetic advance for grain yield and 1000-grain weight reported high in the aerobic trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols
- Parentage of JGL 11727 itself: Not specified in the sources (the record's "Not specified" stands); No evidence found
- QTL / marker studies specific to JGL 11727: No evidence found
- Gall midge QTL / marker work in the IIRR 2023 report is general and not tied to this variety: https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developed at the Rice Research Scheme, Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Jagtial (Polasa), now under PJTSAU, Telangana -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sreedhar-Siddi/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre/links/62fe0727ceb9764f7204ea59/Telangana-State-506-007-India-3-Rice-Research-Centre-7-Administrative-Office-8-Seed-Research-and-Technology-Centre.pdf

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance in the digest. The Southern Zone saline-soil recommendation does not include JGL 17004, but the digest provides no drought mechanism or field evidence.

heat.details: No heat-stress evidence found in the digest. Cold tolerance is reported, but it is a low-temperature trait and is not evidence of heat tolerance: under cold stress the line recorded reasonably good spikelet fertility in some years because it escaped low temperatures. The digest also lists cold tolerance in the ICAR-IIRR newsletter table.

salinity.details: No evidence found. The saline-soil recommendation from the Southern Zone list does not include JGL 17004.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast tolerance: stated in the ICAR-IIRR newsletter table and in the Southern Zone 2015 kharif/rabi recommendations for rainfed areas (described with fine grain and suitability for contingency situations). Brown planthopper, bacterial blight and sheath blight: no evidence found for JGL 17004. Its listing in the BPH-prone category applies to other varieties in the same table.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge: released with resistance, described as multiple, and the line was selected for extra earliness. The female parent JGL 11727 carries gall midge biotype-3 resistance. Brown planthopper: no evidence found for JGL 17004.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. No quantitative yield in kg/ha was found in the retrieved text.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Sowing-date and aerobic simulation results exist, but no multi-environment stability statistics were reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed for rainfed areas in the Southern Zone 2015 kharif/rabi recommendations, with a note of fine grain and suitability for contingency situations. Developed at RARS Polasa, Jagtial, Telangana. Recommended state per variety data: Andhra Pradesh.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 95-120 days (ICAR-IIRR release table); 105 days in the Telangana sowing-date trial, where it was the extra-short-duration entry.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Short-statured, medium slender, non-lodging, with good quality. Selected for extra earliness.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Telangana sowing-date trials (PJTSAU Journal of Research, vol. 43 no. 12): JGL 17004 (105 days) was the extra-short-duration entry, compared with MTU 1010 (120 days) and JGL 11470 (135 days). Yield results: Not found in searched sources. (2) Aerobic irrigated sowing-window simulation with CERES-Rice, validated on kharif 2012-2013 data: simulated mean grain yield under variable sowing dates is shown in a ResearchGate figure; numeric values not found in the digest. (3) Recommended management from PJTSAU (Journal of Research 44-3): 40 kg/ha seed, 15 x 10 cm spacing, 140 N, 60 P2O5, 50 K2O kg/ha. (4) Southern Zone seed-rate guideline: 5-10 kg/ha for medium duration, 15-18 kg/ha for short duration, 12-15 kg/ha rabi. Farm-level yield in kg/ha: Not found in searched sources.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. The Sh-h linked markers are reported for shattering-related marker selection only; no gene function or pathway was reported for JGL 17004.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JGL 17004 (Prathyumna), rice

Name note: The evidence refers to "JGL 17004" (CSC/release name) and "JGL-17004 (Prathyumna)" (Seednet-style name). No search returned a seednet.gov.in page, so no Seednet-specific record was found. Searches used: 4 of 4.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released with resistance to gall midge, cold tolerance, and blast tolerance, per the ICAR-IIRR newsletter table -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Gall midge resistance is described as multiple, and the line was selected for extra earliness -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sreedhar-Siddi/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre/links/62fe0727ceb9764f7204ea59/Telangana-State-506-007-India-3-Rice-Research-Centre-7-Administrative-Office-8-Seed-Research-and-Technology-Centre.pdf
- Under cold stress, the line recorded reasonably good spikelet fertility in some years because it escaped low temperatures -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301589014_Genetic_diversity_and_molecular_characterization_of_rice_landraces_Oryza_sativa_L_using_drought_stress_linked_SSR_and_STS_markers
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, and submergence: No evidence found. The saline-soil recommendation from the Southern Zone list does not include JGL 17004 -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Gall midge resistance and blast tolerance (see IIRR newsletter above) -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Listed for rainfed areas in the Southern Zone 2015 kharif/rabi recommendations, with a note of fine grain and suitability for contingency situations; blast tolerance is stated -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf
- Brown planthopper, bacterial blight, sheath blight: No evidence found for JGL 17004. Its listing in the BPH-prone category applies to other varieties in the same table.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release table gives duration 95-120 days and a 2012 release year -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Plant is short-statured, medium slender, non-lodging, with good quality -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348382178_Development_for_Achieving_Sustainable_Development_Goals_orkan_Rice_Theme-I_Enhancing_rice_productivity_and_quality_IRCTM-1PP-155_KNM_1638_GALL_MIDGE_RESISTANT_EARLY_DURATION_RICE_ORYZA_SATIVA_L_GENOTY
- Under Telangana sowing-date trials, JGL 17004 (105 days) was the extra-short-duration entry, versus MTU 1010 (120 days) and JGL 11470 (135 days) -- https://pjtau.edu.in/files/publications/2025/Journal-of-Research-43-12.pdf
- Recommended management: 40 kg/ha seed, 15 x 10 cm spacing, and 140 N, 60 P2O5, 50 K2O kg/ha -- https://pjtau.edu.in/files/publications/2025/Journal-of-Research-44-3.pdf
- Seed rate in the Southern Zone table: 5-10 kg/ha for medium duration, 15-18 kg/ha for short duration, 12-15 kg/ha rabi -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf
- Aerobic irrigated sowing-window simulation with CERES-Rice (kharif 2012-2013 validation) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Simulated-mean-grain-yield-of-rice-variety-JGL-17004-under-variable-sowing-dates-in_fig2_300001110
- Farm-level yield in kg/ha: No evidence found in the retrieved text.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: JGL 17004 was used as the male parent in the cross JGL 11727 x JGL 17004 (pedigree method, RARS Jagtial, 2010-2011). The female parent JGL 11727 carries gall midge biotype-3 resistance -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sreedhar-Siddi/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre/links/62fe0727ceb9764f7204ea59/Telangana-State-506-007-India-3-Rice-Research-Centre-7-Administrative-Office-8-Seed-Research-and-Technology-Centre.pdf
- Marker-assisted backcross (MTU 1010/JGL 17004 BC2F2 populations, 2014-15): three markers linked to the Sh-h shattering gene were polymorphic between MTU 1010 and JGL 17004 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301589014_Genetic_diversity_and_molecular_characterization_of_rice_landraces_Oryza_sativa_L_using_drought_stress_linked_SSR_and_STS_markers
- Of 774 SSR markers, 137 were polymorphic between MTU 1010 and JGL 17004 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301588915_Genetic_diversity_and_maternal_lineage_among_early_maturing_genotypes_of_Indica_and_Japonica.
- DUS fingerprinting with 21 informative traits, which includes JGL 17004 -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/13102818.2021.1987324
- Parent of derived line KNM 1638 (see Publications): gall midge resistance transfer is reported as simple inheritance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing station: Rice Research Scheme, Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Polasa, Jagtial, Prof. Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU), Telangana -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre
- PPV&FR applicant: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjune2020signed.pdf

Laxman are authors of the RARS Jagtial studies that used JGL 17004; this does not establish them as its developers -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301589014_Genetic_diversity_and_molecular_characterization_of_rice_landraces_Oryza_sativa_L_using_drought_stress_linked_SSR_and_STS_markers
- Station history: Polasa, Jagtial was established in 1980 -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JGL 3828 (Manair Sona), rice

Name note: The CSC minutes name is JGL 3828 (Manair Sona). The Seednet name, JGL-384, is a different variety. In the sources below, JGL 384 is Polasa Prabha, released in 2002. The findings below refer to JGL 3828 unless marked otherwise. The Seednet entry looks like a name mismatch and should be checked on the portal. I ran four searches, which is the maximum allowed. I did not run a separate seed-availability or breeder-contact search, so those headings rest on what the four searches happened to return.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Gall midge resistance (moderate): KNM 1638, JGL 3828, and WGL 505 were found to be moderately resistant to gall midge incidence. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320088206_Screening_of_different_Rice_entries_against_Rice_Gall_Midge_Orseolia_oryzae_Wood-Mason
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The aerobic-condition study covers water regime, not drought tolerance as such. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Gall midge: Res gall midge, tolerant to rice tungro, fine grain is the IIRR entry for Manair Sona (JGL 3828), released 2009, 135-150 days. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Rice tungro tolerance: stated in the same IIRR table row as above. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Rice weevil (Sitophilus oryzae): the abstract shows JGL 3828 in a varietal-preference table, with a "moderately susceptible" label, but the table is garbled and I could not confirm the score. Treat as unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346675746_Varietal_preference_of_different_rice_genotypes_by_rice_weevil_Sitophilus_oryzae_L

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Duration 135-150 days and fine grain type, per IIRR table. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Aerobic-condition evaluation of 10 lowland genotypes, including JGL 3828, over 2007-2009 on Alfisols; the study reports variability, genetic divergence and stability, with JGL-3828 grouped in a cluster with JGL-384 and JGL-3844. Yield values for JGL 3828 are in a garbled table and not reliable enough to quote. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols
- Multi-season 42-genotype characterisation that includes JGL 3828 (maturity and trait contribution data). Figures are not cleanly legible, so no values are reported. -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025/vol7issue9/PartA/7-8-50-936.pdf
- Yield (t/ha): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL:
- Pedigree of JGL 3828 is given in a figure caption as one of ten lowland genotypes, but the pedigree text was not extracted. The brief "Samba Mahsuri/Kavya" parentage was not verified in any result. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Pedigree-and-special-characteristic-features-of-10-genotypes-selected-in-the-study_tbl1_286195470
- QTL, marker, or SSR studies specifically on JGL 3828: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- The IIRR newsletter lists Manair Sona (JGL 3828) among varieties developed and released by the Andhra Pradesh Rice Research Institute, Maruteru, ANGRAU. This is an institute-level attribution; no breeder named for JGL 3828. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- The "JGL" prefix is, by my own inference and not stated in these sources, associated with Jagtial. The PJTAU Rice Research Unit at Jagtial appears in its IPR page. This is unverified. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/ipr-research-wing/

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Institute: Andhra Pradesh Rice Research Institute and Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, ANGRAU, Andhra Pradesh (named in the newsletter; no postal address, phone or email found). -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Individual breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page URL: not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not extracted. Title: Genetic analysis of rice (Oryza sativa L.) genotypes under aerobic conditions on alfisols. Journal: not identified (ResearchGate record). Year: not extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols
- Authors not extracted. Title: Screening of different rice entries against rice gall midge, Orseolia oryzae (Wood-Mason). Journal: not identified. Year: not extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320088206_Screening_of_different_Rice_entries_against_Rice_Gall_Midge_Orseolia_oryzae_Wood-Mason
- Authors not extracted. Title: Varietal preference of different rice genotypes by rice weevil Sitophilus oryzae (L.). Journal: not identified. Year: not extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346675746_Varietal_preference_of_different_rice_genotypes_by_rice_weevil_Sitophilus_oryzae_L
- Authors not extracted. Title: Genetic diversity and maternal lineage among early maturing genotypes of Indica and Japonica. Journal: not identified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301588915_Genetic_diversity_and_maternal_lineage_among_early_maturing_genotypes_of_Indica_and_Japonica
- AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, DOIs: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No evidence found. Seed sources (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, ANGRAU sales, dealers) were not searched in a dedicated query.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Andhra Pradesh: the IIRR newsletter lists Manair Sona as a variety developed at the Maruteru station, which serves the Godavari zone. This supports an AP link but does not state a formal recommendation. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- A Bihar-hosted notified-varieties list gives JGL 3828 (Manair Sona), year 2007, notification date 10/09/2012, S.O. 2125(E). The release-year conflict is 2007 here versus 2009 in the IIRR table. The list's scope (central or state) is not stated. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Release year: unresolved between 2007 (notified list) and 2009 (IIRR table). The CSC minutes date is not in the record.

drought.details: No direct evidence found for drought tolerance in JGL 3855 (or JGL-384). The CSC stress_reaction field reads 'NONE'. The digest's stress note states no direct evidence for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in either name. The low-temperature stress observation in the digest refers to JGL-384 (Polasa Prabha), not JGL 3855, and is excluded here.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in JGL 3855. The digest's low-temperature observation at Jagtial concerns JGL-384 under late sowing and is not attributed to JGL 3855, so it is not used as evidence here.

salinity.details: No direct evidence found for salinity tolerance in either name. CSC stress_reaction field reads 'NONE'.

flood.details: No direct evidence found for flood tolerance in either name.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: listed as tolerant for JGL 3855 in the IIRR 2015 release table (super-fine grain, 135-140 days). The Telangana Sona source describes JGL 3855 as tolerant to blast when it served as a parent of Telangana Sona. No evidence found for bacterial leaf blight, tungro or other diseases of JGL 3855. CSC disease_reaction field reads 'Not Specified'. Note: the JGL-384 (Polasa Prabha) records are not attributed to JGL 3855 and are excluded.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge: listed as resistant for JGL 3855 in the IIRR 2015 release table; the Telangana Sona source describes it as tolerant to gall midge when used as a parent. Yellow stem borer: JGL 3855 was the test variety in a Polasa rabi 2014-15 and 2015-16 insecticide trial; the paper reports chlorantraniliprole and related products as most effective but gives no resistance score for JGL 3855. No evidence found for BPH, BLB-vector response, tungro vector response or panicle mite reaction of JGL 3855. CSC pest_reaction field reads 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC average yield: 5440.00 to 6229.00 Kg/Ha. Trial data: about 7054 kg/ha in rabi 2007-08 at Jagtial under four nitrogen levels (highest in that season); 7054 kg/ha reported in a separate organic-production comparison. Trial yields exceed the CSC average range; trial conditions and replication details are not captured in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Only one season-level comparison is documented per trial; no multi-environment stability analysis was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC: for irrigated areas of Northern Telangana zones of Andhra Pradesh. Digest also describes JGL 3855 as a popular Telangana paddy variety in rabi seasons. Developed at RARS Polasa, Jagtial, Karimnagar district. Agro-climatic fit beyond these statements not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SEMI-DWARF, PROFUSE TILLERING, ERECT FLAG LEAF, COMPACT PANICLE, MEDIUM SLENDER GRAINS LIKE THAT OF BPT-5204. CSC agronomic features: NON-LODGING, NON SHATTERING, FERTILIZER RESPONSIVE. IIRR 2015 table lists super-fine grain. Plant height not found in the digest for JGL 3855. Duration conflict: IIRR 2015 lists 135-140 days versus CSC 150-165 days; this should be verified before use.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Jagtial kharif and rabi 2007-08 nitrogen-level trial under four N levels: about 7054 kg/ha in rabi 2007-08, highest in that season. (2) Organic-production comparison: 7054 kg/ha, higher than other varieties compared. (3) Kharif 2008 nitrogen study: superior N uptake, reported alongside JGL 11470. (4) Polasa insecticide trial against yellow stem borer, rabi 2014-15 and 2015-16: JGL 3855 used as test variety; no resistance score reported. (5) Hayman diallel parent table: days to 50% flowering given as 24.71, flagged in the digest as inconsistent with a 135-140 day variety and requiring checking. (6) Aerobic genetic study (2014): reports parentage for sister line JGL-3844 only; does not confirm JGL 3855 results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: SSR markers RM 12398, RM18704, RM25661 and RM 19697 distinguish JGL 3855 from other Telangana varieties in a DNA fingerprinting study. These are fingerprinting markers; chromosomal positions were not found in the digest. Phenotypic marker: anthocyanin colouration of the auricle distinguishes JGL 3855 from several varieties.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL mapping study for JGL 3855 found. Diallel analysis (Hayman approach) suggested more dominant genes controlling days to 50% flowering in JGL 3855 than in other parents; no QTL effects quantified in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME CHECK -- The CSC variety_name JGL 3855 (Karimnagar Samba, released 2010) and the Seednet name JGL-384 (Polasa Prabha, released 2002) are different varieties. Each line below says which name its evidence refers to. No source found for JGL-384 confirms the parentage given for JGL 3855. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
[JGL 3855] Listed as resistant to gall midge and tolerant to blast, with super-fine grain and 135-140 days duration. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
[JGL 3855] Described as tolerant to blast and gall midge when it served as a parent of Telangana Sona. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365717035_Telangana_sona_RNR_15048_a_short_duration_low_glycemic_super_fine_grain_high_yielding_rice_variety
[JGL-384 / Polasa Prabha, not JGL 3855] Listed as gall midge resistant with fine grain, 135-150 days. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
[JGL-384, not JGL 3855] Showed resistance to gall midge in a Kharif 2017 Polasa trial, used as a resistant check. -- https://ijpab.com/articles/IJPAB-2018-6-4-712-724.pdf
[JGL-384, not JGL 3855] Under low-temperature stress at Jagtial, JGL 384 gave high grain yield under late sowing. -- http://researchjournal.co.in/upload/assignments/6_415-417.pdf
No direct evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
[JGL 3855] Gall midge resistance and blast tolerance are listed in the IIRR release table. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
[JGL 3855] Used as the test variety in a Polasa field trial of insecticides against yellow stem borer in rabi 2014-15 and 2015-16; the paper reports chlorantraniliprole and related products as most effective, but gives no JGL 3855 resistance score. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344626532_Comparative_efficacy_of_some_new_insecticides_against_rice_yellow_stem_borer_Scirpophaga_incertulas_Walker_under_field_conditions
[JGL-384, not JGL 3855] Gall midge resistance recorded in a Jagtial screening (see Stress Tolerance). -- https://ijpab.com/articles/IJPAB-2018-6-4-712-724.pdf
No evidence found for BPH, BLB, tungro or panicle mite reaction of JGL 3855 specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[JGL 3855] In Jagtial trials from kharif and rabi 2007-08, the variety gave grain yield of about 7054 kg/ha in rabi 2007-08, the highest in that season, under four nitrogen levels. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324587038_Production_Potential_of_Rice_Oryza_Sativa_L_Varieties_under_Different_Nitrogen_Levels
[JGL 3855] A separate organic-production comparison reported JGL-3855 yielding 7054 kg/ha, higher than other varieties. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5291
[JGL 3855] Recorded superior N uptake in kharif 2008 alongside JGL 11470. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324587038_Production_Potential_of_Rice_Oryza_Sativa_L_Varieties_under_Different_Nitrogen_Levels
[JGL 3855] Described as a popular Telangana paddy variety in rabi seasons. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344626532_Comparative_efficacy_of_some_new_insecticides_against_rice_yellow_stem_borer_Scirpophaga_incertulas_Walker_under_field_conditions
[JGL-384, not JGL 3855] Recorded 60% head rice recovery in a 2013 Rajendranagar grain quality study of 25 genotypes. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/files/publications/2025/Journal-of-Research-43-12.pdf
Plant height, duration and days to flowering for JGL 3855 are in the Hayman diallel parent table (days to 50% flowering 24.71 in that table, which looks inconsistent with a 135-140 day variety and should be checked). -- https://arrworyza.com/AdminPanel/download/Genetic%20studies%20of%20quantitative%20traits%20through%20Hayman%E2%80%99s%20approach%20in%20rice.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
[JGL 3855] Distinguished from other Telangana varieties by unique SSR markers RM 12398, RM18704, RM25661 and RM 19697 in a DNA fingerprinting study. -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/13102818.2021.1987324
[JGL 3855] Anthocyanin colouration of the auricle distinguishes it from several varieties. -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/13102818.2021.1987324
[JGL 3855] Diallel analysis suggested more dominant genes for days to 50% flowering in JGL 3855 than in other parents. -- https://arrworyza.com/AdminPanel/download/Genetic%20studies%20of%20quantitative%20traits%20through%20Hayman%E2%80%99s%20approach%20in%20rice.pdf
No QTL mapping study for JGL 3855 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
[JGL 3855] Developed at Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Polasa, Jagtial, Karimnagar district, now under Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU); the same station's 2015 newsletter lists it as Karimnagar Sambha (JGL 3855). -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
[JGL 3855] Developed at RARS Jagtial as a derivative in the Samba Mahsuri lineage; no breeder name is explicitly tied to this variety in the sources. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols
[JGL 3855] Station scientists listed in the 2015 newsletter (plant breeding and entomology staff, names not linked to this variety): N. Lingaiah (Plant Breeding, AICRIP), B. Satish Chandra and K. Rukmini Devi (Plant Breeding), V. Venkanna (Plant Breeding), A. Venkat Reddy and S. Malathi (Entomology), Y. Hari (Biotechnology). -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
[JGL-384] Polasa Prabha, released 2002, with parentage Kavya / BPT 5204 in a 2002-era variety table. -- https://www.ijsrp.org/research_paper_dec2011/ijsrp-dec-2011-13.pdf
[JGL 3855] Parentage in the CSC record is SAMBA MAHSURI/KAVYA; the 2014 aerobic paper gives Samba Mahsuri/ARC 5984//Kavya for JGL-3844, a sister line, and does not confirm JGL 3855's parentage. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols

CONTACT DETAILS
Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station, Polasa, Jagtial, Karimnagar district, Telangana. Village Polasa, Jagtial Rural mandal, Jagtial district; about 8 km from Jagtial town and 56 km from Karimnagar. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
Address format: Polasa Village, Jagtial Rural, Jagtial district. -- https://venuetag.ai/north-telangana-zone/
Named breeder email or phone: No evidence found. No official institute email, phone or contact-page URL was returned by any search. A 2017 news report says the centre lacked scientists at the time, so the listed staff may have changed. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/Telangana/2017-05-30/Polasa-research-centre-sans-scientists/303218
Suggested check: the PJTSAU main site contact page and the Rice Research Centre, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, which is not confirmed here.

drought.details: No direct drought tolerance evidence found for JKRH 3333. Indirect evidence only: a breeding review lists JKRH 3333 among hybrids suited to aerobic conditions, and a drip-irrigated rice study lists it with strong root length and volume and statistically superior grain yield among genotypes tested. Neither source quantifies drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found for JKRH 3333 specifically.

salinity.details: No evidence found for JKRH 3333 specifically.

flood.details: No evidence found for JKRH 3333 specifically.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB): moderate tolerance claimed by the developer, and listed as resistant or moderately resistant in an IRRI-hosted hybrid rice table. Blast: moderate tolerance claimed by the developer only. Also listed as resistant or moderately resistant in the same IRRI-hosted table: RTV and BS (abbreviations as listed in the digest; full names not stated in the digest). The developer describes the hybrid as having moderate blast tolerance. The IRRI table is the only independent source; the developer claims are not independently verified.

pest_resistance.summary: Whitebacked planthopper (WBPH): resistant or moderately resistant, per the IRRI-hosted hybrid rice table. No evaluation of other insect or pest species found in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Developer's specified yield potential: 7.5-8.0 t/ha. Krishak Jagat hybrid list gives a yield figure of 5.98, with unit and basis not stated. Long-term multi-environment tests (2005-2019) report JKRH 3333 yielding about 10% more than inbred checks. The drip-irrigation study reports it as statistically superior in grain yield among genotypes tested (values not given in the digest).
agronomic_details.stability: Long-term multi-environment tests (2005-2019) report yield about 10% above inbred checks across environments. The developer describes wider adaptability. No environment-specific stability statistics found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Developer describes wider adaptability and suitability for direct seeding and machine sowing. A breeding review lists it among hybrids suited to aerobic conditions. Recommended states per the CSC-aligned Krishak Jagat entry: West Bengal, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh. Conflict: a second Krishak Jagat entry gives a 2017 record under Madhya Pradesh; this should be checked against the CSC minutes. The IRRI-hosted proceedings list Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. The company states notification for cultivation across India, which is broader than the CSC state list.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 135-140 days (developer specification; Krishak Jagat hybrid list gives the same duration)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 105-110 cm; 12-14 productive tillers per plant; panicle about 30 cm, compact; non-lodging, strong sturdy stem with heavy tillering; medium slender grain; good cooking quality; high hulling and milling recovery (developer's claims). Parentage: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRIP Initial Hybrid Rice Trial, medium slender, Kharif 2021, 32 locations: JKRH-3333 served as National Check Hybrid-1 (NCH-1); location-wise yields and checks are tabulated in the report, but the values are not in the digest. (2) 56th Annual Rice Research Group Meeting 2021 draft proceedings: JKRH-3333 (NCH-1) listed among checks in the trials; no yield values in the digest. (3) Long-term multi-environment tests, 2005-2019: JKRH 3333 among hybrids yielding about 10% more than inbred checks. (4) Drip-irrigated rice root study: JKRH 3333 listed with strong root length and volume and statistically superior grain yield among genotypes tested. Trial site details and quantitative values are not in the digest for (2) and (4).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JKRH 3333 (CSC minutes name) / JKRH-3333 (Seednet name), rice hybrid (paddy)

Name note: The evidence below refers to "JKRH 3333" or "JKRH-3333" on JK Agri Genetics pages and in ICAR/AICRIP documents. Both names are used in the sources, so I treated them as the same variety. The search budget was 4 queries, and none targeted seednet.gov.in directly, so the Seednet portal entry is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderate tolerance to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) and blast is claimed for JKRH 3333 by the developer. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333-moderate-tolerance-to-blb-blast/
- The developer describes wider adaptability and moderate blast tolerance, with a strong sturdy stem and heavy tillering. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- A paper on drip-irrigated rice lists JKRH 3333 as a genotype with strong root length and volume, and as statistically superior in grain yield among the genotypes tested. -- https://f1000research.com/articles/6-125/v2
- A hybrid rice table lists JKRH3333 as resistant or moderately resistant to BLB, RTV, BS and WBPH. The table is in the IRRI-hosted 6th International Hybrid Rice Symposium proceedings. -- http://books.irri.org/9789712203039_content.pdf
- A breeding review lists JKRH 3333 among hybrids suited to aerobic conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351749037_Rice_breeding_in_India_eight_decades_of_journey_towards_enhancing_the_genetic_gain_for_yield_nutritional_quality_and_commodity_value
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for JKRH 3333 specifically. The only abiotic items were the aerobic-suitability listing and the drip-irrigation root study above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate tolerance to BLB and blast is the developer's claim (see stress section). -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333-moderate-tolerance-to-blb-blast/
- Resistant or moderately resistant to BLB, RTV, BS (bacterial sheath/sheath blight-type entry as listed) and WBPH. Source table is cited under stress tolerance. -- http://books.irri.org/9789712203039_content.pdf
- Insect or other pest evaluation beyond WBPH: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Crop duration 135-140 days, medium slender grain, yield potential 7.5-8.0 t/ha, plant height 105-110 cm, 12-14 productive tillers per plant, 30 cm compact panicle, non-lodging stem (developer's specification). -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333-moderate-tolerance-to-blb-blast/
- Suitable for direct seeding and machine sowing, with good cooking quality and high hulling and milling recovery (developer's claims). -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- Krishak Jagat hybrid list gives the IET number 20759, release 2013 and 2016, duration 135-140 days, and a yield figure of 5.98 (unit and basis not stated). -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- AICRIP Initial Hybrid Rice Trial (medium slender), Kharif 2021, 32 locations: JKRH-3333 served as National Check Hybrid-1 (NCH-1). Location-wise yields and checks are tabulated. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf
- 56th Annual Rice Research Group Meeting 2021 draft proceedings list JKRH-3333 (NCH-1) among checks in the trials. -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- Long-term multi-environment tests (2005-2019) report JKRH 3333 as one of the hybrids yielding about 10% more than inbred checks. -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/csc2.20747

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: No evidence found. The sources give the IET identifier 20759 but no parent lines.
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: JK Agri Genetics Limited (JKAGL), Hyderabad, which states it was notified by the Government of India. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- The company says it has in-house crop breeding and biotechnology R&D units recognised by DSIR and several multi-location trial centres. The research page does not name the lead breeder. -- https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The company achievements page names no individual for this hybrid. -- https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/achievements/
- Collaborations listed for rice (BSSKV Dapoli, IIRR, IARI, Intelli Biotechnology): these are company-level and are not attributed to this variety by name. -- https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/
- CVRC or CVRC-type notification: the company timeline states the hybrid was notified by the Government of India for cultivation across India, without a date or notification number. -- https://jkagri.com/timeline/2009/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level address, JK Agri Genetics Limited: 1-10-177, 4th floor, Varun Towers, Begumpet, Hyderabad – 500016. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- Breeder name, role, email and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute email or phone: No evidence found on the pages retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved snippet (2022). Grain yield performance of hybrid rice in relation to inbred cultivars in long-term multi-environment tests in India. Crop Science -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/csc2.20747 (DOI 10.1002/csc2.20747)
- Authors not shown in retrieved snippet (year not stated in snippet, the F1000 page is about 3403 days old). Variation in rice root traits assessed by phenotyping under drip irrigation. F1000Research, article 6-125 v2 -- https://f1000research.com/articles/6-125/v2
- AICRIP Hybrid Rice Progress Report (2021), Initial Hybrid Rice Trial, Medium Slender, Kharif 2021. Hybrid Rice Progress Report, AICRIP -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf
- Authors not shown (2021). Draft Proceedings of the 56th Annual Rice Research Group Meeting. ICAR-IIRR -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- JK Agri Genetics product listing for JKRH 3333 under Field Crops and Paddy. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/ and https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/page/2/
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.
- Excluded: a news item about a seed dispute refers to "JKRH-333" (missing a digit), so it is not this variety. -- https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/jk-agri-genetics-seeks-arbitration-67-74-lakh-dues/53082566

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh, as listed in the hybrid release list for 2016 and the 2013 and 2016 entries. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- A second entry in the same list gives a 2017 record for JKRH 3333 under Madhya Pradesh. This conflicts with the 2016 entry and should be checked against the CSC minutes. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- The IRRI-hosted proceedings list JKRH 3333 among recommended hybrids for Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. -- http://books.irri.org/9789712203039_content.pdf
- The company says the hybrid was notified for cultivation across India, which is broader than the CSC state list. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
