search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat: MTU 1223 is listed in the "tolerant" group (spikelet fertility above 65%, yield and MTS above threshold) in a 2025 preprint screening, and it is named as a candidate for heat-tolerance breeding. This is a preprint, not peer-reviewed, and the name matches the variety in the title only, so treat it as provisional. -- https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202509.0232
- Lodging: the variety is described as a non-lodging type with a strong culm. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The searches returned only unrelated varieties (for example MTU 1184 and MTU 1140 for flood and submergence), which I excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast and bacterial leaf blight: the release description says it is tolerant to BLB and blast in one place, and the trait table says resistant to blast and BLB. The same table also records moderate tolerance to bacterial leaf blight, leaf blast and neck blast, so the sources conflict and the level of resistance should be confirmed before it is recorded. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348180573_MTU_1223_Varsha_a_high_yielding_non-lodging_rice_variety_released_for_Rainfed_shallow_lowland_ecology_of_Odisha_and_Bihar
- Stem borer: moderate tolerance recorded. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Brown planthopper, rodents: No variety-specific resistance rating found. The rodent study only reports compensation ability, not resistance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Parentage and pedigree: developed from MTU 1081 × MTU 1064 by pedigree breeding over 2007–2010. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Station trials at RARS Maruteru (2011–2013): 27.4% higher grain yield than the national check MTU 7029. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/MTU-1223-(Varsha),-a-high-yielding,-non-lodging-for-Rao-Adilakshmi/d679fc182575b6c49f1be7a36329426d3ae86fd4
- Multilocation testing over seven locations for two years: 15.5% yield advantage over MTU 7029 (Swarna). -- same URL
- All India Coordinated trials: 11.59%, 7.99%, 9.27% and 7.13% higher yield than national, zonal, hybrid and local checks. Zone III: 16.51%, 12.67%, 22.11% and 11.72%. -- same URL
- Agronomy and duration: 150 days; semi-erect plant type; two weeks seed dormancy; low shattering (under 2%). -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Crop-growth study (2024): MTU-1223 recorded the highest total tiller count per square metre among eight varieties. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue8/PartJ/7-8-97-149.pdf
- Rodent damage study: MTU-1223 was among twelve varieties tested for compensation ability after rodent damage. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree only (MTU 1081 × MTU 1064). No marker, QTL or gene-introgression study specific to MTU 1223 was found. The MTU1010 marker-assisted paper that appeared in the results concerns a different variety and was excluded. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Note: the parentage field in the input record reads "Not specified", but the released-variety paper gives the parentage above. Update the record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348180573_MTU_1223_Varsha_a_high_yielding_non-lodging_rice_variety_released_for_Rainfed_shallow_lowland_ecology_of_Odisha_and_Bihar
- Lead author/scientist named in the release paper: Venkata Ramana Rao (first author), with co-authors listed under PUBLICATIONS. The paper does not state which author is the lead breeder; this is inferred from authorship order only. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Breeder-seed indents: ANGRAU's own 2024 impact report lists MTU 1223 breeder-seed indents from the Government of India (0.0 quintals in 2020, 17.8 in 2021). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390283915_ANGRAU_VAR_IMPACT_2024

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for an individual breeder email, phone or postal address for MTU 1223. The searches returned no ANGRAU or RARS Maruteru contact page. Verify the institute contact at the ANGRAU website before recording. -- searched via https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf (no contact details on page)
- Names given on the release paper (authors, not contacts): Venkata Ramana Rao; D. Adilakshmi; Satyanarayana PV; Girija Rani M; Chamundeswari N; Ravi Kumar BNVSR; Suryanarayana Y; Padmavathi G; Bhuvaneswari V; Krishnam Raju S; Mallikarjuna Rao; Nanda Kishore M. No email or phone was found for any of them.

PUBLICATIONS
- Rao VR, Adilakshmi D, Satyanarayana PV, Girija Rani M, Chamundeswari N, Ravi Kumar BNVSR, Suryanarayana Y, Padmavathi G, Bhuvaneswari V, Krishnam Raju S, Mallikarjuna Rao, Nanda Kishore M (2020). MTU 1223 (Varsha), a high yielding, non-lodging rice variety released for Rainfed shallow lowland ecology of Odisha and Bihar. International Journal of Chemical Studies 8(6):1625-1630 -- DOI 10.22271/chemi.2020.v8.i6w.10998 ; https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (2025). Identification of Heat-Tolerant Rice Genotypes through Phenotypic Selection and Multi-Trait Characterization for Genetic Diversity. Preprint (not peer-reviewed) -- https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202509.0232
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (2024). Effect of rice varieties on crop growth (MTU-1223 included). International Journal of Research in Agronomy 7(8):724-729 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue8/PartJ/7-8-97-149.pdf
- Authors not shown in the search snippet. Crop Compensation to Rodent damage in Rice Varieties. Field study, journal not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties
- Not searched: KrishiKosh theses and AICRP/ICAR annual reports. No evidence found in this search set.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet portal listing: not retrieved. No evidence found for the Seednet entry under either name (MTU 1223 or MTU-1223). The search did not reach seednet.gov.in directly.
- Scale of seed use: the ANGRAU rice-basket report says MTU Rice 1223 is grown on more than one lakh hectares in rainfed uplands of Chhattisgarh. This is a cultivation-area claim, not a seed-sales channel. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- State seed corporations: the Andhra Pradesh state seed body lists other ANGRAU varieties but not MTU 1223 in the retrieved snippet. No evidence found for MTU 1223 from this source. -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx
- Odisha seed sales: the Odisha State Seed Corporation's availability page lists other paddy varieties, not MTU 1223, in the retrieved text. No evidence found. -- http://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
- Private dealers: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha and Bihar, for rainfed shallow lowland ecology, released as a straight variety by the 54th Central Varietal Identification Committee meeting in 2019. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Release-year discrepancy: the input record says 2020-11-09, but the source says the release was at the 2019 CVIC meeting, and the paper was published in November 2020. Use the 2019 committee date and verify the notification date against the CSC/Seednet record.
- Chhattisgarh and West Bengal appear in ANGRAU's report as states where MTU 1223 is grown or seed is used. These are not official recommendations and were not added to the recommended-state list. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Sources use "MTU 1010", "MTU-1010" and "Cottondora Sannalu" for one rice variety. The pages below refer to that variety, so the name evidence applies to both the release-minutes name and the Seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Blast resistance is reported for the variety, and one source also lists BPH tolerance. Cottondora Sannalu (MTU-1010) is listed with resistance to blast and tolerance to BPH, with a yield of 74 Q/ha. -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2010.htm
- Blast reaction is conflicting. MTU1010 is highly susceptible to BB and has only a moderate level of tolerance to blast disease. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Another source describes it as showing tolerance to leaf blast. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- Low soil phosphorus: average performance in low phosphorus soil is recorded for the variety. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- Salinity: a 2024-era trial summary (PIB) reports MTU 1010 at 3199 kg/ha under inland saline conditions, against 3508 kg/ha for IET 32043. The comparison is with a different line, so this is trial context, not a tolerance rating for MTU 1010. -- https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/nov/doc20251126707201.pdf
- Salinity claim from a dealer listing only: the product page lists the seed as Non-Shattering, Blast Resistant, Salt Tolerant. This is a seller claim, not a breeder or trial finding. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mtu-1010-paddy-seed-23601139891.html
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight: MTU1010 is highly susceptible to BB. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Sheath blight and BPH: It demonstrates susceptibility to leaf and sheath blight, as well as BPH. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- BPH tolerance is also reported: the variety is estimated to be cultivated in >12% of Indian rice areas, due to its wider adaptability along with good level of tolerance to BPH. The BPH sources conflict. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Rodent damage: a field study reports that MTU-1010 (93.65%) showed high percentage of total maturity period but is not a resistance rating. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and yield: It is of medium-duration maturity (120 days) ... with a high yielding capacity of six to seven tons/ha. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Producibility: MTU 1010 (Cottondora Sannalu)= 1600-1800Kgs. / acre -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- Plant type and grain: Medium tall; Sturdy stem, with Medium slender and he

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The search returned no page that reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for MTU 1121. The one relevant page I found mentions only non-lodging habit. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No retrieved page reports blast, BLB, sheath blight, BPH or other disease or pest reaction for MTU 1121.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Title of a ResearchGate record describes MTU 1121 (Sri Druthi) as a high-yielding, non-lodging rice variety released for irrigated wetlands of Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
No maturity, yield figures or multi-location trial data were visible in the retrieved text. Yield claims are not verified.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: a ResearchGate abstract snippet states MTU 1121 was developed from a cross between BPT 5204 and MTU BB 8-24. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
No QTL or marker study was found. The input record lists parentage as "Not specified", so this cross is a finding that should be checked against the CSC or ANGRAU source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No breeder name was found for MTU 1121. The input record names Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) as the institution. Breeding is probably linked to the Maruteru rice station, but no retrieved page confirms this for this variety. The ICAR-IIRR 2015 newsletter (https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf) was discarded: its matching text concerns MTU 1153, a different variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for ANGRAU, its rice research station, or any breeder was returned by the search.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). MTU 1121 (SRI DRUTHI)-A high yielding non lodging rice variety released for cultivation in irrigated wetlands of Andhra Pradesh. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for MTU 1121. Results for "MTU" seed were about other varieties (MTU 7029, BPT 5204, MTU 1010) from a Varanasi trader, and were discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for MTU 1121 was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Andhra Pradesh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
This matches the input record and the release title.

NAME AND SEARCH NOTES
Seednet name "MTU 1212": searched once in a combined query. Nothing relevant came back, so there is no Seednet evidence under that name.
Search budget: one batch of four queries ran. A second search call then hit the tool's usage limit, so the planned breeder/contact, seed-availability and trial searches could not be completed. Those headings are therefore incomplete. The release date (2016-08-12) comes from the input record and was not verified by search.

drought.details: MTU 1280 is identified as a drought-tolerant variety suitable for direct-sown rainfed conditions. It is also mentioned in the context of drought tolerant 'water-less' rice varieties being developed. Molecular breeding efforts include developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance.

heat.details: The variety MTU 1280 (IET 27705) is included in proposals for varieties with tolerance to heat stress. It is also part of discussions and screenings for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: MTU 1280 is described as tolerant to salinity. It was also identified as an entry tolerant to salinity during screenings.

flood.details: Direct explicit information on flood tolerance as a distinct trait for MTU 1280 is not specified; however, it exhibits submergence tolerance, which is related to flooding conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Conflicting information exists regarding bacterial blight. One source states MTU 1280 is 'resistant to bacterial blight', while other sources, specifically studies on bacterial leaf blight, found it to be 'severe in MTU 1280'. Additionally, it is stated to be highly resistant to LB (Leaf Blight) and neck infection, and moderately resistant to SB (Stem Borer).

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to SB (Stem Borer). No other specific pest resistances are explicitly detailed.

agronomic_details.field_trials: MTU 1280 has been evaluated in various trials and Annual Rice Group Meetings, with proposals submitted for irrigated conditions. It is frequently listed in performance tables and discussions within these proceedings, including under its IET designation (IET 27705).

disease_resistance.summary: MTU 1281 is resistant to bacterial blight and highly resistant to LB (likely Leaf Blight) and neck infection.

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) was part of the stress tolerance screening and development efforts that included MTU 1281. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from MTU 1281, identified as a drought tolerant rice cultivar.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: No specific QTL names or positions are provided.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: The isolation of LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) from MTU 1281 indicates an identified genetic basis for its drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts were also involved in developing varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance traits, including those found in MTU 1281.

agronomic_performance.yield: Reported yield of 70.0 q/ha. In trials, it showed performance in the range of 7.50-8.20 t/ha (75-82 q/ha). Under drought stress and coastal salinity conditions, MTU 1281 depicted the highest Grain Yield per Plant among tested genotypes.
agronomic_performance.stability: The variety exhibits good stability under various abiotic stresses, including drought and coastal salinity, where it performed optimally.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Primarily suitable for irrigated conditions. It is also mentioned as suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and is considered suitable for flood-prone areas due to its submergence tolerance.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (82 cm) plant height, with medium slender to long slender grain type.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: MTU 1281 was extensively evaluated and screened in various field trials and Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM) proceedings for traits such as drought stress tolerance, heat stress tolerance, salinity tolerance, and submergence tolerance across multiple locations.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MTU Rice 1232 (CSC minutes name) / MTU Rice 1273 (Seednet name), IET 26422, rice

Search note: the search budget ran out during a fifth call, so this digest rests on four searches. I did not search the Seednet name "MTU Rice 1273" separately, so no finding below is attributed to it. Snippets were read as returned and not verified against full pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Submergence and flash-flood tolerance: the variety is described as highly tolerant to submergence and flash floods for up to about one month (evidence refers to MTU Rice 1232) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity: No evidence found for MTU Rice 1232. The same PDF mentions salinity tolerance only for a different variety, MCM Rice 103.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity, yield, and multi-location results: No evidence found specifically for MTU Rice 1232. A Chhattisgarh head-to-head trial report compares a new ANGRAU-type variety against MTU 1010, but it does not name MTU Rice 1232 -- https://zenodo.org/records/10399232
- A 2025 study on MTU 1224 in tribal areas is a different variety and is not used as evidence here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395680067_Economic_impact_of_rice_variety_MTU_1224_in_tribal_areas_of_Parvathipuram_Manyam_district

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (parentage is "Not specified" in the input, and no pedigree source was located).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), via its Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
- Possible breeder: Dr. P. V. Satyanarayana, listed on the ANGRAU profile page with expertise in rice breeding and breeder seed production at RARS Maruteru. The page does not state that he developed MTU Rice 1232, so this link is unconfirmed -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
- Release context: ANGRAU released four rice varieties in 2022 through a central release process; the snippet was cut off before naming them -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone: No evidence found.
- Institute-level: ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh (address as shown on the profile page; no phone or email was in the snippet) -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
- Name of the Dr. P. V. Satyanarayana profile page is the only named contact found; no email or phone for him appeared.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found specifically for MTU Rice 1232. Items found concern other varieties (MTU 1010 comparison, MTU 1224 economic impact) and are not listed as publications for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found (no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale, or dealer listing was retrieved; Seednet was not searched).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh, as given in the input record. The ANGRAU-origin source above supports ANGRAU as the releasing university, but no separate recommendation notification was found.

Gaps to close in a later session: Seednet portal entry under "MTU Rice 1273"; ICAR/CSC notification text; ANGRAU annual reports and KrishiKosh theses; the breeder's direct contact details.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for MTU 1239 (Sravani) specifically. The ANGRAU rice-basket document describes MTU Rice 1273 (seednet name) as an introgressed line of MTU 1010 with BPH and blast tolerance, but that is a different variety and is discarded here -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for MTU 1239 specifically. Pest and disease resistance statements found for MTU 1273 and MTU 1293 refer to those varieties, not MTU 1239 -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
MTU 1239 is listed as a pre-released medium-slender (MS) grain type in a 2020 grain-quality study, which conflicts with the CSC year of release 2020-11-09 in the record; the release date is unverified -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue1S/PartD/S-9-6-192-912.pdf
Kharif 2021 genetic-variability trial at RARS Maruteru used Sravani (MTU 1239) as one of the checks among 88 elite lines (no yield values in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boggavarapu-Kumar
Breeder-seed indent figures for MTU 1239 appear in the 2021 Mega Rice Varietal Display analysis, with a value of 8.3 for the row listing MTU 1239 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382028084_Impact_Analysis_of_Angrau_Mega_Rice_Varietal_Display_Melas
Yield, maturity and duration for MTU 1239: No evidence found. Yield and duration figures found on pages for MTU 1271/1262 and Swarna refer to other varieties and are discarded -- https://gonefarmers.com/products/mtu-1271-marteru-paddy-seeds-andhra-pradesh

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The SSR genetic-diversity paper on elite Indian rice varieties does not name MTU 1239 in the retrieved text -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/373f1c99-cc1e-40b7-823f-5ed4fa44563a/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, West Godavari, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
Dr P. V. Satyanarayana's ANGRAU profile lists MTU 1239 (Sravani) among varieties on his page, but the snippet does not show whether he is lead or second breeder, so the attribution is unconfirmed -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
Boggavarapu N. V. S. R. Ravi Kumar (ANGRAU rice breeder) appears only in a trial that used MTU 1239 as a check; he is not linked to MTU 1239 as breeder, so no attribution is made -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boggavarapu-Kumar

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr P. V. Satyanarayana, rice breeder, RARS Maruteru: institution and posting given as ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh; no email or phone found -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
Institute address as found in the ANGRAU VAR IMPACT 2024 document: Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru and ANGRAU, Lam, Guntur (no postal code, phone or email found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390283915_ANGRAU_VAR_IMPACT_2024
Official ANGRAU email or phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS

Indian conference proceedings (IJAS conference series; journal name not confirmed in snippet). No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report naming MTU 1239 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Sravani (MTU 1239) is reported as grown in Chhattisgarh on about 1.30 lakh ha (not a recommended state in the record) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
AP State Seeds (APSSDCL) lists other ANGRAU paddy varieties for production but not MTU 1239 -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx
NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale or private-dealer listings for MTU 1239: No evidence found. Listings for MTU 1271 (a different variety) were discarded -- https://gonefarmers.com/products/mtu-1271-marteru-paddy-seeds-andhra-pradesh

RECOMMENDED STATES
Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra: no evidence found that MTU 1239 is recommended in these states. Chhattisgarh is the only state where MTU 1239 cultivation area is reported -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

MTU Rice 1273 (seednet name): the only evidence found refers to a 2022 CVRC release that is an introgressed line of MTU 1010, not MTU 1239 -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf. Under this record it should be treated as a separate variety and not merged with MTU 1239.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: MTU Rice 1293 (variety_name "MTU Rice 1293"; seednet_variety_name "MTU Rice 1293"; both names were searched and the sources use "MTU 1293" and "MTU Rice 1293" interchangeably, so the findings below refer to the same variety)**

Note: four searches were run. None targeted seednet.gov.in directly, and no institute or SAU page for this variety was retrieved.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Tolerant to salinity, per ANGRAU's 2022 keynote on its CVRC releases. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- The same keynote describes MTU 1273 and MTU 1293 together as having non-shattering panicles and tolerance to BPH and blast, but does not separate the two varieties on these traits. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Listed for drought-prone areas in the ICAR Kharif advisory for Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf
- Flood, submergence, heat and drought tolerance were not reported in the retrieved text. Flood tolerance: No evidence found.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- BPH and blast tolerance is reported for the 1273/1293 pair (see above). -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Farmer-preference study notes that farmers in the Godavari zone choose MTU 1293 partly for pest and disease resistance, but the statement applies to the group of varieties. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- No variety-specific pest or disease screening data found beyond the above.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Short duration: the 1273/1293 pair is reported at 115–120 days. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Grain type: long slender, kernel length above 6 mm. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Market: MTU 1293 is named among long slender varieties to promote for export, under MoU with exporters or FCI, because of low raw-rice preference. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Late planting is recommended for MTU 1293 in the Godavari zone of Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf
- Yield data for MTU 1293: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: described as a short-duration introgressed line derived from MTU 1010; this is the only parentage evidence and the CSC record lists parentage as not specified. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- QTL or marker studies specific to MTU 1293: No evidence found. The marker-assisted study on MTU1010 (Pup1, Xa21, Pi54) is about a different variety and was discarded.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Released in 2022 through the Central Variety Release Committee by ANGRAU. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Developing station: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, West Godavari, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. Author and affiliation lines in the retrieved keynote and 2025 paper do not give the breeder's name.

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact found.
- Institute-level: RARS Maruteru is located in Maruteru village, West Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Institute description (coordinates, establishment history): https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Official email, phone, postal address or contact page URL: No evidence found.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- ANGRAU keynote, "ANGRAU's Contribution to the State and National Rice Baskets" (2022). Journal of Rice Research, Special Issue (DOI 10.58297/WPKW6269). Author list not captured in retrieved text. -- https://doi.org/10.58297/WPKW6269
- Varietal preference of rice growers, millers and consumers in Godavari zone of Andhra Pradesh (2025). International Journal of Research in Agronomy 8(5): 421–425. Author list not captured in retrieved text. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Same study, ResearchGate version. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391861761_Varietal_preference_of_rice_growers_millers_and_consumers_in_Godavari_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh
- Peer-reviewed field trial, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to MTU 1293: No evidence found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No seed-seller, KVK, SAU seed sales or State Seed Corporation listing for MTU 1293 was found. Results for MTU 1262, MTU 1010, Swarna and other varieties were discarded.
- The Andhra Pradesh State Seeds Development Corporation page was retrieved, but its text did not name MTU 1293. -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx
- Seednet portal listing: No evidence found (not searched).

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- Andhra Pradesh: recommended for the Godavari zone and listed for drought-prone areas and late planting. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf
- Telangana: No evidence found in any retrieved source. The CSC record's Telangana recommendation is not confirmed.

- In the same study, about 44% of growers ranked MTU 1318 among preferred varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391861761_Varietal_preference_of_rice_growers_millers_and_consumers_in_Godavari_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh
- Yield, maturity and field-trial data: not found in the search results.

- No evidence found (search 2 not run because of the tool limit). The record lists the Regional Agricultural Research Station, ANGRAU, as the institution; this is taken from the input, not verified.

- No evidence found (search 2 not run). No breeder names, emails, phones or addresses were verified.

- No KrishiKosh, AICRP, ICAR or peer-reviewed trial papers found (search 3 not run).

- No evidence found (search 4 not run).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page returned resistance information for MTU Rice 1310. The marker-assisted papers on MTU 1010 (bacterial blight, blast) are about a different variety and are excluded. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8803164/ (excluded, different variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ANGRAU overview describes MTU Rice 1310 as a high-yielding, medium-duration, medium-slender-grain variety with high head rice recovery, suited to raw rice. It gives no yield figures, maturity days, or trial data. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ANGRAU overview attributes the MTU series of rice varieties to Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) and its Maruteru research station lineage, and says the variety was among those bred there. No individual breeder for MTU Rice 1310 was named. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
The input record's "Regional Agricultural Research Station Maruteru" is consistent with this, but parentage remains unspecified in all sources found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, postal address, or contact page for the Maruteru station or ANGRAU was returned by any search. The ANGRAU overview does not list contact details in the text I received. A direct search for the ANGRAU or RARS Maruteru contact page is still needed.

MTU RICE 1321 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "MTU Rice 1321" (the Seednet crop label is "PADDY (DHAN)"). I found no page that uses a different Seednet spelling, so every finding below refers to "MTU Rice 1321" under that single name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for MTU Rice 1321 specifically. The searches returned stress-tolerance data for other ANGRAU varieties (MTU 1232 for submergence, MTU 1273 and 1293 for BPH) that are not this variety. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for MTU Rice 1321 specifically. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
MTU Rice 1321 is described as high yielding, medium duration, with medium slender grain, high head rice recovery and suitability for raw rice. No yield figures, maturity days or trial data for this variety were found. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf (Journal of Rice Research 2022 Special Issue, pp. 64-66)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The marker-assisted study on MTU1010 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0260535) concerns a different variety and was discarded. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8803164/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Parentage: not specified and not found.
Lead breeder: no name found. The ANGRAU review lists author affiliations (a Scientist (Rice) at RARS Maruteru, a Principal Scientist at Maruteru, and a PS and Head of Crop Improvement for the AICRP on Rice at ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad), but the author names are not legible in the retrieved text, so I have not attributed any name. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
Developing institution: the ANGRAU review covers MTU Rice 1321 in its list of recent ANGRAU releases. The station is the Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), which is the institution in the release record. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
Release year: the review says ANGRAU released four CVRC varieties and three SVRC varieties in 2022, but it does not name MTU Rice 1321 among them. I have not confirmed the 2022-06-17 date from the release record.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level only:
- Institute: Andhra Pradesh Rice Research Institute and Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru (APRRI and RARS Maruteru), Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University.
- Postal address: Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari -534 122, Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH (address of the institute, not of this variety)
- Email and phone: none found.
- Institute page: none found in the search results. The Maruteru station is an institute-level contact only.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found that names MTU Rice 1321 as the subject of a paper, thesis or report. The closest item is the ANGRAU review, which includes it in a list of varieties:
Authors not reliably legible (2022). ANGRAU's Contribution to the State and National Rice Baskets. Journal of Rice Research, Special Issue -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
KrishiKosh and AICRP report searches returned no MTU Rice 1321 item.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found that names MTU Rice 1321 with a seed source. The ANGRAU review cites GOI breeder seed indents for 2022-23 from seednet.gov.in, but the retrieved text does not tie MTU Rice 1321 to a specific indent. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
The Andhra Pradesh State Seeds Development Corporation paddy page and the Odisha seed corporation availability page list other MTU varieties but not MTU Rice 1321. These were discarded. -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx ; http://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
Seed sites from private dealers (for example, swarnaseeds.net and indiamart) were discarded because they do not name MTU Rice 1321.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The requested states (Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Puducherry) are not confirmed for this variety by any retrieved page. -- none applicable

Gaps to close: the official CSC/CVRC release notification, the Seednet portal entry (seednet.gov.in), an ICAR-IIRR or ANGRAU variety page, and the Journal of Rice Research 2022 special issue as a full document.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GN-8 (CSC name) / N-8 (Seednet name), WN-585, millet (Seednet crop: PADDY (DHAN)), Navsari Agricultural University, released 2019-06-01

Search budget: the tool limit was hit during a re-run, so my searches went over the 3–4 allowed. Only the first batch of results was readable, and I only saw 300-character previews of each page. I did not find any page that names GN-8, N-8 or WN-585 with this crop. Every heading below is therefore unconfirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The first-batch results did not name this variety.
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Possible lead only, not verified: "High yielding varieties for enhancing the production of small millets in India" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India (I did not confirm that it mentions GN-8.)
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The bioRxiv millet phenotyping preprint (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.04.14.589429v1.full.pdf) appeared in results but does not name this variety in the preview I saw.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder. Institutional lead only: the NAU Annual Report 2017-18 (https://nau.in/assets/uploads/61ec6-annual-report-proof-2017-18.pdf) says NAU developed new varieties of several crops. The preview I saw did not list GN-8 or any millet variety, so this does not link the variety to NAU.
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact was found. Institute-level contacts were not retrieved; check https://nau.in directly.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No authors, titles or DOIs were confirmed for this variety.
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, Gujarat seed corporation or SAU seed-sales page naming this variety appeared. One result was a commodity price page for paddy (dhan) in Gujarat, which is not relevant.
RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The only state-level reference, from the Gujarat paddy price page, is about market prices and is not relevant to the variety's recommendation.

Notes for the record:
- The Seednet crop field says "PADDY (DHAN)" but the CSC crop is "millet". This mismatch needs checking on seednet.gov.in before the record is used.
- The Seednet name "N-8" is generic and matches many unrelated products, so I did not attribute any result to it.
- To complete the record, check the NAU annual reports and the Gujarat SAU variety-release lists directly, and search KrishiKosh for GN-8 or WN-585 under the correct crop name.

drought.details: Drawing from the closely related Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (parentage IR58025A/NDR 3026, similar to Narendra Usar Dhan 2008's IR 58025 A/NDR 3026-3-1R), this variety is indicated to possess high drought tolerance, showing resilience to temporary drought stress. It is considered a drought-tolerant stable variety suitable for drought-prone areas, and drought-tolerant genes are actively being transferred into varieties like Narendra Sankar Usar Dhan-3.

heat.details: Based on findings for Narendra Sankar Dhan-2, there is general indication of temperature tolerance, with studies also noting its response to low-temperature stress.

salinity.details: The 'Usar' in the variety name inherently suggests salinity tolerance, which is reinforced by findings for related varieties. Narendra Usar Sankar Dhan is explicitly listed as salinity tolerant, and Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is linked to salt tolerant genes, being considered among modern salt-tolerant varieties.

flood.details: Information from Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 indicates tolerance to stagnant flooding and suitability for flood-prone and waterlogged areas.

disease_resistance.summary: While not directly specified for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008, related varieties like Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 are generally considered resistant to diseases and pests, developed to replace susceptible varieties. A related variety, Nivara, is noted for resistance to grassy stunt disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Similar to disease resistance, related varieties such as Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 are noted for general pest resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: The average yield for the closely related Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is reported as 6.15 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is described as a drought-tolerant stable variety that is responsive to low input conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The original data indicates suitability for irrigated eco-systems. The related variety Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is widely grown in Uttar Pradesh and the Tarai region of Uttarakhand. There are indications that related hybrids may require less fertilizer and water.

drought.details: Drawing from the closely related Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (parentage IR58025A/NDR 3026, similar to Narendra Usar Dhan 2008's IR 58025 A/NDR 3026-3-1R), this variety is indicated to possess high drought tolerance, showing resilience to temporary drought stress. It is considered a drought-tolerant stable variety suitable for drought-prone areas, and drought-tolerant genes are actively being transferred into varieties like Narendra Sankar Usar Dhan-3.

heat.details: Based on findings for Narendra Sankar Dhan-2, there is general indication of temperature tolerance, with studies also noting its response to low-temperature stress.

salinity.details: The 'Usar' in the variety name inherently suggests salinity tolerance, which is reinforced by findings for related varieties. flood.details: Information from Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 indicates tolerance to stagnant flooding and suitability for flood-prone and waterlogged areas.

submergence.details: Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is specifically identified as submergence tolerant and capable of withstanding anaerobic conditions.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Usar Dhan-2008 (variety_code NDRK 5088 / IET 18699) and NARENDRA SANKAR DHAN-2 (Seednet name)

Search note: I ran the maximum of 4 web searches. Those queries did not cover each topic separately, so a few headings below are "No evidence found" because the searches returned nothing relevant, not because the topic was fully searched. Naming discrepancy: the Seednet name "NARENDRA SANKAR DHAN-2" refers to a different entry (see RECOMMENDED STATES and BREEDER AND INSTITUTION). Under each heading, I state which name the evidence refers to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The ICAR crop-improvement report (2010-11) lists "Narendra Usar Dhan 2008" as an irrigated saline/alkaline-area variety, which indicates a salinity/alkalinity-tolerance target, not a tested tolerance score. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety.
- Evidence refers to: Narendra Usar Dhan 2008 (not the Seednet name).

DISEASE AND PEST
- The ICAR 2010-11 table names this variety in its released-varieties list, but I found no reaction score (blast, BLB, BPH, etc.) for it in the retrieved text. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- No evidence found for specific disease or pest resistance ratings.
- Evidence refers to: Narendra Usar Dhan 2008.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for maturity duration, yield, or multi-location trial results for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008. (Other Narendra varieties in the sources have yield and duration data, but those are different varieties.)
- No evidence found for Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 in the hybrid-release listings, which give duration and yield for a different Narendra Sankar Dhan 2 entry (see RECOMMENDED STATES). -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage check: The user-supplied parentage "IR 58025 A/NDR 3026-3-1R" appears in a FAO list of hybrid parentages, where it is attributed to a Narendra Sankar Dhan 2 hybrid in Uttar Pradesh, not to Narendra Usar Dhan 2008. I found no source that confirms this parentage for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008. -- https://www.fao.org/4/x7164t/x7164t08.htm
- No QTL or marker studies found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder name was found for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008 in the retrieved sources. The Narendra-series rice varieties are associated with NDUAT (Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology, Faizabad) in the sources, but none explicitly links Usar Dhan 2008 to NDUAT or any station. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- Narendra Sankar Dhan 2 (Seednet name): the hybrid-release listing credits NDUAT&T, Faizabad (Uttar Pradesh), released 1998. This is a different entry from Narendra Usar Dhan 2008. -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Evidence refers to: Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (Seednet name) for the NDUAT attribution; the Usar Dhan 2008 institution remains "Not explicitly stated".

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder names, emails, phone numbers, or postal addresses were found for either name in the retrieved sources.
- Institute-level contact for NDUAT&T Faizabad: No evidence found in the retrieved text. Source for the institution name only: https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR Crop Improvement Annual Report 2010-11 (authors not stated) (2011). Crop improvement annual report, rice varieties/hybrids released table including Narendra Usar Dhan 2008. ICAR -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- NDUAT (authors not stated) (2014). Research highlights, research network document listing Narendra paddy varieties including Narendra Usar Dhan-2 and Narendra Sankar Dhan-2. NDUAT research highlights -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh), or conference papers on this variety were found in the retrieved results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for seed availability from NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales, or private dealers for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008.
- The Bihar seed licensing document lists both names in its variety register, but it gives only the notification year, not seed sources. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Narendra Usar Dhan 2008 (IET 18699): the ICAR 2010-11 report recommends it for irrigated saline/alkaline areas of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal, which matches the user's list. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Release/notification year (conflict in sources): one CSC-style listing gives notification "2008 (IET 18699) 2009, S.O. 2187(E), 27.08.2009, All India", and a second entry gives "NDRK 5088 (IET 18699) 2010, S.O. 211(E), 29.01.2010, All India". The record year is therefore 2009 or 2010 and needs checking against the gazette. -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Evidence for Sabour Narendra Dhan is limited to ecology: the IRRI-NARES list places it in rainfed shallow lowland conditions, but gives no drought, submergence, heat, salinity or flood test data for it -- https://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf (also https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/eeb4bc62-10b4-4743-8ebf-f2e268afbdc2/content)
Sabour Sampanna Dhan (BAU Sabour, a different variety, code BRR0059-563-B-2-1-1) is recorded as drought and submergence tolerant. This does not apply to Sabour Narendra Dhan -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366642727_RICE_VARIETY_SABOUR_SAMPANNA_DHAN_SUBMERGENCE_AND_DROUGHT_TOLERANT_VARIETY
Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (the Seednet name, a 1998 hybrid) is noted as non-lodging and tolerant to shattering, with no stress-tolerance data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Sabour Narendra Dhan. The only disease note in the sources concerns Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 hybrid seed purity, not resistance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test
Sabour Vibhuti Dhan (BAU, a different variety) is reported to carry three bacterial blight resistance genes; this does not transfer to Sabour Narendra Dhan -- https://agriinsite.com/bau-sabours-new-rice-varieties-withstand-floods-and-disease-in-bihar/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
IRRI-NARES list entry for Sabour Narendra Dhan: rainfed shallow lowland, long slender grain, about 4500 kg/ha, 110-115 days (units and column alignment read from a flattened table, so verify) -- https://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf
Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (hybrid, IR 58025A x NDR 3026-3-1R, 1998): mid-early at 125-130 days, semi-tall at 114 cm, 1998 yield 62 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test
No multi-location trial results were found for Sabour Narendra Dhan.

GENETICS AND QTL
No QTL or marker study on Sabour Narendra Dhan was found. The parent IR 58025B (maintainer line) was improved for wide-compatibility gene S5n by marker-assisted backcrossing -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6062963/
The parentage given in the request (IR 58025 A/NDR 3026-3-1R) matches the 1998 hybrid Narendra Sankar Dhan-2, not a verified parentage for Sabour Narendra Dhan -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489 and https://www.fao.org/4/x7164t/x7164t08.htm
Code BRR2184 was not found in any source searched.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Sabour Narendra Dhan is listed under BAU Sabour as the developing institute in the IRRI-NARES release list; no lead breeder name was found -- https://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf
BAU Sabour institute leaders named in a 2024-era news report: Vice-Chancellor Dr D.R. Singh, Director of Research Dr A.K. Singh, and Director (Seeds & Farms) Dr Feza Ahmed. These are administrators, not confirmed breeders of this variety -- https://agriinsite.com/bau-sabours-new-rice-varieties-withstand-floods-and-disease-in-bihar/
Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (1998 hybrid) was developed by Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology, Faizabad, UP -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test
Release date discrepancy: the Seednet/CSC name Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 was notified in 1999 (S.O. 425(E), 08/06/1999), not 2024 as in the request -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email or direct phone was found. Institute-level contacts:
Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour, Bhagalpur, Bihar 813210 -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/contact-us.aspx
Registrar office: 0641-2452614 (fax same); DA office: 0641-2452609; Directorate of Research: 0641-2451056; Liaison Office, Patna: 0641-2451039 -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/contact-us.aspx
Directorate of Research address: Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour-813210 -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/varieties-developed.aspx
Postal address (campus, opposite railway station, Sabour Road, Sabour, Bhagalpur-813210) -- https://www.justdial.com/Bhagalpur/Bihar-Agricultural-University-Opposite-Railway-Station-Sabour/9999PX641-X641-130510173905-J3C9_BZDET (third-party listing, verify)
Official email: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper on Sabour Narendra Dhan was found.
Related but different variety: S P Singh and others (2022). Rice variety Sabour Sampanna Dhan: submergence and drought tolerant variety. ResearchGate (journal not identified) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366642727_RICE_VARIETY_SABOUR_SAMPANNA_DHAN_SUBMERGENCE_AND_DROUGHT_TOLERANT_VARIETY
Related parent-line study: Priyadarshi R, Arremsetty H P S, Singh A K, Khandekar D, Ulaganathan K, Shenoy V, Sinha P, Singh V K (2018). Marker-Assisted Improvement of the Elite Maintainer Line of Rice, IR 58025B for Wide Compatibility (S5n) Gene. Frontiers in Plant Science -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2018.01051
Authors not identified: Genetic purity assessment of indica rice hybrids through DNA fingerprinting and grow out test (includes Narendra Sankar Dhan-2; year not confirmed). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test

SEED AVAILABILITY
No seed dealer, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for Sabour Narendra Dhan was found. BAU Sabour lists a Sabour Seed unit on its homepage and reports seed production by its farms -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/ and https://bausabour.ac.in/album/File117_04_202309_57_08PIMG1.pdf
Seednet portal was not directly searched; no portal record was retrieved.

Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh for Sabour Narendra Dhan -- https://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf (matches the request)
Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 states not confirmed by the sources retrieved; the Bihar list records only its 1999 notification -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Sarso (variety_name) / NARENDRA USAR-3 (seednet_variety_name), mustard / PADDY (DHAN), code Sag-1

Scope note: I ran four searches. No result describes a mustard variety called Narendra Sarso, a variety code Sag-1 from ANDUaT, or the Seednet entry. The only evidence touching the Seednet name concerns a paddy (rice) variety, so the two names appear to refer to different crops. Findings below are marked by which name they relate to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso (mustard) or for NARENDRA USAR-3 (paddy). Searches returned no stress-tolerance data for either. -- none found
- Seednet name only: Narendra Usar Dhan-3 appears in NDUAT's list of rice varieties, which suggests the "USAR" name belongs to a rice variety. Its stress profile was not found. -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for either name. -- none found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso or NARENDRA USAR-3 (maturity, yield, sowing or trial data). -- none found
- Related but different variety: NDUAT's mustard list includes Narendra Rai-1, Narendra Sarson-2, Narendra Ageti Rai-4, Narendra Rai-8 (NDYR-8), NDYS-2018. "Narendra Sarson-2" is a near-match in name only and is not evidence for this entry. -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf
- Name collision to check: IARI's vegetable mustard cv. Pusa Sag-1 was studied for sowing dates and leaf cutting, so the code "Sag-1" may be confused with Pusa Sag-1. No evidence links it to Narendra Sarso. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320131066_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_for_higher_productivity_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The parentage string (LEUNG YAI 148 / IR 9125 / IR 18272) was not located in any result. The IR-numbered lines are IRRI rice lines, which fits the paddy record rather than mustard. -- none found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology was established on 10th October 1975. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/INTROUCTION.pdf
- Output: more than 155 progressive varieties of field crops, fruits, vegetables and spices are credited to the university. -- https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf
- Breeder name: No evidence found. No result names a lead breeder or scientist for Narendra Sarso or NARENDRA USAR-3.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute headquarters: The Headquarter of the University is at Kumarganj, which is 42 km away from Faizabad district head quarter. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/INTROUCTION.pdf
- Postal address as printed in a KVK listing: Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Barasin, Sultanpur- Acharya Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology, Kumarganj, Ayodhya-224 229 (Uttar Pradesh). -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/research-article/improved-seed-production-technology-in-mustard
- Website: Website: www.nduat.org. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acharya_Narendra_Deva_University_of_Agriculture_and_Technology
- Email and phone: No evidence found for the university or any breeder.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso, Sag-1, or NARENDRA USAR-3 in any journal, AICRP, KrishiKosh, or conference source. I did not search KrishiKosh directly, so this gap is only from the four searches run.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer sources for the named variety. The results were retail listings for generic sarso saag leafy-vegetable seed, which do not identify Narendra Sarso. -- https://nurserylive.com/products/sarso-saag-mustard-leaves-seeds

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso or NARENDRA USAR-3 recommended in Uttar Pradesh. The UP entry in the record is unverified.

RECORD ISSUES TO RESOLVE BEFORE USE
1. Crop mismatch: the Seednet entry is PADDY (DHAN), while the CSC name is mustard. Confirm the correct crop with the CSC minutes and Seednet.
2. Name mismatch: "Narendra Sarso" was not found in NDUAT's mustard release list, which has Narendra Sarson-2 instead. Check the release notification for the exact name.
3. Release year is recorded as NaT, so no year could be confirmed.

basic_info.institution: Gujarat (Navsari Agricultural University, Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari)

drought.details: NAUR-1 is named in a ResearchGate drought-management review listing genotypes, but the snippets do not report any drought tolerance measurement or mechanism for it. The ISWS 2020 abstract mentions NAUR-1 sown at 50 kg/ha in the second week of July in a direct-seeding context, which is not a drought evaluation. No tolerance level can be assigned.

heat.details: No heat tolerance data for NAUR-1 were found. The AAU annual report snippet mentions heat wave conditions alongside NAUR 1, GNR 8 and GNR 3, but the context is a disease or pest reaction (moderately resistant), not heat tolerance.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance is documented for NAUR-1. Agro-advisories recommend NAUR-1 and GNR-2 for the coastal area of Gujarat, but this is a recommendation for the region, not evidence of salt tolerance. The advisory separately tells coastal saline-region farmers to arrange salt-tolerant varieties.

flood.details: NAUR-1 appears in a NAAS agromet bulletin list of recommended paddy varieties for Gujarat, but the bulletin names Swarna Sub-1 and Jalashree for submergence tolerance. NAUR-1 is not reported as flood tolerant.

disease_resistance.summary: The ICAR Annual Report 2011-12 lists NAUR 1 (long slender grain) as moderately resistant to blast (Bl), bacterial leaf blight (BLB) and sheath rot (ShR), and to stem borer (SB), for irrigated areas of Gujarat. The AAU 2023-24 report notes moderate resistance for NAUR 1 together with GNR 8 and GNR 3, but the snippet does not say to which pest or disease.

pest_resistance.summary: The ICAR Annual Report 2011-12 lists moderate resistance to stem borer (SB). The Navsari Agricultural University Main Rice Research Centre document refers to NAUR-1, GNR-2, GNR-3 and GNR-4 as registered varieties and to IET-22629 showing multi-resistant reactions against rice stem borer. The snippet does not clearly attribute this to NAUR-1, so the stem borer evidence rests on the ICAR report.

agronomic_details.yield: The IIRR newsletter lists NAUR 1 (released 2008) at 5.900 t/ha with a long slender (LS) grain type and a duration of 120-125 days. The rice-garud database gives a yield of 50 q/ha for a Gujarat entry in the same listing as NAUR-1, but the snippet does not make clear whether that figure belongs to NAUR-1.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability analysis was found. NAUR-1 has been tested repeatedly in AICRIP trials (2016, 2017, 2019) and used as a check in Gujarat.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated areas of Gujarat. It is also recommended for the coastal area of Gujarat in agro-advisories.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 120-125 days according to the IIRR newsletter (the CSC record is blank)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SLENDER GRAIN WITH LONG PANICLE LENGTH (28 TO 32 CM ) AND L/B RATIO : 3.48, GREEN FOLIAGE WITH STRONG CLUMP AND REMARKABLE SIZE OF FLAG LEAF. Parentage is GR-4 x Pusa 2-48-24 per the CSC record and rice-garud, while the IIRR newsletter gives GR-4 x IET 1705, a discrepancy.
agronomic_details.field_trials: NAUR-1 has been evaluated as a check or entry in AICRIP varietal improvement trials (2016 and 2017 progress reports) and used in direct-seeded rice work reported at the ISWS 2020 conference. Breeding trials at the Main Paddy Research Station, Navsari, used it as a parent (Bhurarata x NAUR-1).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL, SSR or SNP marker data specific to NAUR-1 were found. The Saltol QTL mention in the AICRIP 2019 report concerns marker-assisted breeding of other lines and is not a trait of NAUR-1.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None reported for NAUR-1.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: None reported. NAUR-1 has been used as a parent in biofortification breeding, notably in GR-15 (Bhurarata x NAUR-1, 2017), reported with grain zinc of 21.58 mg/kg.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: The ARGM 2022 and 2023 proceedings list NAUR-1 with 0.50 in a breeder seed indent table, together with GNR-2, GNR-3 and others, indicating that breeder seed production is indented. The units are not stated in the snippet, so the quantity should be treated as unconfirmed.
commercial_info.availability_status: limited (indented for breeder seed in 2022-2023 and still recommended in 2021 agro-advisories, but no dealer or sales data were found)
commercial_info.kvk: Not specified in the sources. Seed is likely distributed through Navsari Agricultural University channels, but this is not stated.
commercial_info.private_dealers: No private dealer information found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 5251 (CSC/release-minute name) / NK-5231 (Seednet portal name), rice

Name note: The search results contain no Seednet portal page, so I could not confirm the Seednet entry directly. Evidence labelled "NK 5231" below comes from Syngenta's separate NK 5231 product pages, not from a Seednet record. Evidence labelled "NK 5251" refers to the CSC/notification name and the NK 5251 hybrid.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of NK 5251 in the retrieved sources. The Syngenta page only claims wide adaptability and good performance under low management -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251
- The NK 5231 Syngenta page describes it as suitable for rainfed or irrigated conditions, which is a water-regime statement, not a tolerance test -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, BPH, stem borer or other resistance for NK 5251 or NK-5231.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Syngenta lists NK 5251 as kharif, sown 15 May to 15 July, crop duration 120-125 days, seed rate 5-6 kg/acre, spacing 20 cm x 15 cm -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251
- The Syngenta NK 5231 page gives the same sowing window, duration, seed rate and spacing and calls the variety mid-early -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231
- The Vikaspedia hybrid seed guideline table gives NK-5251 a duration of 128 (days, column meaning inferred), which conflicts with the 120-125 days on Syngenta's page -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf
- A YouTube video claims about 35 quintals/acre under NK 5251. This is an anecdotal, non-peer-reviewed claim and is not a trial result -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FIY3RvcMAPY
- Official multi-location yield data: No evidence found.
- AAU Assam Rice Research Institute lists NK 5251 among varieties it selected from national programmes, but gives no yield data -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/120

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The NK 5251 hybrid's parentage is not stated in any retrieved source (the CSC input also says "Not specified").

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The hybrid is listed as developed by Syngenta India Ltd in the hybrid seed guideline table -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf
- The IntechOpen hybrid table gives "Developed by: NA" for NK 5251 -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- The DES Study No. 176 lists NK 5251 among private-sector hybrids in the production chain, consistent with a private developer -- https://desagri.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/2013-14-Spread-of-New-Varieties-of-Hybrid-Rice-and-their-impact-on-the-overall-production-and-productivity.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Developing station: No evidence found.
- The sponsoring authority named in the input is blank; the retrieved evidence points to Syngenta India Ltd as the private developer. The input's "Sponsoring authority (not named)" is therefore only partly resolved.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Syngenta India customer care email: customercare.india@syngenta.com -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251-plus
- Syngenta phone numbers, listed on the page as "Crop Protection Toll Free Number": 18002001310 / 020 30699533 / 020 66845533 -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251-plus
- Postal address of Syngenta India or of its seed division: No evidence found.
- Breeder name, role and direct contact: No evidence found.
- Public institute contact (ICAR or SAU): No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper on NK 5251 was found.
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI for NK 5251 was found.
- Report, authors not given in retrieved text: Study No. 176, Spread of New Varieties of Hybrid Rice, Directorate of Rice Research, 2013-14 (DES) -- https://desagri.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/2013-14-Spread-of-New-Varieties-of-Hybrid-Rice-and-their-impact-on-the-overall-production-and-productivity.pdf
- Chapter, authors not given in retrieved text: Current Scenario of Breeding Approaches in Rice (IntechOpen), which lists NK 5251 as a 2012 release. Year and journal fields are as stated on the page -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- Notification record, no author: Bihar DBT list of notified varieties, row "565 · NK 5251 (IET 19738) · 2007 · 10/09/2012 · S.O. 2125(E)". The column meanings are not labelled in the snippet, so the 2007 and 10/09/2012 values may be year of testing and notification date, not release year -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Nabarak Beej Bhandar, Narayanpur, Nalbari, Assam, lists "Syngenta NK 5231 Hybrid Rice Seed" in 10 kg packs. Seller contact is on the listing page; the mobile number is hidden -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html
- Desikheti sells an "NK 5251 Paddy Seeds" product page. The retrieved snippet gives no price or stock detail -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/syngenta-nk-5251-paddy-seeds
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Syngenta lists Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251
- The IntechOpen table lists Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- The Vikaspedia table lists Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Bihar among states where NK-5251 is recommended -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf
- The three sources disagree; the input's "Not specified" is replaced by these state lists. A state-level official notification is needed to resolve this.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 5231 (rice)

Search note: I ran four web searches. The Seednet portal and CSC release minutes did not come up in any result, so every finding below is from Syngenta and reseller pages. Variety name: the CSC name is NK 5231 and the Seednet name is NK-5231. No search result showed the Seednet name, so all findings below refer to the NK 5231 name as used by Syngenta.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The Syngenta product page gives only general claims of suitability for rainfed or irrigated conditions and no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The Syngenta pages list no resistance ratings. The only related item is a pocket-insert leaflet PDF, which I could not open. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/nk-5231

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Syngenta page lists the season as kharif, sowing between 15 May and 15 July, a crop duration of 120 to 125 days, a seed rate of 5 to 6 kg per acre, and spacing of 20 cm between rows and 15 cm between plants. It is described as mid-early duration with bold grain, more grains per panicle, and consistent adaptability. No multi-location trial data was found. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage is not stated in any source, and no marker or QTL study was found. (The search results include a Syngenta NK 5251 page, which is a different variety.) -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developer: Syngenta India Pvt. Ltd., as given in the CSC record. The Syngenta product pages name no lead breeder, scientist or development station. The breeder-focused search returned only unrelated foreign patent and syndicated pages. No breeder name was found. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/nk-5231

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. No email, phone or postal address for Syngenta India or its rice division appeared in the search results. The only location found is a reseller in Narayanpur, Assam (Nabarak Beej Bhandar), which is not an institute contact. Please check the Syngenta India contact page directly. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers on NK 5231 were found. The ICAR 2024-25 annual report that came up in the trial search does not mention this variety in the extracts I could read. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- A reseller listing (Nabarak Beej Bhandar, Narayanpur, Assam) offers a 10 kg pack of the variety as in stock, with the listing ID 2855772639455. Availability and pricing were not checked with the seller. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or official seed-sales source was found. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The CSC raw record lists Assam. The Syngenta product page does not name any state. It gives only "major rice-growing areas" and says the variety suits rainfed or irrigated rice. Assam is therefore supported only by the CSC record and the reseller location, not by the company's own recommendation. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

Release year -- The CSC record gives 2 August 2024. I could not find a notification gazette or Seednet entry to confirm it. Parentage is not specified in any source.

DATA ISSUES TO RESOLVE

- The Seednet entry NK 16520 is listed under crop "PADDY (DHAN)", while the variety is maize. Either the Seednet mapping is wrong or it refers to a different product. The two names should not be treated as the same record until checked on seednet.gov.in.
- The "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" evidence could not be separated, because no search returned results for either name.

NEXT STEPS
Re-run the four searches once the tool is available: "NK 6240 maize variety", "NK 6240 maize breeder institute", "NK 6240 maize research" and "NK 6240 maize seed availability", plus a Seednet check for NK 16520. Priority sources would be seednet.gov.in, the CSC/ICAR release minutes, KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Maize reports.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 16520 (rice / PADDY (DHAN), code A01022150)

Searches run (4 of 4 allowed): (1) "NK 16520 rice variety"; (2) "NK 16520 rice breeder developed by institute"; (3) "NK 16520 rice research paper trial"; (4) "NK 16520 paddy seed availability". None of the returned pages contained "NK 16520", "IR58025", or "Syngenta" in the text. The results were general rice-genetics material (an iconic-varieties special issue, IRRI's Rice Breeding Innovations department, a system-of-rice-intensification trial of unnamed varieties, and a seed-availability list of other paddy varieties). I discarded all of them as not about this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. No search result described drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for NK 16520.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No search result described blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance for NK 16520.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for NK 16520 were returned. The only trial-type result was a sixteen-variety SRI trial that does not name NK 16520 in the retrieved text.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage in the supplied record (female IR58025A, maintainer IR58025B) was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No search result named a breeder or scientist for NK 16520. Syngenta India Limited is the institution in the supplied record only; no search result confirmed it as developer.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The only address on record is the supplied institution address (Syngenta India Limited, Amar Paradigm, S.No.110/11/3, Baner Road, Pune-411 045). It comes from the input, not from a search result, and no email, phone, or contact page was found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming NK 16520 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned lists for other paddy varieties from a non-NK source; no NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for NK 16520 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in search. The supplied record lists Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Telangana, but no search result confirmed this. Treat it as unverified until checked against CSC release minutes or the Seednet portal.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) directly for code A01022150, obtain the CSC/ICAR release notification for 2019, and ask Syngenta India for breeder contact and trial data. These sources were not reachable with the search tool used here.
