search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Blast resistance: RC Maniphou-12 is described as resistant to leaf and neck blast under natural disease pressure in Manipur -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Blast and false smut: a second description in the same Indian Farming article says it is tolerant to leaf and neck blast and false smut under natural conditions in Manipur -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Flood: no submergence or flood-tolerance trait is stated. The article only reports that a short-duration RC Maniphou-12 seed was offered free to flood-affected farmers in Manipur -- https://assamtribune.com/40000-hectares-of-farm-land-under-floodwater
Flood (second report): RC Maniphou-12 is described as a short-duration variety harvestable in about 100 days, offered to flood-affected farmers. This conflicts with the 130-day maturity in the ICAR article -- https://pothashang.in/2017/07/12000-metric-tons-rice-available-distribution-cm/
Drought, heat, salinity: No evidence found. The search returned only unrelated QTL and drought studies (e.g., qtl12.1 on Vandana/Way Rarem) that do not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Leaf and neck blast resistance and false smut tolerance (see STRESS TOLERANCE) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Insect pests: No evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Plant type: semi-dwarf, about 100 cm tall, about 11 effective tillers per hill, improved cooking quality with ASV value 6 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Maturity: medium-maturing, about 130 days -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Photoperiod: photo-insensitive -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Yield potential conflict: one ICAR article gives 4.5–5 t/ha with 11% amylose -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067 ; the other gives 7–8 t/ha and about 250 filled grains per panicle -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Farm-level yield gain: in an Imphal West participatory seed production study of 50 farmers, RC-Maniphou-12 yield was reported at 3.5 t/ha under local cultivars versus 4.5 t/ha under the ICAR variety, a 28.5% increase -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373490735_Impact_of_ICAR-participatory_seed_production_on_the_income_of_the_small-holders_farmers'_in_Imphal_West_district_of_Manipur_India
Multi-variety trial: ICAR Manipur reports RC Maniphou-7, 10, 12 and 13 yielded 5.6–6.8 t/ha in trials; the figure is not separated for RC Maniphou-12 -- https://nenow.in/north-east-news/manipur/manipur-cm-reviews-icar-roadmap-to-boost-agricultural-productivity-and-food-security.html

GENETICS AND QTL
Grain quality: soft cooking quality with original Chakhao grain quality -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Parentage: No evidence found. The parentage field is "Not specified" and no retrieved page gives a cross.
QTL/markers: No evidence found. The blast-resistance QTL study (qLNBL-5 and qLNBL-7) names RC Maniphou-10, not RC Maniphou-12, so it is excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332875547_On-Farm_Multilocation_Adaptability_Trial_of_Promising_Rice_Genotypes_across_Manipur

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Manipur Centre, Lamphelpat, Imphal; the RC Maniphou series is credited to this centre -- https://nenow.in/north-east-news/manipur/manipur-icar-develops-12-new-rice-varieties-for-northeast.html
Lead breeder for RC Maniphou-12: No evidence found. Dr Konsam Sarika is credited with RC Manichakhao-1, not RC Maniphou-12, so she is not attributed here -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/icar-manipur-centre-releases-indias-first-high-yielding-semi-dwarf-black-rice-variety-rc
Seed multiplication: the centre worked on RC Maniphou-12 seed multiplication with farmers under participatory seed production (2012 press item) -- https://sri.cals.cornell.edu/news/yearlynews/2012.html
Institutional scope: the centre has developed 12 RC Maniphou series rice varieties -- https://eastmojo.com/free-digest/2025/11/06/manipur-hosts-field-day-to-bridge-farmer-scientist-gap-on-rice-cultivation/

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute profile (Manipur Centre): Dr. Ramgopal Laha, HoRC and Principal Scientist (Veterinary Parasitology), phone 9612918346, email rglaha@gmail.com; address ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Manipur Centre, Lamphelpat-795004 -- https://icarneh.icar.gov.in/Profile/Manipur_Profile.html
Institute address alternative: one ICAR document gives Imphal 795 001 for the same centre -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Regional headquarters: Director, ICAR Complex for NEH Region, Umroi Road, Barapani-793103 -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/15035
Breeder-level contact for RC Maniphou-12: No evidence found. The directory lists scientists whose names are not linked to this variety, so none is given here.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in the retrieved text (2023 or nearby, year not stated). Status and dimension of rice production in Manipur: an analysis of the yield gap. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373452977_STATUS_AND_DIMENSION_OF_RICE_PRODUCTION_IN_MANIPUR_-An_analysis_of_the_yield_gap

SEED AVAILABILITY
Participatory seed production: KVK Thoubal included RC Maniphou-12 among varieties in its participatory rice seed production programme -- https://www.kvkthoubal.org/home/page/14/participatory-rice-seed-production

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME/CROP NOTE -- The variety code RAUF-17 and the blast-resistant finger millet description refer to Rajendra Madua-1 (a finger millet). The Seednet name Rajendra Mahsuri-1 is a paddy variety (BR51-46/Mahsuri cross). The parentage in the input record matches Rajendra Mahsuri-1, not Madua-1. Findings below are labelled by which name they refer to. No evidence was found that the input parentage, the 2025-03-13 release date, or the PADDY (DHAN) seed category applies to Madua-1.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Madua-1: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches returned only general finger millet descriptions, such as a general claim that the crop is hardy and adapted to harsh conditions, which is not specific to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370599648_Blast_disease_A_threat_to_finger_millet_cultivation
Mahsuri-1: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Crop-model results show that water stress during the reproductive stage cuts yield by 43 percent, so the variety is sensitive to that stress, not tolerant of it. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10333-020-00799-3

DISEASE AND PEST
Madua-1: Described as a high-yielding, blast-resistant finger millet variety. -- https://www.nabi.res.in/profile/scientists?id=MzI1 (also https://sites.google.com/rpcau.ac.in/rn-bahuguna/curriculum-vitae)
Madua-1: Gamma-irradiated mutants of this variety were screened for blast over 41,032 M2 plants, and 125 showed higher resistance than the unirradiated parent. This shows the parent's blast status but does not give its resistance rating. -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/09553002.2026.2669162
Madua-1: No evidence found for pest resistance (stem borer, weevil or caterpillar) specific to this variety. -- searched via the blast and general finger millet pages above
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Resistant to brown planthopper and leaffolders, and moderately resistant to sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/004/291/004291981.php
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Moderately resistant to sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight. -- https://rpcau.ac.in/academics/departments/department-of-plant-breeding-and-genetics/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Madua-1: Plant height 105-116 cm, erect, light green leaves, brown panicle. Release recorded as 2025. -- https://rpcau.ac.in/academics/departments/department-of-plant-breeding-and-genetics/
Madua-1: No evidence found for maturity duration, yield levels or multi-location trial results. -- searched via the RPCAU department page and the blast studies above
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Semi-dwarf (100-110 cm), 140-150 days, medium to shallow lowland, yield about 55 q/ha. The name appears under the 2004 release in the notified-varieties table. -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Long duration (145-150 days), suited to shallow lowland, yield potential 50-60 q/ha. Notification year given as 2002. -- https://rpcau.ac.in/academics/departments/department-of-plant-breeding-and-genetics/
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): In medium-land and shallow-lowland trials it yielded 5.0 t/ha and 4.9 t/ha, above the check varieties. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/004/291/004291981.php
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): The university annual report lists it as a local check in several trials, with yields of about 3472 and 4608 kg/ha. The planting-date yields of 31.6 and 24.8 q/ha are in a fragmentary passage and are not confirmed as this variety's trial results. -- https://www.rpcau.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Detail-Annual-Report-2018-19.pdf
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Crop-model study found optimum transplanting in June and crop residue of up to 2500 kg/ha raised yield by about 22 percent. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10333-020-00799-3

GENETICS AND QTL
Madua-1: No evidence found for QTL or marker-trait mapping of this variety itself. The gamma-mutant study used SSR markers on mutants derived from it. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42207999/
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Developed from the cross BR51-46/Mahsuri (designated RAU83-500). -- https://eurekamag.com/research/004/291/004291981.php
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): No evidence found for QTL or marker studies. -- searched via the publication results above

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Madua-1: The developing institution is Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University (RPCAU), Pusa, Samastipur, Bihar. -- https://rpcau.ac.in/academics/departments/department-of-plant-breeding-and-genetics/
Madua-1: Scientist R. N. Bahuguna's CV states he contributed to the development of this variety. This is a contributor statement, not a confirmed lead-breeder designation. -- https://sites.google.com/rpcau.ac.in/rn-bahuguna/curriculum-vitae
Madua-1: A NABI scientist profile states that the profile holder, as part of the wheat biofortification team, helped develop this variety. The name on that page was not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://nabi.res.in/profile/scientists?id=MzI1
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Authors of the 2004 IRRN release note are V. N. Sahai, S. Ghosh and R. C. Chaudhary. The release note does not name the breeder as lead developer. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/004/291/004291981.php
Mahsuri-1 (Seednet name): Developed by the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, RPCAU. -- https://rpcau.ac.in/academics/departments/department-of-plant-breeding-and-genetics/

CONTACT DETAILS
Madua-1 and Mahsuri-1 (institute-level only; no breeder contact found): Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, Pusa, Samastipur - 848 125, Bih

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest for salinity tolerance.

flood.details: The variety was developed for flood-prone rainfed lowlands of Assam, where flash floods cause severe establishment losses. The digest gives no separate quantified flood-tolerance measurement; the documented flood-related tolerance is the submergence tolerance reported in the submergence section. The medium rating reflects this targeted development context and the absence of direct flood-specific data.

disease_resistance.summary: No variety-specific disease resistance evidence was found in the digest. A general review notes that Sub1 varieties remain susceptible to several diseases and other abiotic stresses, and that breeding must address these. No specific diseases are named and no resistance is documented.

pest_resistance.summary: No variety-specific pest resistance evidence was found in the digest. Pest reaction is unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: AAU listing: 5-5.5 t/ha. On-farm trials: about 100% more yield than the local check. Morigaon demonstrations (2020-21, 157 ha, 430 farmers): pooled yield 20.04% higher than farmers' varieties. Lakhimpur (2018-19 and 2019-20): benefit-cost ratio 1.58 and 1.54 versus 1.31 and 1.35 for the farmers' variety; net returns Rs 24,460 and Rs 24,600 versus Rs 9,700 and Rs 10,698. The original record's average_yield field ('Kg/Ha') has no numeric value.
agronomic_details.stability: Submergence survival was reported across multiple districts and seasons: Nalbari and Morigaon (9-12 days), Morigaon KVK 2016 (12 days), and Lakhimpur 2018-19 and 2019-20 (up to 15 days). Yield advantage was reported in on-farm and demonstration settings. No formal multi-environment yield stability analysis is in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Lowland, rainfed flood-prone ecosystems of Assam; sali/kharif season (AAU listing).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Foreground and background marker-assisted selection was used. The selected BC2F2 line (Ranjit-Sub1) had 96.54% recurrent-parent (background) genome recovery. Marker positions beyond the donor segment size are not given in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Sub1 QTL introgressed into Ranjit by modified marker-assisted backcrossing. Donor segment is about 1.65 Mb. The selected line showed tolerance similar to the Sub1 donor parent. Foreground and background selection were combined with 62 DUS characters to maintain recurrent-parent identity.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified in the evidence digest beyond the Sub1 QTL introgression.

AAU listing rates it tolerant up to 2 weeks of submergence. The tolerance is similar to the Sub1 donor parent in the selected BC2F2 line (see genetics section).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- ADT 57 (CSC name) is reported as resistant to blast, moderately resistant to sheath blight and brown plant hopper, and field-tolerant to brown spot -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/ADT57.html
- ADT 51 (Seednet name, different accession AD 09367) is reported as blast-resistant and moderately resistant to leaf folder, stem borer, BPH, sheath blight and sheath rot -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/967
- ADT 51 is also reported as moderately resistant to stem borer, leaf folder, gall midge, BPH and WBPH under field conditions -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/ADT%2051.html
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to ADT 57 or ADT 51.

DISEASE AND PEST
- ADT 57: blast resistance, moderate sheath blight and BPH resistance, brown spot field tolerance -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/ADT57.html
- ADT 51: blast resistance, moderate resistance to leaf folder, stem borer, BPH, sheath blight, sheath rot -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/ADT%2051.html
- ADT 51 farmer opinion: tolerance to major pests and diseases reduces input needs -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372770412_Rice_ADT_51_-_A_high_yielding_long_duration_rice_variety_suitable_for_Samba_season_in_Cauvery_Delta_Zone_of_Tamil_Nadu

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- ADT 57: duration 115-120 days; season Kar/Kuruvai/Navarai/Summer; average grain yield 6502 kg/ha; high milling out-turn (64.9%); intermediate amylose; LER 1.6 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/ADT57.html
- ADT 57: duration 130-135 days and yield 6-7.5 t/ha on a low-reliability aggregator page, which conflicts with the TNAU duration; treat as unverified -- https://agri.bot/docs/duration-and-average-yield-for-adt-57-paddy-variety
- ADT 57: suitable for direct sowing -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news
- ADT 51 (AD 09367, BPT 5204 / Improved White Ponni): duration 155-160 days, Samba (August sowing), average yield 6533 kg/ha, 1000-grain weight 23.9 g -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/ADT%2051.html
- ADT 51 trial: highest yield 10036 kg/ha at Thiruvisanallur, Thanjavur, in an OFT -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/967
- ADT 51 is non-lodging in heavy rain (January 2021) compared with CR 1009 Sub1 -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/swc/RICE.pdf
- No ADT 57 multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Searches returned no QTL, marker or genomic study naming ADT 57 or ADT 51 (the parentage "ADT (R) 45 / ACK 03002" is from the TNAU page above, not a genetic study).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- ADT 57 breeder: No evidence found. The searches returned no named breeder for ADT 57.
- ADT 57 institution: Tamil Nadu Rice Research Institute (TRRI), Aduthurai, TNAU; TRRI recommended ADT 57 among kuruvai varieties -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news
- Institute-level unit: Plant Breeding and Genetics unit, TRRI, works on rice ecosystem varieties and seed supply -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/trri/ci
- ADT 51 breeder (Seednet name, different accession): Suresh Ramalingam, TNAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372770412_Rice_ADT_51_-_A_high_yielding_long_duration_rice_variety_suitable_for_Samba_season_in_Cauvery_Delta_Zone_of_Tamil_Nadu
- Institute-level unit head listed as Dr. R. Saraswathi, Professor (PBG); this is not linked to ADT 57 or ADT 51 -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/trri/ci

CONTACT DETAILS
- Tamil Nadu Rice Research Institute, Aduthurai (institute-level; no breeder contact found): phone 0435-2472108 / 2472098; email dirtrri@tnau.ac.in -- http://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf (dated 31.07.2021; verify before use)
- Location: Aduthurai, Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news
- Postal address and breeder email: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Aarthi et al. (2023). Characterization and Identification of Recent Rice varieties through Chemo-Taxonomical Test (includes ADT-57 among ten varieties tested). Biological Forum 15(8a): 300-306 -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Characterization-and-Identification-of-Recent-Rice-varieties-through-Chemo-Taxonomical-Test-N-Aarthi-49.pdf
- Ramalingam S. (2026). Rice ADT 51 - A high yielding long duration rice variety suitable for Samba season in Cauvery Delta Zone of Tamil Nadu. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 11(3): 721-726 (ADT 51, Seednet name; only Suresh Ramalingam is shown as author in the source) -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/967
- AICRIP/ICAR and KrishiKosh items for ADT 57: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- ADT 51: 700 units (quantity unit not stated) listed at TRRI Aduthurai in TNAU seed stock as on 31.07.2021 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- ADT 51 and ADT 52 were listed for breeder-seed indent and certified-seed production in the 2021 Scientific Workers Conference proceedings -- http://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/swc/RICE.pdf
- ADT 57: No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or dealer listings.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu only (per input). TRRI recommended ADT 57 among kuruvai varieties; the Tamil Nadu Agriculture crop-climate page lists ADT 53, CO 51, ADT 43, ADT (R) 45 and others for kuruvai but does not list ADT 57 -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news ; https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/01_Rice.pdf
- Release year 2022 (CSC) is not confirmed by any search result for ADT 57. The TNAU ADT 51 release year is given as 2017 or 2018 in different sources, so the Seednet record may refer to a different year or accession -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-aduthurai/varieties-released/

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Department of Rice, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics,  Tamil Nadu Agricultural University,  Coimbatore – 641 003.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated condition as a transplanted crop in Sornavari/Kar/kuruvai/Navaria seasons of Tamil Nadu.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Lodging : Non lodging Shattering : non shattering Seasons : Sornavari/Kar/kuruvai/navarai seasons Seed rate: 20 kg/ha under normal conditions. 5 kg/ha under SRI Age of seedling: 22-25 days under normal conditions 14-15 days under SRI. CB o6 535 was evaluated under SRI system of cultivation in KHARIF 2010-11 at Coimbatore. The culture recorded higher yield under SRI than normal method. The culture recorded better agronomic efficiency (37.2 and 48.3% under normal and SRI respectively) than the check variety ADT 3 (30.5 and 33.5% under normal and SRI systems). The culture possesses higher physiological efficiency by registering higher crop growth rate, leaf areas Index, better light transmission ratio, spikelet fertility, Dry matter production and Harvest Index.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height (cm)  - 90-100 cm, - Distinguishing morphological characters - Early plant vigour -Good, -  coleoptiles- Green, - basal leaf sheath colour - Green, - leaf sheath - Green, - leaf blade colour - Green, - leaf Pubescence - Intermediate, - leaf length - 35.0 cm(5.0 mm), - leaf width, - 2.00 cm, -Days to 50% flowering, - 75-80 days, - Panicle exertion - Exerted panicle, - Stigma colour - White, -  Apiculus colour - Light green, - Number of effective tillers - 15-18, - Panicle length- 23-28 cm
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress:
Abiotic – Not tested 
Biotic – reaction to pests and diseases  furnished in Para 8 (e) and 8 (f)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
The culture CB 06 535 was screened against all the epidemic diseases viz., blast, bacterial blight, sheath rot, saheat blight, brown spot and rice tungro disease (RTD) under artificially inoculated conditions during 2009, 2010 and 2011. The culture CB 06 535 is found to be moderately resistant to blast (scale 5), in 1 to 9 scale. The corresponding scores for ADT 43 are 7 or 9 scale for all the disease.
Under AICRIP, the culture was screened in NSN-1 and DSN-1, wherein CB 06 535 was found to be moderately resistant to blast.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests:
The culture CB 06535  was evaluated for three years (2009, 10 & 11) at Coimbatore,k Madurai and Aduthurai against the major pests and the culture CB 06 535 was moderately resistant to GLH (5) asn BPH (3) 

Under AICRIP, the culture was screened during 2010, CB 06 535 was found to be moderately resistant to WBPH, leaf folder and stem borer.

drought.details: No drought tolerance was found for CO 51 in the searched sources. The variety is described as semi-dwarf and early with a 105-110 day duration. The original record states abiotic stress was not tested.

heat.details: Flowering peaks around 10:30-11:30 a.m. CO 51 showed higher spikelet sterility than an early-morning-flowering line, indicating heat vulnerability at flowering. A marker-assisted backcross version with early-morning flowering was developed to escape heat.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: No flood tolerance was found for CO 51 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: moderately resistant under artificial conditions (culture CB 06 535), also listed as moderate in the TNAU release sheet. Bacterial blight: the TNAU Rice Technologies page lists multiple resistance to blast, BPH and bacterial blight (BB), but this conflicts with the moderate resistance in the release sheet and is not confirmed elsewhere. Sheath rot, sheath blight, brown spot and rice tungro disease: CB 06 535 was tested under artificial inoculation in 2009, 2010 and 2011, but the retrieved text does not give scores, so resistance levels are Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper (BPH): moderate resistance under artificial conditions (culture CB 06 535) and listed as moderate in the TNAU release sheet. Green leafhopper (GLH): moderate resistance under artificial conditions and listed as moderate in the TNAU release sheet.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean yield of 6623 kg/ha over seven years of trials, 10.72% above ADT 43. Highest recorded trial yield was 11,377 kg/ha at Nallampalli, Dharmapuri.
agronomic_details.stability: Mean yield was reported over seven years of trials. Stability indices were not found in the digest. Agronomic efficiency was higher than ADT 43 under both normal and SRI methods.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated condition as a transplanted crop in Sornavari, Kar, Kuruvai and Navarai seasons of Tamil Nadu. Seed rate is 20 kg/ha under normal conditions and 5 kg/ha under SRI, with seedling age of 22-25 days (normal) or 14-15 days (SRI).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf and early. Non-lodging and non-shattering. Medium slender white rice with 69% milling and 63% head rice recovery, and intermediate amylose (about 22%).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Seven years of trials gave a mean yield of 6623 kg/ha, 10.72% above ADT 43. The highest trial yield was 11,377 kg/ha at Nallampalli, Dharmapuri. Agronomic efficiency was higher than ADT 43 under both normal and SRI methods. Suitability was reported for Kar, Kuruvai, Sornavari and Navarai seasons in Tamil Nadu. Multi-location testing of herbicide-tolerant near-isogenic lines was found in the digest, but these are not CO 51 and were excluded to avoid misattribution.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Marker-assisted backcrossing was used for herbicide-tolerance loci and for the early-morning-flowering version, but no marker names, positions or SSR/SNP details were given.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL mapping study specific to CO 51 was found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed herbicide-tolerance loci from donor ROBIN-HTM into CO 51. Specific genes and pathways were not identified in the digest. Parentage is ADT 43 / RR 272-1745; the cross was made in Kharif 2003 and stabilised at F5 as CB 06 535.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Rice CO 51 (CSC minutes name "Rice CO 51"; Seednet name "Rice CO 51", not verified because seednet.gov.in did not appear in results; TNAU also uses "CO 51", "CO(R) 51", "TNAU Rice CO 51 (IET 21605)" and culture code "CB 06 535")

Discrepancy: the record gives release date 2016-08-12, but TNAU and journal sources say the variety was released in 2013. The sources also differ on the number of states (12 in the record, "14 states" in the MDPI paper).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Sources describe the variety as semi-dwarf and early, with 105-110 day duration; no drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was found for CO 51. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/variety_release_2013.pdf
- Heat: flowering peaks around 10:30-11:30 a.m., and CO 51 showed higher spikelet sterility than an early-morning-flowering line, so it is heat-vulnerable at flowering. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/13/3/553

DISEASE AND PEST
- The culture CB 06 535 is moderately resistant to blast, BPH and GLH under artificial condition. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- Moderate resistance to blast, brown planthopper and green leafhopper is also listed in the TNAU release sheet. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/variety_release_2013.pdf
- The TNAU Rice Technologies page lists "multiple resistance to blast, BPH & BB" (bacterial blight). This conflicts with the "moderate" resistance in the release sheet; bacterial blight is not confirmed elsewhere. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
- Under artificially inoculated conditions in 2009, 2010 and 2011, CB 06 535 was tested against sheath rot, sheath blight, brown spot and rice tungro disease. The retrieved text does not give the scores for these diseases. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227 (pdf: https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/2598/f8361d7e6dc3e8268a273066b5989323fe8b.pdf)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mean yield of 6623 kg/ha over seven years of trials, 10.72% above ADT 43. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- Highest recorded trial yield was 11,377 kg/ha at Nallampalli, Dharmapuri. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- Grain quality and milling: medium slender white rice, 69% milling and 63% head rice recovery, intermediate amylose (about 22%). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/variety_release_2013.pdf
- Suitable for Kar, Kuruvai, Sornavari and Navarai seasons in Tamil Nadu. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- Agronomic efficiency was higher than ADT 43 under both normal and SRI methods. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334196659_TNAU_Rice_CO_51_IET_21605_-_A_high_yielding_short_duration_fine_grain_rice_variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Multi-location testing of two herbicide-tolerant near-isogenic lines (CBHTR22001 and CBHTR22002) gave 20.2% and 22.4% higher yield than CO 51. -- https://www.researchgate.net/institution/Tamil-Nadu-Agricultural-University

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage ADT 43 / RR 272-1745; the cross was made in Kharif 2003 and stabilised at F5 as CB 06 535. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334196659_TNAU_Rice_CO_51_IET_21605_-_A_high_yielding_short_duration_fine_grain_rice_variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed herbicide-tolerance loci from donor ROBIN-HTM into CO 51. -- https://www.researchgate.net/institution/Tamil-Nadu-Agricultural-University
- Marker-assisted backcross breeding was used to develop an early-morning-flowering version of CO 51 for heat escape. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/13/3/553
- No QTL mapping study specific to CO 51 was found. "No evidence found" for QTL mapping.

drought.details: Multiple Sahyadri rice variants demonstrate high drought tolerance. Sahyadri 2 is described as a short duration drought tolerant rice suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. The broader Sahyadri 1 to 4 series, Sahyadri Brahma, and Sahyadri Megha are also noted for drought tolerance or screening for drought tolerance. Sahyadri Brahma is specifically mentioned as a drought and submergence tolerant variety.

heat.details: Several Sahyadri rice hybrids exhibit high heat stress tolerance. Sahyadri Brahma, Sahyadri 1, Sahyadri 2, Sahyadri 3, and Sahyadri 5 are identified as heat tolerant or suitable for yield enhancement under heat stress conditions. Researchers at ICAR-IIRR work on heat stress tolerance in rice, specifically mentioning Sahyadri Brahma.

salinity.details: Sahyadri 2 (Vashisthi) is highly tolerant to salinity conditions and is suitable for saline soils of the Konkan region. Sahyadri 2 is also described as a new salt-tolerant rice variety for India. Sahyadri Kempumukthi is a salt-tolerant and multiple stress tolerant variety developed by Dr. S.L. Krishnamurthy. Sahyadri Brahma is noted as a flood and salt tolerant paddy variety.

flood.details: Sahyadri rice varieties, particularly Sahyadri 1 to 4, are identified as flood tolerant varieties. Sahyadri is noted as tolerant to other forms of flooding, including stagnant flooding. Sahyadri Brahma is described as a flood and salt tolerant paddy variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Sahyadri rice varieties, including Sahyadri and KRH 2, are reported to be resistant to Bacterial Blight (BB).

pest_resistance.summary: Sahyadri rice varieties, including Sahyadri and KRH 2, are reported to be resistant to Brown Planthopper (BPH).

agronomic_details.yield: Sahyadri 2 demonstrated a 10.5% increase in grain yield over the check variety Karjat 4 in front-line demonstrations during the 2004-05 rabi season. No absolute quantitative yield figures are provided in the search results.
agronomic_details.stability: The widespread recommendation and demonstration of various Sahyadri rice variants across diverse stress conditions and regions suggest broad adaptability and potentially good stability, but explicit stability performance data across environments is not provided.

drought.details: Multiple Sahyadri rice variants demonstrate high drought tolerance. Sahyadri 2 is described as a short duration drought tolerant rice suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. The broader Sahyadri 1 to 4 series, Sahyadri Brahma, and Sahyadri Megha are also noted for drought tolerance or screening for drought tolerance. Sahyadri Brahma is specifically mentioned as a drought and submergence tolerant variety.

heat.details: Several Sahyadri rice hybrids exhibit high heat stress tolerance. Sahyadri Brahma, Sahyadri 1, Sahyadri 2, Sahyadri 3, and Sahyadri 5 are identified as heat tolerant or suitable for yield enhancement under heat stress conditions. Researchers at ICAR-IIRR work on heat stress tolerance in rice, specifically mentioning Sahyadri Brahma.

salinity.details: Sahyadri 2 (Vashisthi) is highly tolerant to salinity conditions and is suitable for saline soils of the Konkan region. Sahyadri 2 is also described as a new salt-tolerant rice variety for India. Sahyadri Kempumukthi is a salt-tolerant and multiple stress tolerant variety developed by Dr. S.L. Krishnamurthy. Sahyadri Brahma is noted as a flood and salt tolerant paddy variety.

flood.details: Sahyadri rice varieties, particularly Sahyadri 1 to 4, are identified as flood tolerant varieties. Sahyadri is noted as tolerant to other forms of flooding, including stagnant flooding. Sahyadri Brahma is described as a flood and salt tolerant paddy variety.

submergence.details: Sahyadri 2 demonstrates one week of submergence tolerance and is suitable for semi-deep water conditions. Sahyadri Brahma is a drought and submergence tolerant variety and acts as a donor for anaerobic germination tolerance, which is crucial for survival under submerged conditions. Sahyadri 4 is recognized for submergence tolerance, and Sahyadri Megha has been screened for submergence and anaerobic germination tolerance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE --
No evidence found for Swarna Madhu (litchi) or SAMPADH SWARNA (paddy/dhan) on drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence. The only stress-related litchi lines found concern a different cultivar, Swarna Roopa: fruit-cracking resistance and high TSS -- https://thehillstimes.in/web-stories/best-litchi-varieties-in-india
The paddy results (Swarna Samriddhi Dhan, Swarna Sukha Dhan) are different varieties and are not evidence for SAMPADH SWARNA -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/131717 and https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/143280/53178/391485

DISEASE AND PEST --
No evidence found for Swarna Madhu or SAMPADH SWARNA. Swarna Roopa is reported as resistant to fruit cracking, and a source names fruit-splitting resistance for Swarna Roopa (IIHR page, Hindi) -- https://www.iihr.res.in/hi/litchi-swarna-roopa
No paddy disease or pest data for SAMPADH SWARNA was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
No evidence found for Swarna Madhu field trials, yield, or maturity. Swarna Roopa is described as a mid-season cultivar, with fruits maturing by the third week of May and 8-20 fruits per cluster -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/litchi-breeding/232350922
Swarna Roopa is also described as a shy-to-moderate yielder, with 50-60 kg/tree in one source -- https://nhb.gov.in/pdf/fruits/litchi/lit013.pdf
These figures are for Swarna Roopa, not the target.
No paddy agronomy for SAMPADH SWARNA was found.

GENETICS AND QTL --
No evidence found for Swarna Madhu or SAMPADH SWARNA. Swarna Roopa is described as a clonal selection from seedless-group material at CHES Ranchi -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/litchi-breeding/232350922
Possible name confusion: "Madhu" litchi lines found (Sabour Madhu, H-105, a Purbi x Bedana hybrid released 1997 by BAU Sabour) are a different cultivar -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352763015_Subtropical_Fruit_Varieties_AICRP_STF_Mango_Guava_Litchi_and_Grapes

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION --
No evidence found naming a breeder or developing scientist for Swarna Madhu.
The only Ranchi litchi origin found is Swarna Roopa, credited to CHES (Central Horticultural Experiment Station), Ranchi -- https://www.thedailyjagran.com/trending/list-of-popular-varieties-of-litchi-found-in-india-shahi-litchi-to-seedless-know-their-origin-quality-market-price-and-more-10238886
The record's institution, ICAR RCER Farming System Research Centre for Hill and Plateau Region, was not found in any source.
No breeder or institution evidence found for SAMPADH SWARNA.

CONTACT DETAILS --
No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL for ICAR RCER FSR Centre (Hill and Plateau Region) or CHES Ranchi appeared in the four searches. Searching the institute's own website (icar-rcer.org.in or the ICAR directory) is needed.

PUBLICATIONS --
No evidence found for Swarna Madhu or SAMPADH SWARNA. Items below concern other cultivars and are context only:
Singh, U. (year not shown). Scientific Cultivation of Litchi. In: Scientific Cultivation of Tropical Fruit Crops, pp. 117-130, A K International Publication -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/401306538_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Litchi
Authors not shown in source (2021 or later). Seventy five years of research and development in Litchi. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361054810_Seventy_five_years_of_research_and_development_in_Litchi
Mohapatra, S., Panda, A.K., Bastia, A.K., Mukherjee, A.K., Sanghamitra, P., Meher, J., Mohanty, S.P., and Pradhan, S.K. (2021). Development of Submergence-Tolerant, Bacterial Blight-Resistant, and High-Yielding Near Isogenic Lines of Popular Variety, 'Swarna' Through Marker-Assisted Breeding Approach. Frontiers in Plant Science, DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.672618 -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.672618/full (paddy 'Swarna' line, not SAMPADH SWARNA)

SEED AVAILABILITY --
No evidence found for Swarna Madhu or SAMPADH SWARNA from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, or dealers. Swarna Roopa plants are listed by a nursery in West Bengal, which is not the target -- https://m.indiamart.com/proddetail/swarna-roopa-litchi-plant-2851949455762.html
Unrelated paddy listings named "Swarna" (MTU-7029, SS-511, Sub-1) were found, but none is SAMPADH SWARNA -- https://www.porwalhybridseeds.com/paddy-seeds.html

RECOMMENDED STATES --
No evidence found for Jharkhand as a recommended state for Swarna Madhu. Swarna Roopa is described as suitable for the Chotanagpur plateau -- https://nhb.gov.in/pdf/fruits/litchi/lit013.pdf
Swarna Roopa is a different cultivar. The Jharkhand-recommended paddy variety Swarna Sukha Dhan (IET 24692) is also a different variety -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/143280/53178/391485

NAME MISMATCH NOTE --
The CSC name "Swarna Madhu" (litchi) and the Seednet name "SAMPADH SWARNA" (paddy) were both searched. Neither returned a matching record. The evidence above refers to other varieties, so it should not be attached to this record. Verify the CSC notification and the Seednet entry directly, and check the crop mapping.

One JSS KVK note says MSN-99 suits both the onset and last rains and gives yield sooner (the variety was developed as an alternative to the small rice variety RNR-15048, and it will provide yield sooner and is suitable during both the onset and last rains) -- https://jssonline.org/new-paddy-variety-msn-99-introduced-in-maagudilu-village/ . This is a farmer-facing statement, not a trial result.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for MSN 99 specifically. Context only: the ZARS Mandya profile reports screening for resistance to BPH, leaf blast and neck blast across the station's germplasm, not for MSN 99 -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

drought.details: No search result gives drought data for blackgram OBG 33 (Shashi). The 'Sashi' drought results refer to other crops. The rice variety Sashi (IET-14105, IR-50 x Patnai-23) is listed in the ICAR rice database, and jute Sashi (JRC-532) is described as tolerant to drought and waterlogging. Neither can be attributed to the blackgram variety. The parentage 'IR 50/PATNAI 23' in the blackgram record matches the rice variety Sashi, which suggests the source data may be mixed up with rice. SJR-5 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "SJR-5", so every search used the same name. Evidence below refers to SJR-5 (IET-19972) unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Four searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for SJR-5.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page describing blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, BPH, stem borer or other resistance for SJR-5 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No page gave maturity, plant height, yield, or multi-location trial data for SJR-5.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No page gave parentage (the input record also says "Not specified") or any marker or QTL study for SJR-5.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page named a breeder, developing institute or station for SJR-5. A search for "SJR-5 rice breeder developed by institute" returned general IRRI, IR8 and ICAR-IIRR pages that do not mention SJR-5, so none were attributed to it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute or station contact for SJR-5 was returned. The only ICAR-IIRR address seen (Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad 500030) appears as the affiliation of an author on an unrelated paper, so it is not attributed to SJR-5.

PUBLICATIONS:
Prasad, G. S. V. et al. (2022). Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India. Journal not visible in search snippet; SJR 5 appears only as one name in a cultivar table in the article -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2 (DOI 10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2). Note: the snippet shows only the first author's name, so the full author list and journal are unverified. The article does not describe SJR-5 itself.
No other publication, thesis, AICRP/ICAR report or KrishiKosh record for SJR-5 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for SJR-5 was returned. Results for other paddy varieties (Pusa Basmati, PB, IFFDC, OSSC lists) were discarded as not relevant.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Partial evidence only. A Bihar list of notified varieties gives "SJR-5(IET-19972) · 2011 · 10/10/2011 · S.O. 2326(E)" as a notification entry -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf. This page does not list the states. The states "Jammu, Haryana and Tamilnadu" come only from the input record and were not confirmed by any search result. The Bihar notification date (10/10/2011) differs from the input year_of_release (2011-06-28); this needs checking against the CSC minutes or the Gazette.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swarna Purvi Dhan-4 (rice)

Name note: The CSC release name "Swarna Purvi Dhan-4" appears in the search results. The Seednet name "SWARN PURBI DHAN-4" did not appear in any result, so every finding below refers to "Swarna Purvi Dhan-4". Variety code IET 29405 and parentage were not confirmed by any source. The institution, release date and state list come from the input record unless a source is cited.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Dhan-4 specifically. The IRRI-NARES list gives its type as aerobic, which describes the cultivation system, not a verified stress tolerance. -- http://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The Package of Practices for Eastern India names Dhan-4 among eastern varieties but does not identify it as resistant to any disease or pest. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The IRRI-NARES list includes Swarna Purvi Dhan-4 among 31 varieties released and notified in 2024, with long grain and suitability for Bihar, Jharkhand, Haryana and Gujarat; no yield or maturity values were in the retrieved text. -- http://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The IRRI news release describes the 31 varieties as notified in the Gazette of India in 2024 and available for large-scale cultivation; it does not name Dhan-4 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.irri.org/news-and-events/news/31-high-impact-irri-nares-developed-rice-varieties-now-available-across-india
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The eastern India Package of Practices lists Swarna Purvi Dhan 4 among rice varieties recommended for the region; no trial data are given. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ICAR Annual Report 2024-25 cites drought-tolerant Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 and 2 and Swarna Shusk Dhan, but not Dhan-4. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per the IRRI-NARES list: ICAR-RCER (ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region), in collaboration with IRRI. -- http://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ICAR-RCER release page reports the release and notification of Swarna Purvi Dhan varieties and other new paddy varieties developed by ICAR RCER, Patna; Dhan-4 is not named in the retrieved text. -- https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, theses or KrishiKosh entries specific to Dhan-4 were found in the searches.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swarna Purvi Dhan-5 (rice)

Name check: CSC release name "Swarna Purvi Dhan-5" (also "Swarna Purvi Dhan 5", IET 29036, RCPR 68-IR83929-B-B-291-2-1-1-2). Seednet name "SWARN PURBI DHAN-5" was not searched, so no finding below is confirmed under that spelling. Searches 1 to 4 used the CSC name and the IET code.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Suited to direct-seeded aerobic conditions in drought-prone rainfed and water-limiting areas in kharif, per the ICAR-released list -- https://agriculturepost.com/agri-research/crop-wise-details-of-109-varieties-of-field-and-horticultural-crops-released-by-pm-recently/
- Reported yield of 29.02 q/ha under moderate drought -- https://krishijagran.com/news/pm-modi-released-109-high-yielding-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-of-crops/
- Listed among drought-tolerant varieties for eastern India -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India
- Described as ideal for submerged stress conditions, with 38 q/ha under stress and 56 q/ha under normal conditions (conflicts with the 29.02 q/ha drought figure; treat as unverified) -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/prime-minister-modi-unveils-nine-high-yield-rice-varieties-3527
- Submergence tolerance is not confirmed for this variety. A 2010 blog attributes submergence tolerance and 150-day maturity to a variety whose identity is unclear, so it should not be used as evidence -- https://agroconsultants.blogspot.com/2010/12/agroconsultancy.html

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as a selection for resistance in eastern-India management guidance (false smut context) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India
- Moderate resistance to leaf blast is reported -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/prime-minister-modi-unveils-nine-high-yield-rice-varieties-3527
- No pest-specific data (BPH, stem borer, gall midge) found for this variety

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 110-115 days, per a 2010-11 blog on the pre-release variety; the Khetivyapar source gives 120-125 days. Conflicting, so confirm with the notification document -- https://agroconsultants.blogspot.com/ and https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/prime-minister-modi-unveils-nine-high-yield-rice-varieties-3527
- Grain zinc 25.5 ppm and iron 13.1 ppm -- https://krishijagran.com/news/pm-modi-released-109-high-yielding-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-of-crops/
- Long slender, translucent grain -- https://agroconsultants.blogspot.com/2010/12/agroconsultancy.html
- Open-pollinated variety -- https://agriculturepost.com/agri-research/crop-wise-details-of-109-varieties-of-field-and-horticultural-crops-released-by-pm-recently/
- Multi-location trial data not found beyond the yield figures above

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree/identifier given as RCPR 68-IR83929-B-B-291-2-1-1-2; the parentage field in the record is "Not specified", and no cross or marker study was found for this variety -- https://agriculturepost.com/agri-research/crop-wise-details-of-109-varieties-of-field-and-horticultural-crops-released-by-pm-recently/
- No QTL or marker study found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna, Bihar -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/prime-minister-modi-unveils-nine-high-yield-rice-varieties-3527
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found
- Station or division within the complex: No evidence found
- IRRI reports it among 2024-notified varieties developed through IRRI-NARES collaboration; it was developed under the ICAR-IRRI/AICRP framework -- https://www.irri.org/news-and-events/news/31-high-impact-irri-nares-developed-rice-varieties-now-available-across-india

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only, as found: ICAR-Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna, Bihar (city only; no address, phone, or email in sources) -- https://agriculturepost.com/agri-research/crop-wise-details-of-109-varieties-of-field-and-horticultural-crops-released-by-pm-recently/
- The address given in the record ("ICAR Pariser, P.O. Bihar Veterinary College") was not verified by any search result
- Official email, phone, or contact-page URL: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, or KrishiKosh record specific to Swarna Purvi Dhan-5 found
- ICAR Annual Report 2024-25 mentions the variety in its list of new varieties (author: ICAR) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- Rice Package of Practices for Eastern India lists the variety for drought and disease tolerance (authors not shown in the search snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India
- Field trial and AICRP reports with the variety's yield data: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed-supply listing from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, an SAU, or the Seednet portal found
- Searches returned only generic "Swarna" paddy seed sellers (Maa Agrotech, Swarna Seeds, Bengal Seeds) that sell different varieties (e.g., Swarna Dhan IET-5656), not Swarna Purvi Dhan-5 -- https://www.indiamart.com/paddy-seed/ ; https://swarnaseeds.net/seeds.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand -- https://agriculturepost.com/agri-research/crop-wise-details-of-109-varieties-of-field-and-horticultural-crops-released-by-pm-recently/
- Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Puducherry are listed in one source, but this conflicts with the official list and should be ignored unless confirmed -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/prime-minister-modi-unveils-nine-high-yield-rice-varieties-3527

Open items: the Seednet portal entry under "SWARN PURBI DHAN-5", the CSC release minutes (notification date 2 Aug 2024 per the record), the breeder's name, and official contacts still need to be checked directly on seednet.gov.in, the ICAR-RCER site, and the CSC notification.

Scope note: Four searches were run (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). Almost none of the results refer to Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 itself. The Seednet name "SWARN PURBI DHAN" and the variety code "RCPR 19-IR 84899-B-179-13-1-1-1 / IET 24660" were not searched separately, because the four-search limit was reached. Results containing "Purvi"/"Purbi" or the code were checked, and the only matches are listed below. Where the evidence refers to a different name or line, that is stated.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found for Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 specifically. Results on drought, flood and submergence tolerance concern Swarna-Sub1 or other varieties, not this one. -- https://ricetoday.irri.org/swarna-sub1-odishas-food-for-a-goddess/ (Swarna-Sub1 only, excluded)

DISEASE AND PEST:

Matching name on Seednet ("SWARN PURBI DHAN"): not searched; no evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:

The Package of Practices lists it among varieties for eastern India, but no duration or yield is given for it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India

drought.details: Sahyadri Megha is a drought-tolerant rice variety, described as short-duration and suitable for direct-sown rainfed conditions. It is also referred to as moderately drought tolerant. A novel abiotic stress-responsive gene, LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from a drought-tolerant rice cultivar, Sahyadri Megha, indicating its genetic basis for this trait. Molecular breeding efforts aim for inbuilt drought resistance/tolerance.

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance and has been included in screenings for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: Sahyadri Megha is tolerant to salinity, and its yield and salinity tolerance in rice have been subjects of study.

flood.details: Information specifically on flood tolerance (beyond submergence) is not provided.

disease_resistance.summary: Sahyadri Megha is resistant to blast disease (a fungal disease) and highly tolerant to blast. It is also resistant to Helminthosporium spot and gall midge. Molecular breeding aims for inbuilt blast resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety is resistant to gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: 65 quintals per hectare (q/ha)
agronomic_details.stability: Suitable for both irrigated and direct-sown rainfed conditions. Recommended for the Kharif season.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Primarily adapted for cultivation in Karnataka.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Sahyadri Megha is a non-Basmati, new red variety of paddy. It is noted for being protein-rich and high in nutrients.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has undergone and been reported in various trials, including those for drought stress tolerance, heat stress tolerance, salinity tolerance, and submergence tolerance as part of the All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) and IIRR annual reports. Performance scores are reported in these proceedings, indicating its participation in multi-location evaluations.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety was developed through hybridization. Molecular breeding techniques have been utilized for the development of rice varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast.

drought.details: Sava 200 is identified as a short duration drought tolerant rice hybrid suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Molecular breeding efforts have aimed to develop varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar, and Sava 200 is listed in this context.

heat.details: The variety is tolerant to temperature stress, and high temperature tolerance has been a focus in developing abiotic tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: While salinity and osmotic stress tolerance trials are conducted within the research context, specific tolerance levels for Sava 200 are not provided in the search results.

flood.details: Sava 200 is suitable for semi-deep water conditions and exhibits tolerance to one week of submergence.

disease_resistance.summary: Sava 200 is highly resistant to Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB/LB) and neck infection. It is also tolerant/resistant to blast, rice bunt, Rice Tungro Disease (RTD), and Sheath Blight (ShBl).

pest_resistance.summary: Sava 200 is moderately resistant/tolerant to Stem Borer (SB). It also shows tolerance to gall midge, Brown Planthopper (BPH), and Green Leafhopper (GLH).

agronomic_details.yield: Sava 200 is described as a high yielding hybrid with reported yields of 65 q/ha and 76.5 q/ha in different contexts.
agronomic_details.stability: Based on two years of evaluation, Sava 200 was found suitable for cultivation in Zone-II. It has been included in All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) trials and multi-location testing.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Sava 200 is a Non-Basmati hybrid suitable for both rainfed and irrigated ecology, including early rainfed and irrigated conditions. It is also suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water environments. It has been identified as suitable for cultivation in Zone-II.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Sava 200 is a semi-dwarf variety (82 cm) with long slender (LS) grains. It is also noted to be lodging tolerant.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Sava 200 has been an entry in All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) trials, including Soil stress tolerant trials and AVT 1-E TP Zone -2 & 3 Kharif 2016. It was evaluated for two years for its suitability in Zone-II and included in multi-location testing for grain yield performance.

drought.details: Sava 300 is a drought tolerant rice hybrid suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and irrigated early stress conditions. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Sava 300, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts have also focused on developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance.

heat.details: It is suitable for irrigated early stress conditions, which can include temperature stress. Research on high temperature tolerance has contributed to the development of abiotic tolerant rice varieties, within which Sava 300 is categorized.

salinity.details: While general abiotic stress tolerance breeding is mentioned, specific tolerance to salinity for Sava 300 is not detailed in the provided results. One result mentions a different variety (AC43037) tolerant to salinity, but this is not attributed to Sava 300.

flood.details: No direct information on general flood tolerance is provided, separate from submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Sava 300 exhibits enhanced disease tolerance and resistance. It is highly resistant to Leaf Blight (LB), neck infection, and Sheath-rot. It shows moderate resistance (MR-BL) to Blast (including leaf blast and bacterial leaf blast), and resistance to brown spot and false smut. Molecular breeding for blast resistance has been conducted.

pest_resistance.summary: Sava 300 shows tolerance to major insect pests. It is tolerant to Green Leaf Hopper (T-GLH), Brown Plant Hopper (BPH), leaf folder, gundhi bug, stem-borer, and gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: No specific quantitative yield data is provided for Sava 300.
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified in the provided results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Sava 300 is a Non-Basmati hybrid suitable for irrigated conditions, specifically for early stress conditions. It is also suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Sava 300 is a semi-dwarf hybrid, with a height of 82 cm. It produces long slender (LS) grains. As a SmartRice® hybrid, it offers lodging tolerance, higher milling percentage, and non-chaffy panicles, contributing to better water resource utilization.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Sava 300 has been evaluated by ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (AICRIP) and is listed in their draft proceedings, indicating its participation in evaluation programs.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), has been isolated from the drought tolerant rice cultivar Sava 300.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs linked to Sava 300 traits are provided in the search results. A mention of 128 QTLs was for maize, not rice.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Molecular breeding has been utilized for the development of rice varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil phosphorus (P), and blast, which aligns with the reported traits of Sava 300. The identified gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) contributes to abiotic stress response.

drought.details: No evidence found in searched sources for drought tolerance.

heat.details: Described as a cold-tolerant, early-maturing indica (SDIOPR paper). A farmer reported good crop health through a heatwave and flood-like conditions; this is anecdotal and not trial data, so no heat tolerance level is assigned.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources for salinity tolerance.

flood.details: A farmer reported crop health under flood-like conditions and good performance across weather conditions at high altitude. This is anecdotal, not trial data, so no level is assigned.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: moderate resistance reported in the SDIOPR paper. A 2025 news report describes it as resistant to blast (named 'Shalimar-4', alongside Shalimar-5); this conflicts with the 'moderate' rating. A KVK Kupwara paper describes SR-4 as high-yielding and disease-resistant without naming the disease. No other diseases found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Rice-4 (CSC name) / Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name), rice, code SKUA-408, SKUAST-Kashmir

NAME NOTE: The CSC name "Shalimar Rice-4" is supported by sources that use SKUA-408 as its code. No search result tied the Seednet name "Shalimar Rice-2" to this variety. The only Shalimar Rice-2 record found is a separate 2012 release with a different parentage (VL Dhan 221/K 39), so Seednet "Shalimar Rice-2" evidence below is not attributed to SR-4.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as a cold-tolerant, early-maturing indica with moderate blast resistance, for the valley plains -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Described as resistant to blast, alongside Shalimar-5, in a 2025 news report (name given as "Shalimar-4") -- https://ricenewstoday.com/new-kashmir-rice-varieties-yields-over-two-times-national-average-offer-farmers-second-crop-window/
- A farmer reported crop health through a heatwave and flood-like conditions, and good performance across weather conditions at high altitude (anecdotal, not trial data) -- https://risingkashmir.com/farmers-report-doubling-of-rice-yields-with-bumper-harvest-using-sr-4-seed-variety/
- Drought, salinity, submergence: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate blast resistance (see above; conflicts with "resistant" claim in ricenewstoday) -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- A KVK Kupwara paper describes SR-4 as a high-yielding, disease-resistant variety, without naming the disease -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6312
- Insect pests: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Matures in 135-140 days; yield potential 7.5-8.0 t/ha; sown second fortnight of April and transplanted second fortnight of May; 20 x 20 cm spacing; seed rate 50-60 kg/ha -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Budgam FLD (2018-2021) table gives seed rate 60-80 kg/ha and sowing 1st week April to 1st fortnight May (conflicts with 50-60 kg/ha) -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Budgam FLD mean seed yield 85 q/ha vs 50.5 q/ha for local check China-1039 over four years; BCR 2.22 vs 1.38 -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Kupwara FLD (2021-22 to 2023-24, 180 demonstrations): mean 83.33 q/ha vs 51.66 q/ha farmer practice -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6312
- Developer's claimed yield of about 10 t/ha, "three times" national varieties (interview, not trial data) -- https://kashmirlife.net/we-created-a-rice-variety-having-three-times-more-yield-vol-14-issue-44-309051/
- A 2025 report gives a reported yield potential of about 17 q/ha, which conflicts with the 7.5-8.0 t/ha figure -- https://thekashmirimages.com/2026/10/14/skuast-k-works-to-revive-traditional-rice-develop-high-yielding-varieties/
- Irrigation and nitrogen schedule study on SKUA-408 (Shalimar Rice-4) measuring PAR interception -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/issues/article_abstract.php?aid=14811&iid=399&jid=3

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage/cross: No evidence found (CSC lists "Not specified"; the cross listed in a 2012 chapter table belongs to Shalimar Rice-2, not SR-4) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/59698
- QTL/marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by SKUAST-Kashmir; Mountain Research Centre for Field Crops (MRCFC), Khudwani -- https://kashmirlife.net/we-created-a-rice-variety-having-three-times-more-yield-vol-14-issue-44-309051/ and https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6312
- Najeeb-ul-Rehman Sofi, associate director, MRCFC, named as the source on Shalimar-4 (SR-4) development and characteristics -- https://ricenewstoday.com/new-kashmir-rice-varieties-yields-over-two-times-national-average-offer-farmers-second-crop-window/
- Developer role: Najeeb-ul-Rehman Sofi is named as developer of a different variety (Shalimar Sugandh) -- https://c4scourses.in/result/skuast-k-develops-aromatic-rice-variety-for-kashmir/ (listed for context only; not attributed to SR-4)
- 2020 IJGPB article author list: G. A. Parray, S. Najeeb, A. B. Shikari, F. A. Sheikh, A. Hussain, M. A. Ganai, M. N. Mughal, S. A. Waza (the full name of "S. Najeeb" is not shown, so it is not equated with Sofi) -- https://www.isgpb.org/article/rice-shalimar-rice-4-skua-408
- Release year: CSC says 2019; a 2025 FLD paper states release in 2017 (https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf); a 2025 report describes release "in 2025" (https://thekashmirimages.com/2026/10/14/skuast-k-works-to-revive-traditional-rice-develop-high-yielding-varieties/). Unresolved.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Rice-6 (CSC name) / Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name), SKUA-485, rice, SKUAST-Kashmir MRCFC

Scope note: four web searches were run. A fifth search was blocked by a tool limit, so the snippets below are partial and I could not open full pages. No search result I could see names Shalimar Rice-6 directly. Where a line concerns Shalimar Rice-2 or another Shalimar line, it is labelled as such. Treat the CSC/Seednet name mismatch as unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2 (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence not reported in the snippets reviewed).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Extension advisory lists Shalimar Rice-1, Shalimar Rice-2, Shalimar Rice-3 and Shalimar Rice-4 under a recommendation "for higher belts of the valley", with nutrient doses given for lower belts -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf
REAC committee minutes mention Shalimar Rice-8 as a short-duration variety suited to the rice–wheat system, and note that a variety SKAU-528 was at the final stage of release. Neither entry is Shalimar Rice-6 -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=Conduct+of+58th+59th+Research+and+Extension+Advisory+committee+REACMeeting.pdf
Maturity, yield and release-notification details for Shalimar Rice-6 (SKUA-485): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2. A ScienceDirect QTL paper on yield traits on rice chromosome 6 was returned, but it concerns unrelated germplasm and is not evidence for this variety -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1671292708600474

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Mountain Research Centre for Field Crops (MRCFC), SKUAST-K, is at Khudwani in Kulgam district, south Kashmir, and is described as working on traditional rice revival and high-yielding varieties -- https://kashmirlife.net/skuast-ks-khudwani-centre-revives-traditional-rice-develops-high-yielding-varieties-456999/
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

Email and phone: No evidence found in the snippets reviewed. The SKUAST-K official website is the likely source for a contact page but was not verified.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or journal paper on Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2 surfaced in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Shalimar Rice-2 is named in the Directorate of Extension document as a recommended variety for the valley's higher belts, but no seed source (NSC, SKUAST seed sales, KVK, dealer) was found -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf
Seednet portal listing for Shalimar Rice-2 (PADDY (DHAN)): not checked; no evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCHES RUN: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institution; research papers; seed/Seednet name). No further searches were permitted.

NAME NOTE: The CSC name "Shalimar Rice-5" matches the sources as "Shalimar-5", "SR-5" or "Shalimar Rice-5". No source page names "Shalimar Rice-2" as the Seednet entry for SR-5. The "Shalimar Rice-2" pages found refer to a separate, earlier release, so they are not attributed to this variety. The "SKUA-402" code appears in a 2021 study as a separate japonica entry alongside Shalimar Rice-5 is not stated, so the code-to-name equivalence is unconfirmed and no SKUA-402 finding is attributed here.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Both Shalimar-4 and Shalimar-5 are described as resistant to rice blast (SR-5 name used in source: Shalimar-5) -- https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/agriculture/Kashmir-Agricultural-RandD-Unveils-High-Yielding-Rice-Varieties/6a95904aa703e4a8160b85b2
- Blast resistance of Shalimar-4 and Shalimar-5 is also reported by a business newspaper quoting MRCFC associate director Najeeb-ul-Rehman Sofi -- https://www.pressreader.com/india/businessline-delhi-9wvw/20260901/281908780007891
- A SKUAST-K released-variety phenotyping study treats Shalimar Rice-5 as a japonica check and reports better root traits (depth, dry weight, length, surface area) than indica varieties, and links root traits to drought resilience (name used: Shalimar Rice-5) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44279-024-00068-5
- Drought resilience claim is framed at the study level; no drought-trial numbers for SR-5 were captured in the snippet -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44279-024-00068-5
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast resistance (rice blast, fungal) is the only disease trait reported for Shalimar-5 in the retrieved pages -- https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/agriculture/Kashmir-Agricultural-RandD-Unveils-High-Yielding-Rice-Varieties/6a95904aa703e4a8160b85b2
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Test yields of about 7.2 t/ha are reported for Shalimar-4 and Shalimar-5 together, not separately for SR-5 -- https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/agriculture/Kashmir-Agricultural-RandD-Unveils-High-Yielding-Rice-Varieties/6a95904aa703e4a8160b85b2
- SR-5 is described as maturing earlier than conventional varieties, enabling a possible second crop -- https://www.pressreader.com/india/businessline-delhi-9wvw/20260901/281908780007891
- Farmers in Kashmir reported yield gains from SR-4 and SR-5 with yields roughly doubling versus traditional varieties (grower-reported, not trial data) -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuast-k-developed-paddy-varieties-boost-crop-production/
- SR-5 is described as suited to higher-altitude areas, while SR-4 is for plains -- https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/agriculture/Kashmir-Agricultural-RandD-Unveils-High-Yielding-Rice-Varieties/6a95904aa703e4a8160b85b2
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results for SR-5: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or parentage study for Shalimar Rice-5 was retrieved. Parentage is not specified in the record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- SR-4 and SR-5 were developed by the Mountain Research Centre for Field Crops (MRCFC), Khudwani, SKUAST-Kashmir -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuast-k-developed-paddy-varieties-boost-crop-production/
- Same attribution in a business newspaper: the varieties were developed by MRCFC Khudwani under SKUAST-Kashmir -- https://www.pressreader.com/india/businessline-delhi-9wvw/20260901/281908780007891
- Najeeb-ul-Rehman Sofi is named as associate director at MRCFC, speaking on SR-4 and SR-5; not confirmed as lead breeder -- https://www.pressreader.com/india/businessline-delhi-9wvw/20260901/281908780007891
- Farooq Ahmad is named as Professor of Plant Breeding and Genetics at SKUAST-K and MRCFC; he is described as speaking about MRCFC's mandate, not named as SR-5 breeder -- https://kashmirlife.net/skuast-ks-khudwani-centre-revives-traditional-rice-develops-high-yielding-varieties-456999/
- Lead breeder of Shalimar Rice-5 specifically: not confirmed by any page -- no breeder name attributed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Chickpea-2 (CSC name) / Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name)

Search note: 4 web_search calls were run. Little variety-specific evidence was found. The Seednet name "Shalimar Rice-2" returned no matching record, so the Seednet heading below says so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Shalimar Chickpea-2 drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only related item is the adaptation note under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS. No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name).

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found that names Shalimar Chickpea-2 as resistant to any disease or pest. The closest hit is a SKUAST-K paper on gram pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera) resistance genetic resources in chickpea from the Western Himalayas, which mentions the variety only in passing -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Shalimar chickpea-02 is described as the first summer chickpea variety for the Kashmir valley, developed and released by SKUAST-K. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for Shalimar Chickpea-2 were found in the retrieved text. The ICAR-AICRP chickpea report (2021-22) was returned but does not mention this variety in the retrieved text -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name). Rice results returned were for Shalimar-4 and Shalimar-5, which are different varieties: SKUAST-K introduces high-yielding Shalimar-4 and Shalimar-5 rice varieties in Kashmir -- https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/agriculture/Kashmir-Agricultural-RandD-Unveils-High-Yielding-Rice-Varieties/6a95904aa703e4a8160b85b2

GENETICS AND QTL
No QTL, marker or genetic study specific to Shalimar Chickpea-2 was found. The pod borer resistance paper is a genetic resource and QTL study of chickpea, but the retrieved text does not link its QTLs to this variety -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, Kashmir (SKUAST-K), as stated in the input record. The retrieved paper on pod borer resistance is from SKUAST-K's Faculty of Agriculture, and it credits the release of Shalimar chickpea-02 to that group -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
Lead breeder names: no named release breeder for Shalimar Chickpea-2 was found. The paper's authors are M Parthiban (Division of Entomology, FoA, SKUAST-Kashmir) and Reyazul Rouf Mir (Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding, FoA, SKUAST-Kashmir) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025. Their link to the variety's development is not stated in the retrieved text.
Seednet name (Shalimar Rice-2): no breeder or institution record found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Reyazul Rouf Mir, Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding, Faculty of Agriculture, SKUAST-Kashmir; marked as corresponding author on the paper. No email or phone found -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
M Parthiban, Division of Entomology, Faculty of Agriculture, SKUAST-Kashmir. No email or phone found -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
Address (field research location, not a postal address): Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding research field, Wadura Campus, Sopore, Jammu and Kashmir, India -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
Institute-level contact: no official SKUAST-K email, phone or postal address was found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
Parthiban M, Mir RR (year not stated in retrieved text). Genetic resources and genes/QTLs for gram pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera Hübner) resistance in chickpea from the Western Himalayas. Journal not stated in retrieved text -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No other publication specific to Shalimar Chickpea-2 was found, including in KrishiKosh, AICRP reports or theses.

SEED AVAILABILITY

General SKUAST-K seed chain (not variety-specific): SKUAST-K works with the Department of Agriculture to run a seed chain from breeder seed to foundation and certified seed -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
Recommended next step: contact the SKUAST-K seed unit or the Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding, Sopore, for current stock.

RECOMMENDED STATES
