gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is a cold-temperate J&K release with no documented drought, heat, salinity or submergence tolerance, and no yield figure. Its only stress-related attributes are the 'R-BL' code (a weak, unexpanded blast resistance indication) and low-lying adaptation. Citations exist, but they are listings, advisories and a Wx allele study, not stress or performance research. Suitability for Gujarat's warm, semi-arid and coastal conditions is unsupported. The score is 50 ('some stress or climate trait, but no citation') instead of 60 because the available citations do not support the stress traits, and it is capped there because the evidence is weak.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: SKUAST-K release for irrigated lowlands of J&K; 130-135 days; non-basmati; possible blast resistance (unverified)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Shalimar Rice-2 is a non-basmati rice variety from SKUAST-Kashmir, released in 2015, for irrigated lowlands of Jammu & Kashmir, maturing in about 130-135 days. No source documents drought, heat, salinity or submergence tolerance, and the only hint of disease resistance is an unexpanded 'R-BL' code. The evidence is mostly listings and seed production tables, and it suggests the variety is poorly suited to Gujarat.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: SKUAST-K non-basmati variety released in 2015 for irrigated J&K lowlands, maturing in 130-135 days. Yield, parentage and morphology are not reported.

variety_profile.recommended_states: Jammu & Kashmir (irrigated lowlands/plains of the valley, low altitudes). Not recommended for Gujarat in any source.
variety_profile.year_of_release: 2015 (ICAR rice-garud and AICRIP sources). The InTechOpen chapter lists 2012, so the sources conflict.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific drought data. The drought-related snippets are generic AICRIP program text, or refer to a drought-stress trial in which Shalimar Rice 3 appears only as a zonal check.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: Heat tolerance screening is mentioned in the AICRIP 50 Years book, but nothing links it to this variety.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: Salinity appears only in generic program text and in checks such as FL478. No data on this variety.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The 'semi-deep water, one week submergence' snippet in the rice-garud results belongs to a different entry on that page.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No SUB1 or other submergence data for this variety. The SUB1A mention in the InTechOpen chapter concerns modern varieties in general.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Not confirmed. The ICAR crop-improvement table has an 'R–BL' notation next to Shalimar Rice 3, which may mean resistant to blast, but the snippet is ambiguous and needs verification.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (insufficient evidence; no stress trait is confirmed)
key_stress_attributes: Suited to the cooler, low-altitude irrigated conditions of Kashmir. This is adaptation, not a documented stress tolerance.

genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Not specified (conventional is likely but unconfirmed)

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: 7,000-7,500 Kg/Ha (ACS Omega 2023 experiment description). A 'Shalimar Rice 3 (ZC) 1742.22' figure appears in an HPKV annual report, but its units and context are unclear.
agronomic_performance.yield_stability: Used as a zonal check in AICRIP hill and medium-hill trials (AVT1-M(H)), which indicates multi-location use. No stability statistics are reported.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Irrigated lowlands and low altitudes of Jammu & Kashmir, up to about 1650 m according to one source.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 125-130 days (rice-garud) or 135-140 days (ACS Omega). The sources conflict.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Non-basmati; grain quality data in the 2021 Rice Grain Quality book (milling 68.1%, 'SB' grain type). The 'SB' code is unexplained.
agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: Serves as the zonal check in AVT trials, with Vivekdhan 86 as the national check. A farmer-field report (ResearchGate FAMPAR/IRD) describes SR3 as performing better than SR1 and SR2, which were late maturing.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Positive: SR3 is cited as performing well in farmers' fields, unlike SR1 and SR2. It is listed in J&K paddy advisories.

breeder_and_development_info.development_timeline: Released 2012 or 2015 (sources conflict). Later tested as a zonal check in AICRIP trials from 2018 to 2023.
breeder_and_development_info.research_publications: ACS Omega 2023 (sowing time and weed management study, doi:10.1021/acsomega.3c01361); InTechOpen chapter on rice biodiversity in the Kashmir Himalayas; AICRIP progress reports and proceedings.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are multiple citations (ICAR, AICRIP, a peer-reviewed ACS Omega paper) and some yield data (7.0-7.5 t/ha). No stress tolerance trait is documented, which matches the 'at least one citation but weak on stress traits' band. The variety is bred for the temperate, cold-climate J&K valley and is not recommended for Gujarat, so its suitability for Gujarat is doubtful.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Temperate irrigated lowland variety for J&K; 7.0-7.5 t/ha potential; zonal check in AICRIP trials; no documented stress tolerance.
dashboard_data.seasons: Kharif (inferred from irrigated paddy advisories; not explicit)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Shalimar Rice-3 is a non-basmati, irrigated lowland variety from SKUAST-Kashmir for Jammu & Kashmir, with a yield potential of about 7.0-7.5 t/ha and maturity of 125-140 days. No drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, or pest tolerance is documented, and disease resistance is unconfirmed. Evidence is moderate for agronomic data but absent for stress traits, and the variety is not recommended for Gujarat.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Non-basmati irrigated variety released in J&K in 2012 or 2015, maturing in 125-140 days with a 7.0-7.5 t/ha potential. It is used as a zonal check in AICRIP hill and medium-hill trials.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific stress tolerance evidence was found; the stress-related search hits are generic program text or other entries. Possible blast resistance is ambiguous and unverified. It is unsuitable as a stress-tolerant choice for Gujarat.

drought.details: Identified as a drought tolerant rice variety, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, and capable of tolerating moisture stress. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Sikkim Dhan-1, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance.

heat.details: Mentioned in the context of climate-resilient technologies aimed at reducing heat stress, and within discussions on developing abiotic tolerant rice varieties with high temperature tolerance.

salinity.details: No direct evidence found for salinity tolerance in Sikkim Dhan-1.

flood.details: Suitable for semi-deep water conditions and exhibits one week submergence tolerance. It has been included in screening programs for submergence tolerance in rice.

disease_resistance.summary: Reported to be moderately resistant to multiple diseases. Specific resistances include bacterial leaf blast (BLB), false smut, blast, and neck blast. It is generally considered a disease-resistant variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance for Sikkim Dhan-1 is detailed, though general pest management advisories and evaluation of insect pests are mentioned in documents listing the variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield of 34.32 Q/ha (quintals per hectare).
agronomic_details.stability: Suitable for both rainfed and irrigated conditions, indicating adaptability across different water regimes. It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well-adapted to Sikkim and considered for climate-resilient technologies in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. It is suitable for both rainfed and irrigated cultivation.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 135 days. It is described as an early maturing and medium-duration variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-Basmati type. It is high yielding, lodging tolerant, and has a plant height of 103 cm. Grain characteristics are described as 'SB' (Short Bold) and also noted as 'LS' (Long Slender) in different entries within the same database source.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field days have been celebrated by ICAR Sikkim Centre for Sikkim Dhan-1, indicating successful demonstrations and cultivation. It is included in Kharif Agro-Advisories for farmers.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Sikkim Dhan-1 and identified as being associated with drought tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specifically detailed as QTLs, but the isolation of the OsCHI2 gene from Sikkim Dhan-1 implies a genetic basis for its stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) is identified as an abiotic stress responsive gene. The variety's origin is noted as 'Selection from IURON (BP. 3180-MR-6)'. Molecular breeding for drought, low soil P, and blast resistance is a broader research focus in which Sikkim Dhan-1 is mentioned.

commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available for cultivation, specifically highlighted for farmers in ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisories. It is one of the cultivars recommended for organic rice cultivation in India.

drought.details: Sikkim Dhan-3 is characterized as a drought-tolerant rice variety, particularly suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), associated with drought tolerance, has been isolated from this cultivar. Molecular breeding efforts are focused on developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance, indicating the importance of this trait in Sikkim Dhan-3.

heat.details: The variety exhibits high temperature tolerance and is considered in the context of developing abiotic tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: While salinity and osmotic stress tolerance are discussed in the context of varieties listed alongside Sikkim Dhan-3, the direct salinity tolerance of Sikkim Dhan-3 is not explicitly stated in the provided results.

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: High resistance to multiple diseases. It is moderately resistant to Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB), leaf blast, and neck blast. The variety exhibits multiple disease resistance against rice blast and bacterial blight. Molecular breeding efforts are also ongoing for enhancing blast resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Medium resistance. Sikkim Dhan-3 is moderately resistant to stem borer and gundhi bug. It is broadly considered a pest-resistant variety.

agronomic_details.yield: 55-60 quintals per hectare (q/ha)
agronomic_details.stability: Demonstrates stability by being suitable for both irrigated and rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well-adapted for cultivation in Sikkim, suitable for both irrigated and rainfed conditions, including direct sowing in rainfed areas, and semi-deep water conditions. It is a Non-Basmati rice variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Resistant to lodging. Grains are described as long slender (LS).
agronomic_details.field_trials: The reported yield, maturity, and adaptation for different cultivation conditions imply that the variety has undergone field trials.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), has been isolated from Sikkim Dhan-3 (IET 25539) and is associated with drought tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Molecular breeding efforts for the development of rice varieties, including Sikkim Dhan-3, focus on inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) represents a molecular mechanism for abiotic stress response. Beta amylase 1 in Sikkim Dhan-3 has shown significant changes under cold stress, indicating its role in cold tolerance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety under either name. One ResearchGate record (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423) carries a description of a "cold tolerant" long slender variety, but that snippet is not tied to JGL 21078 on the page, so I have not attributed it.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Telangana Vari 3 / Telangana Vari 4 / JGL 21078 (IET 26125). Blast and gall midge results on the returned pages belong to other varieties (Telangana Sona/RNR 15048 and KNM 1638) and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only agronomy data returned (maturity, grain size, yield) are for KNM 1638, a different variety (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre), and were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or marker data for JGL 21078 (IET 26125) appeared. The parentage field "Not specified" stays as is.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Name match: the only page matching the variety code JGL 21078 (IET 26125) calls it "Telangana Rice 3," not "Telangana Vari 3." The evidence does not refer to the Seednet name "TELANGANA VARI 4," and I found no evidence for that name.
- Chandra Mohan Yeshala, Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423
- Vajra Thirumala Rao, PJTSAU (listed as co-author on the notification proposal) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vajra-Thirumala-Rao
- Boddupalli Srinivas and Keshwini Sukumar are co-authors; their affiliations are not shown on the page -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423
- Thippewamy Sanka, listed with Syngenta (affiliation shown on the page) -- same URL
- Lead breeder: not identified. The author list does not say who led the breeding work.
- Institution and station: PJTSAU Rice Research Centre, Telangana State. The page header is garbled and does not give a complete postal address -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page for this variety was returned. The PJTSAU Rice Research Centre header above is the only location reference, and it is incomplete. Individual researcher profiles (ResearchGate) show no email or phone.

PUBLICATIONS --
Chandra Mohan Yeshala, Boddupalli Srinivas, Thippewamy Sanka, Vajra Thirumala Rao, Keshwini Sukumar (2021). Proposal for the notification of paddy variety JGL 21078 (IET 26125) under Section 5 of the Seed Act, 1966, Central Rice Research Scheme. Submitted to the state sub-committee on crop standards and release of varieties (record titled "Release proposals of rice culture JGL 24423") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423
The page gives the date as January 2021. The author list is partly truncated in the snippet, so the full author list should be checked against the source. No DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, SSC, KVK, SAU seed-sales, or dealer listing for this variety appeared. The Telangana seed-stock figures returned (https://english.rtvlive.com/telangana-restricts-rice-bonus-to-seven-approved-varieties-targets-38-lakh-acres-under-fine-grain-cultivation/) are not variety-specific and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Telangana; Kerala. The proposal abstract says the variety is a high-yielding, medium-slender type released as "Telangana Rice 3" and suitable for Telangana and Kerala -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vajra-Thirumala-Rao

Notes on the record:
- The CSC release date (2020-11-09) and the notification status are not confirmed by any source found.
- Telangana Sona (RNR 15048), KNM 1638, WGL 962, WGL 1119, and the Kerala/Chittimallelu articles are other varieties or unrelated products and were excluded.
- Four searches were used in total. A dedicated Seednet search for "TELANGANA VARI 4" was not run as a separate query; the final query covered the code and the alternate name together.

drought.details: Identified as a short duration, drought tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and upland areas. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Telangana Vari 4, linking its drought tolerance to a specific genetic mechanism. Molecular breeding efforts have also contributed to its drought tolerance.

heat.details: Exhibits heat stress tolerance and has been part of screening for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes, with high temperature tolerance contributing to the development of abiotic tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: Reported as tolerant to salinity.

flood.details: No specific information on flood tolerance distinct from submergence tolerance was found.

disease_resistance.summary: This variety is generally described as disease-resistant. Specifically, it shows resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, sheath-rot, and bacterial leaf blight.

pest_resistance.summary: Exhibits tolerance to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH), white-backed BPH (wBPH), stemborer, grasshopper, and gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported average yield is 65 quintals per hectare (q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: While not explicitly detailed for yield, the variety's performance under various stress screenings across multiple locations (4-6 centers for submergence, various locations for insect pests) suggests a degree of adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated conditions and is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, including upland environments. It is recommended for cultivation in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Telangana Vari 4 is a Non-Basmati rice variety with Long Slender (LS) grains. Images of its grain, rice, and panicle have been documented.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety, identified as IET 27869 (JGL 25958), has been subject to various screenings, including for submergence tolerance (at 4 and 6 centers) and high temperature tolerance. Over 500 on-farm trials were conducted for the IET 27869 line.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Telangana Vari 4, specifically linked to its drought tolerance. The development of this variety involved molecular breeding for resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast, suggesting the utilization of genetic markers in its breeding program. Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) is generally applied in the context of stress tolerance breeding for rice.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs (Quantitative Trait Loci) are detailed, beyond the identification of the OsCHI2 gene related to abiotic stress tolerance in this variety.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) is implicated in abiotic stress response, particularly drought tolerance.

drought.details: No evidence found for this variety. The digest reports drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance as not found in searched sources.

heat.details: Heat tolerance: no evidence found for this variety. The IIRR newsletter mentions heat-responsive gene expression in heat-tolerant and sensitive cultivars but does not name Tellahamsa as one of them. Separately, the variety is reported as released as a cold-tolerant variety, with a Rabi-season crop described as early maturing and cold tolerant; the 2015 IIRR newsletter table also lists RNR 10754 as cold tolerant. Cold tolerance is not a heat finding and is not used to infer heat level.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight (BB): the variety itself is reported as highly susceptible to BB and blast (PLoS ONE 2020). Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed xa13 and Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 and Pi1 (blast) into Tellahamsa; two ICF3 pyramided lines, TH-625-159 and TH-625-491, showed high resistance, but these are breeding derivatives and not the released variety. Blast response of the four-, three- and two-gene pyramided lines varied. Resistance at the level of the released variety is therefore not established; the reported high susceptibility is the only release-level disease finding.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge: the IIRR newsletter reports that the Gm4 gall midge gene was moved into Warangal sannalu and Tellahamsa, so a gall-midge-resistant Tellahamsa derivative is reported; release-level resistance is not confirmed. Brown planthopper (BPH): no evidence found for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative yield data for this variety were found. The only yield descriptor is 'high yielding'. The Seednet average_yield field is given as Kg/Ha with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rabi-season crop described as early maturing and cold tolerant; grouped as early maturity in a Telangana morphological characterisation of 15 varieties. Recommended state: Telangana. Crop-model calibration was carried out under normal and varied temperatures.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Aerobic-condition trial on alfisols: 1000-grain weight of about 21.34 g; yield not extracted. drought.details: No evidence found for this variety. The digest reports drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance as not found in searched sources.

heat.details: Heat tolerance: no evidence found for this variety. The IIRR newsletter mentions heat-responsive gene expression in heat-tolerant and sensitive cultivars but does not name Tellahamsa as one of them. Separately, the variety is reported as released as a cold-tolerant variety, with a Rabi-season crop described as early maturing and cold tolerant; the 2015 IIRR newsletter table also lists RNR 10754 as cold tolerant. Cold tolerance is not a heat finding and is not used to infer heat level.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight (BB): the variety itself is reported as highly susceptible to BB and blast (PLoS ONE 2020). Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed xa13 and Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 and Pi1 (blast) into Tellahamsa; two ICF3 pyramided lines, TH-625-159 and TH-625-491, showed high resistance, but these are breeding derivatives and not the released variety. Blast response of the four-, three- and two-gene pyramided lines varied. Resistance at the level of the released variety is therefore not established; the reported high susceptibility is the only release-level disease finding.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge: the IIRR newsletter reports that the Gm4 gall midge gene was moved into Warangal sannalu and Tellahamsa, so a gall-midge-resistant Tellahamsa derivative is reported; release-level resistance is not confirmed. Brown planthopper (BPH): no evidence found for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released as a cold-tolerant variety; the Rabi-season crop is described as early maturing and cold tolerant -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- The 2015 IIRR newsletter table also lists the RNR 10754 entry as cold tolerant -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Heat tolerance: no evidence found for this variety. The IIRR newsletter mentions heat-responsive gene expression in heat-tolerant and sensitive cultivars, but does not name Tellahamsa as one of them -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The variety is reported as highly susceptible to bacterial blight (BB) and blast -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed xa13 and Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 and Pi1 (blast) into Tellahamsa. Two ICF3 pyramided lines, TH-625-159 and TH-625-491, showed high resistance; these are breeding derivatives, not the released variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/ and https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Blast response of the four-, three- and two-gene pyramided lines varied -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-024-09549-8
- Gall midge: the IIRR newsletter says the Gm4 gall midge gene was moved into Warangal sannalu and Tellahamsa, so a gall-midge-resistant Tellahamsa derivative is reported; release-level resistance is not confirmed -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Brown planthopper (BPH) resistance: no evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: about 110 days; early maturing -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Grouped as early maturity in a Telangana morphological characterisation of 15 varieties, including Tellahamsa -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/152%20Morphological%20characterization%20of%20Quantitative%20Traits%20and%20Estimation%20of%20Dormancy%20Period%20in%20Promising%20Rice%20Varieties%20(Oryza%20sativa%20L.)%20of%20Telangana%20State%20Bharathi%20Y.pdf
- Aerobic-condition trial on alfisols: 1000-grain weight of about 21.34 g; yield not extracted -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols
- Crop-model calibration (DSSAT) for three cultivars, including Tellahamsa (RNR 10754) under normal and varied temperatures -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377634475_Yield_Prediction_Sensitivity_Analysis_and_Calibration_of_DSSAT_Crop_Model_for_Different_Cultivars_Establishment_Methods_and_Nitrogen_Levels_in_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L_Under_Normal_and_Varied_Temperatures
- Yield: only the descriptor "high yielding" was found; no quantitative yield data for this variety -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: HR 12 x TN-1 per the PLoS paper; the Seednet field reads "HR 12 x T (N) 1", which is consistent -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088 and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/
- Gene-specific markers used for foreground selection: pTA248 (Xa21), xa13prom (xa13), Pi54MAS (Pi54), RM224 (Pi1) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/
- Recurrent parent genome recovery of 92% and 94% in BC2F1 lines -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/
- Unique SSR markers for Tellahamsa: RM 12983, RM14698, RM23819 -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/13102818.2021.1987324
- QTL/metaQTL: the disease metaQTL paper cites the Tellahamsa MAGP study but does not study this variety directly -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12038-024-00460-9

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Name-matched sources show the release from Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Gene-pyramiding development team (2020 PLoS paper): Md. Jamaloddin, Ch. V. Durga Rani, G. Swathi, and others, across PJTSAU, ANGRAU, IRRI and ICAR-IIRR -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/ (these are derivative-line developers, not the original 1968/1971 release breeder)
- Original release breeder: No evidence found.
- Release year conflict: the PLoS paper gives 1968 and the IIRR table gives 1971. The Seednet year field (2014-10-20) appears to be a record or notification date, not the release date; no notification evidence was found.

CONTACT DETAILS

- Email (institute page): iirricar@gmail.com; Phone: 040-24591241 -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-contact-details

- Dr. Abdul Fiyaz, Principal Scientist (Crop Improvement); email genefiyaz@gmail.com -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-contact-details
- No breeder-level contact for this variety was found; the above are institute-level contacts only.

basic_info.institution: Rice Research Station, Tirurkuppam, Tirur; Tamil Nadu Agricultural University

drought.details: Bred as a drought-tolerant, short-duration rice for direct-sown rainfed and semi-dry tracts. Reported to tolerate early water stress, germinate well under direct sowing, and recover strongly after drought. Farmer feedback reports tolerance of water stress, quick recovery after rain, and higher yield under rainfed and semi-dry conditions. Biochemical markers reported: proline content of 2.15 mg/g and a chlorophyll stability index value (numeric value not captured in the digest). The digest gives no graded ranking, so the level is qualitative and based on breeding objective, farmer feedback and biochemical markers.

heat.details: No evidence found.

salinity.details: No evidence found.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to blast, sheath rot, sheath blight, brown spot and rice tungro disease (RTD) (JSRR article). Farmer feedback reports the variety as free from pests and diseases under field conditions (ResearchGate TKM 15 record). The ResearchGate TKM 13 record was excluded from TKM 15 evidence per the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Field-tolerant to leaf folder, stem borer and gall midge (JSRR article). Farmer feedback reports the variety as free from pests under field conditions (ResearchGate TKM 15 record). Tolerance, not resistance, is the stated category for insects.

agronomic_details.yield: Grain yield 3995 kg/ha under rainfed and 4217 kg/ha under semi-dry conditions, 10.42% and 17.89% above check Anna (R) 4. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME NOTE (read first)
- CSC release name: TKM 15 (culture TM 12077). Seednet name: TKM 13. These are two different varieties. TKM 13 is a 2015 release (WGL 32100/Swarna cross, medium duration, 125-130 days). Its evidence is not attributed to TKM 15 below. The Seednet-name search returned only TKM 13 material, so the Seednet record may point to the wrong variety.
- Release date: the input gives 2022-06-17. Sources say the SVRC released TKM 15 in 2022, but they disagree on the notification month (July or August 2022). Verify against the gazette.
- Parentage: no source found for TKM 15. The TNAU press note mentions a TKM 12 x IET 21620 cross, but the text does not clearly link it to TKM 15, so I have not attributed it.

STRESS TOLERANCE (TKM 15)
- Bred as a drought-tolerant, short-duration rice for direct-sown rainfed and semi-dry tracts; reported to tolerate early water stress, germinate well under direct sowing, and recover strongly after drought. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384649909_TKM_15_-A_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Rice_Variety_Suitable_for_Direct_Sown_Water_Limited_Areas_of_Tamil_Nadu_India
- Farmer feedback reports that it tolerates water stress, recovers quickly after rain, and gives higher yield under rainfed and semi-dry conditions. -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476
- Biochemical stress markers reported: higher proline content (2.15 mg/g) and a chlorophyll stability index value. -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476
- Heat and salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST (TKM 15)
- Moderately resistant to blast, sheath rot, sheath blight, brown spot and rice tungro disease (RTD); field-tolerant to leaf folder, stem borer and gall midge. -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311927561_Rice_TKM_13_A_high_yielding_medium_duration_fine_grain_variety (the second URL is TKM 13 wording and is listed for the record only, not as TKM 15 evidence)
- Farmer feedback reports it as free from pests and diseases under field conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384649909_TKM_15_-A_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Rice_Variety_Suitable_for_Direct_Sown_Water_Limited_Areas_of_Tamil_Nadu_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (TKM 15)
- Matures in 118 days. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311927561_Rice_TKM_13_A_high_yielding_medium_duration_fine_grain_variety (abstract text for TKM 15 is in the same ResearchGate record; the JSRR article is the primary source) ; https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476
- Grain yield 3995 kg/ha under rainfed and 4217 kg/ha under semi-dry conditions, 10.42% and 17.89% above check Anna (R) 4. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311927561_Rice_TKM_13_A_high_yielding_medium_duration_fine_grain_variety ; https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/varieties-released/ (Tirur station list also reports yields of 3995 and 4217 kg/ha)
- Plant type: erect, high tillering, non-lodging, panicle about 25 cm with about 253 grains. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311927561_Rice_TKM_13_A_high_yielding_medium_duration_fine_grain_variety
- Grain: white, medium slender, 1000-grain weight 15.0 g, non-sticky, good cooking taste; hulling 80%, milling 68%, head rice recovery 62.9%. -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476
- Multi-location trial data beyond the station and KVK results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for TKM 15 (no QTL, marker or pedigree study located). The only marker study found (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340798362_Morphological_and_microsatellite_markers_assessment_of_rice_genetic_diversity_for_phosphorus_starvation_tolerance_breeding) covers TKM 13, not TKM 15.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (TKM 15)
- Developed at Rice Research Station, Tirur (Tirurkuppam), Tiruvallur district, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University; the station was founded in 1942. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/varieties-released/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384649909_TKM_15_-A_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Rice_Variety_Suitable_for_Direct_Sown_Water_Limited_Areas_of_Tamil_Nadu_India
- Named lead breeder: No evidence found. The TKM 15 paper lists six authors (see PUBLICATIONS) but does not identify a breeder of record.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level contact (page is dated 2002-2003, so verify it is current): Rice Research Station, Tirurkuppam, Tirur-602025, Tiruvallur District; phone 04116-220233; fax 04116-220383; e-mail arstirur@tnau.ac.in. The page lists "P.G. Lavanya, Assistant Professor (Soil Science)" in the contact block, and gives the professor-and-head title without a name. -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/tirur.html
- Named breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS (TKM 15)
- Sheeba, A., Banumathy, S., Yogameenakshi, P., Muthuramu, S., Tamil Selvi, C., Bhaskaran, M. (2024). TKM 15 -A High Yielding, Short Duration Rice Variety Suitable for Direct Sown Water Limited Areas of Tamil Nadu, India. Journal of Scientific Research and Reports 30(10):488-500 -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476 ; DOI 10.9734/jsrr/2024/v30i102476
- Author affiliations, from the journal page: A. Sheeba (KVK Aruppukottai), S. Banumathy and P. Yogameenakshi (RRS Tirur), S. Muthuramu (KVK Ramanathapuram), C. Tamil Selvi (KVK Tirur), M. Bhaskaran (affiliation not captured in the search extract). -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476
- Other TKM 15 publications, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, QTL studies: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- TKM 15 seed stock, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing: No evidence found. TKM 15 appears only in TNAU season-and-variety recommendation tables. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_rice.html
- For TKM 13 only (not TKM 15): TNAU Seed Centre stock lists show TKM 13 at KVK Vridhachalam, AC&RI Eachangkottai, Kumulur, and RRS Tirur. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/pdf/seedavailabilityon13.08.2019.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu only. Recommended for direct sowing under rainfed and semi-dry conditions in named districts, including Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Tiruvallur, Pudukottai, Ramanathapuram, Virudhunagar, Sivagangai and Thoothukudi. -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/2476
- Season listing: semi-dry crop, July to August sowing. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_rice.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TM 07278 (rice). variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "TM 07278", so every finding below refers to that one name. I ran four searches (variety/release, breeder, research, seed availability). The search index returned very little on this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page reporting drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence reactions for TM 07278.

DISEASE AND PEST
TM 07278 is listed as a cross derivative of WGL 32100 / Swarna, and the page does not give a resistance rating for it. A TNAU Rice Research Station page gives a moderate-resistance rating for leaf folder, stem borer, GLH, blast, RTD, brown spot and sheath rot, but it sits under a heading that covers TKM 13 and TM 07278 together, so it is not clearly attributable to TM 07278 alone. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/crop-improvement/
The ResearchGate paper on TKM 13 reports the same resistance profile, but it is about culture TM 07275, a different line, so I have not attributed it to TM 07278. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311927561_Rice_TKM_13_A_high_yielding_medium_duration_fine_grain_variety (discarded for this variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A CVRC 2016 entry in an ICAR-IIRR RTI report lists TM 07278 as "Irrigated mid early" with a numeric value of 5.48. The page does not explain the number (it may be a duration or yield value), so I have recorded it without interpretation. -- https://icar-iirr.org/RTI/Transparency%20audit-2021/RTI%20Quarter%20I%20Report.pdf
A TNAU Tirur page says TKM 13 and TM 07278 were recently released and are cross derivatives of WGL 32100 / Swarna, and that the cross has been used in rice breeding in India. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/crop-improvement/
The same TNAU page gives a mean yield of 5938 kg/ha across 159 locations, 6.2% and 10.1% above the checks CO (R) 49 and BPT 5204. It does not clearly say whether this refers to TM 07278 or to TKM 13, so I have not attributed it. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/crop-improvement/ (unattributed)

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (WGL 32100 x Swarna) is supported by the TNAU Tirur page. No QTL or marker study naming TM 07278 was found. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/crop-improvement/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Rice Research Station, Tirur (the TNAU page names this station as the source of the TKM 13 / TM 07278 releases). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/crop-improvement/
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The parentage note in the input names RARS Warangal (female parent) and RARS Maruteru (male parent); I found no page confirming those stations for TM 07278.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level page: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Rice Research Station, Tirur, crop-improvement page -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/crop-improvement/ (no email, phone or postal address appeared in the retrieved content).

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, report, thesis or conference item naming TM 07278 was returned. The ResearchGate TKM 13 paper concerns TM 07275 and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for TM 07278. The TNAU seed-stock PDFs returned (2015 and 2021 positions) do not mention it in the retrieved text. Other results were unrelated (RARS Pattambi, IFFDC, OSSC/ORISEED list, a private dealer product sheet). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. "Bihar and Odisha" comes only from the input record. No search result tied TM 07278 to Bihar or Odisha, and the one state list I found (a private dealer page) does not name this variety.

NOTE ON SEARCH COVERAGE: the search index returned no institutional release notification, no SeedNet page, and no KrishiKosh record for TM 07278. Those would be the first places to check directly.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TSF-1 / TPS-1 (safflower vs. paddy record)

Search log: 4 web_search queries ran in one batch. A fifth call returned a tool-limit error, so the breeder-contact and publication searches could not be completed. Only the search snippets were returned, so the findings below are limited to what those snippets showed.

Record conflict to resolve before this goes into a reference database: the record says the crop is safflower, but the Seednet crop is "PADDY (DHAN)", the institution is a rice station (TNAU Agricultural Research Station, Tirupathisaram, Kanyakumari), and the parentage (IR 8 / Kattisamba) is a rice cross. TSF-1 is a safflower variety in the AICRP record. The evidence below therefore refers to two different entries, and the search results do not confirm that they describe the same variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for TSF-1 or TPS-1 (searches returned no stress-tolerance data).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for TSF-1 or TPS-1 (searches returned no resistance data).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- TSF-1 (safflower): AICRP safflower achievements state that front-line demonstrations led to spread of Manjira and TSF-1 in the region, alongside a chickpea and safflower fertilizer schedule -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/major-achievements/
- TPS-1 (paddy, TNAU Tirupathisaram station): the TNAU varieties-released list gives parentage IR8/Kattisamba, duration 110-115 days, kharif ("Kannipoo") season, and red bold grain suitable for direct and transplanted sowing. The snippet did not show the variety name beside this entry, so the match to TPS-1 is unconfirmed -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-tirupathisaram/varieties-released/
- Related but different variety: a study of spread and acceptance of TPS 5 paddy in Kanyakumari District notes the Tirupathisaram station origin -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341824270_Spread_and_Acceptance_of_TPS_5_Paddy_Variety_in_Kanyakumari_District_of_Tamil_Nadu

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- TPS-1 / TSF-1 breeder names: not found in the search results.
- Institution (from the record and the TNAU page): Agricultural Research Station, Tirupathisaram, Kanyakumari District, Tamil Nadu, which is a TNAU station for paddy.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, or contact-page URL was returned. The TNAU station page (https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-tirupathisaram/varieties-released/) is the nearest institutional source and should be used to find the station's official contact page.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The searches did not return any paper, report, thesis, or KrishiKosh record for TSF-1 or TPS-1.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listings were searched successfully).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record says "Not specified", and the searches did not add a state recommendation. The AICRP page mentions TSF-1 spread in a regional context but does not name states in the snippet.

Other data to check: the release date "2010-10-10T00:00:00" looks like a placeholder, and "Tandur Kusuma" as the variety code was not found in any result.

basic_info.institution: Agricultural Research Station, Thirupathisaram, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU)

drought.details: Drought tolerance is not established. The impact study notes the variety performed best under conditions with no drought and no inundation. No drought-tolerance mechanism or trial evidence was found in the searched sources. The non-lodging trait was the reason for the cross, not drought tolerance.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. No heat-stress evidence was reported for TPS 5.

salinity.details: No evidence found for TPS 5 in the searched sources. The TRRI note on saline-area varieties refers to an unrelated variety set (TRY varieties) and is not attributed to TPS 5.

flood.details: Reported tolerance to waterlogged conditions, with area expansion linked to that tolerance. The same impact study states the variety performed best with no inundation, and flood tolerance is explicitly stated as not established. Waterlogging tolerance is not equivalent to flood or inundation tolerance, so no level is assigned.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to blast, sheath rot and sheath blast, reported in the impact study (name: TPS 5). Moderate resistance to yellow stem borer is also reported there. Tungro resistance: no evidence found for TPS 5. Blast or bacterial leaf blight resistance stated in the digest for ADT 55 and CB 14508 is not attributed to TPS 5. Bacterial leaf blight: not found in searched sources for TPS 5.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper (BPH): resistance reported in the impact study (name: TPS 5). Moderately resistant to BPH and WBPH under field conditions (culture TP 08010, EJPB paper). Moderately resistant to stem borer, leaf folder and gall midge, per the EJPB paper and the TNAU variety table. The TNAU table repeats the same moderately resistant profile. Note: the impact study describes BPH resistance without the moderate qualifier, while the EJPB and TNAU sources state moderate resistance. Yellow stem borer: moderate resistance per the impact study.

agronomic_details.yield: Station trials: mean 6377 kg/ha over four years (14.7% above ASD 16). Multi-location 2009-10 (10 locations): mean 6315 kg/ha (about 15% above ASD 16). 2011-12 multi-district (44 locations): 5937 kg/ha (11.4% above ASD 16). TNAU Agritech: 6301 kg/ha. TNAU variety table: 6.13 t/ha. Kanyakumari farmer-field study: 6130 kg/ha mean grain yield. Highest recorded yield: 11,567 kg/ha (Mohanoor, Namakkal), 13.21% above ASD 16.
agronomic_details.stability: Mean yields across the reported trials ranged from about 5937 to 6377 kg/ha across environments and years. Performance was best under no drought and no inundation (impact study). Delta conditions delayed maturity (about 125 days versus about 100 days elsewhere), which the TRRI note links to delayed harvests.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for Kar and late Pishanam seasons as a transplanted crop; kuruvai/Kannipoo suitability is noted in the TNAU table. Adopted in Kanyakumari district and trialled at Namakkal and Thirupathisaram. Delta conditions show longer duration (about 125 days).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 118 days (TNAU Agritech); 118-120 days (TNAU variety table); about 125 days in the delta and about 100 days elsewhere (TRRI note).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging is the main trait; the cross replaced lodging-prone ASD 16 in rain-affected harvests. Grain: short bold white, intermediate amylose, soft gel consistency, moderate gelatinization temperature. Milling 67.5%, head rice recovery 58%. Seed rate 60 kg/ha in the Kanyakumari adoption study.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials: mean 6377 kg/ha over four years, 14.7% above ASD 16. (2) Multi-location trial 2009-10 at 10 locations: mean 6315 kg/ha, about 15% above ASD 16. (3) 2011-12 multi-district trial across 44 locations: 5937 kg/ha, 11.4% above ASD 16. (4) Highest recorded yield 11,567 kg/ha at Mohanoor, Namakkal, 13.21% above ASD 16. (5) Kanyakumari farmer-field study: 6130 kg/ha mean grain yield. (6) TNAU Agritech record: 6301 kg/ha. (7) TNAU variety table: 6.13 t/ha. (8) Delta (TRRI) observation of about 125-day duration.

Note: the impact study describes BPH resistance without the moderate qualifier, while the EJPB and TNAU sources state moderate resistance. Yellow stem borer: moderate resistance per the impact study.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. The digest states no QTL or marker study evidence was found for TPS 5.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. Pedigree is ASD 16 x ADT 37, derived by selection through F2 to F4 generations (culture TP 08010).

agronomic_performance.yield: Station trials: mean 6377 kg/ha over four years (14.7% above ASD 16). Multi-location 2009-10 (10 locations): mean 6315 kg/ha (about 15% above ASD 16). 2011-12 multi-district (44 locations): 5937 kg/ha (11.4% above ASD 16). TNAU Agritech: 6301 kg/ha. TNAU variety table: 6.13 t/ha. Kanyakumari farmer-field study: 6130 kg/ha mean grain yield. Highest recorded yield: 11,567 kg/ha (Mohanoor, Namakkal), 13.21% above ASD 16.
agronomic_performance.stability: Mean yields across the reported trials ranged from about 5937 to 6377 kg/ha across environments and years. Performance was best under no drought and no inundation (impact study). Delta conditions delayed maturity (about 125 days versus about 100 days elsewhere), which the TRRI note links to delayed harvests.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Suitable for Kar and late Pishanam seasons as a transplanted crop; kuruvai/Kannipoo suitability is noted in the TNAU table. Adopted in Kanyakumari district and trialled at Namakkal and Thirupathisaram. Delta conditions show longer duration (about 125 days).
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 118 days (TNAU Agritech); 118-120 days (TNAU variety table); about 125 days in the delta and about 100 days elsewhere (TRRI note).
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging is the main trait; the cross replaced lodging-prone ASD 16 in rain-affected harvests. Grain: short bold white, intermediate amylose, soft gel consistency, moderate gelatinization temperature. Milling 67.5%, head rice recovery 58%. Seed rate 60 kg/ha in the Kanyakumari adoption study.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) Station trials: mean 6377 kg/ha over four years, 14.7% above ASD 16. (2) Multi-location trial 2009-10 at 10 locations: mean 6315 kg/ha, about 15% above ASD 16. (3) 2011-12 multi-district trial across 44 locations: 5937 kg/ha, 11.4% above ASD 16. (4) Highest recorded yield 11,567 kg/ha at Mohanoor, Namakkal, 13.21% above ASD 16. (5) Kanyakumari farmer-field study: 6130 kg/ha mean grain yield. (6) TNAU Agritech record: 6301 kg/ha. (7) TNAU variety table: 6.13 t/ha. (8) Delta (TRRI) observation of about 125-day duration.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Non-lodging is the main trait; the cross was chosen to replace lodging-prone ASD 16 in rain-affected harvests (name: TPS 5 / culture TP 08010) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378204932_Impact_of_Non-lodging_Climate_Resilient_Rice_Variety_TPS_5
- Reported tolerance to waterlogged conditions, with area expansion linked to that tolerance (name: TPS 5) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378204932_Impact_of_Non-lodging_Climate_Resilient_Rice_Variety_TPS_5
- The same impact study notes the variety performed best under conditions with no drought and no inundation, so drought and flood tolerance are not established (name: TPS 5) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378204932_Impact_of_Non-lodging_Climate_Resilient_Rice_Variety_TPS_5
- Drought, heat, salinity and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for TPS 5 in the searched sources. The TRRI note covers an unrelated variety set for saline areas (TRY varieties) -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to stem borer, leaf folder, gall midge, BPH and WBPH under field conditions (culture TP 08010) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/697
- Same resistance profile repeated in the TNAU variety table ("moderately resistant" to stem borer, leaf folder, gall midge, BPH, WBPH) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/TPS5.html
- Impact study reports BPH resistance, moderate resistance to yellow stem borer, blast, sheath rot and sheath blast (name: TPS 5) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378204932_Impact_of_Non-lodging_Climate_Resilient_Rice_Variety_TPS_5
- Blast or bacterial leaf blight resistance is stated for ADT 55 and for CB 14508 searches, not for TPS 5 -- not attributed. Tungro resistance: No evidence found for TPS 5.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 118 days; grown in Kar and late Pishanam seasons; yield 6301 kg/ha (name: TPS 5) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/TPS5.html
- Duration 118-120 days; kuruvai/Kannipoo suitability; yield 6.13 t/ha in the TNAU table -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-tirupathisaram/varieties-released/
- Station trials: mean 6377 kg/ha over four years, 14.7% above ASD 16 (culture TP 08010) -- https://www.academia.edu/75326999/Rice_TPS_5_non_lodging_short_bold_grain_variety
- Multi-location trial 2009-10 at 10 locations: mean 6315 kg/ha, about 15% above ASD 16 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321242744_Rice_TPS_5_a_non-lodging_and_short_bold_grain_variety
- 2011-12 multi-district trial: 5937 kg/ha across 44 locations, 11.4% above ASD 16 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321242744_Rice_TPS_5_a_non-lodging_and_short_bold_grain_variety
- Highest recorded yield 11,567 kg/ha (Mohanoor, Namakkal) and 13.21% over ASD 16 (name: TPS 5) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/impact-of-tps-5-rice-variety-in-kanyakumari-district-tamilnadu-india/95926243
- Kanyakumari farmer-field study: 6130 kg/ha mean grain yield (name: TPS 5) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378204932_Impact_of_Non-lodging_Climate_Resilient_Rice_Variety_TPS_5
- Delta (TRRI) observation: matures in about 100 days elsewhere but about 125 days in the delta, causing delayed harvests (name: TPS 5) -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news
- Grain quality: milling 67.5%, head rice recovery 58% (name: TPS 5) -- https://www.academia.edu/75326999/Rice_TPS_5_non_lodging_short_bold_grain_variety
- Seed rate 60 kg/ha in the Kanyakumari adoption study (name: TPS 5) -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/dfac/8a6b843921dd809b3bcab4250b318229142b.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree ASD 16 x ADT 37; derived by selection through F2 to F4 generations (culture TP 08010) -- https://www.academia.edu/75326999/Rice_TPS_5_non_lodging_short_bold_grain_variety
- Grain traits: short bold white, intermediate amylose, soft gel consistency, moderate gelatinization temperature -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/697
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found for TPS 5.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder: M. Arumugam Pillai, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) (name: TPS 5 / TP 08010) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/697
- Co-author of the impact study: Gomathi Preetha, listed with SRM Institute of Science and Technology; not described as a breeder of TPS 5 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378204932_Impact_of_Non-lodging_Climate_Resilient_Rice_Variety_TPS_5
- Developing institution and station: Agricultural Research Station, Thirupathisaram, TNAU (name: TPS 5) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-tirupathisaram/varieties-released/
- Release year 2014 (name: TPS 5); one extension paper says 2013 -- https://www.extensioneducation.org/index.php/jee/article/view/451
- Breeder name "Eraivan Arutkani Aiyanathan K" appears only as an author profile on an Academia copy of the TNAU paper; role not verified -- https://www.academia.edu/75326999/Rice_TPS_5_non_lodging_short_bold_grain_variety

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released for aerobic (non-flooded, direct-seeded) conditions, but no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence test data for this variety were found. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
- Parentage claim: the source says it came from Naveen crossed with a drought-tolerant local jhum variety, Kataktara. This is a parentage statement, not a tolerance measurement, and it conflicts with the supplied parentage "Sale 6 (4TH SRR DSBWYT-40)". -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for this variety. The search returned resistance data for other rice varieties (for example DRR Dhan 55/56/70/71 and DRR Dhan 80), which were discarded. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant height 95 cm, 120–125 days maturity and 3.4 t/ha yield in hill ecology appear in the source, but the layout places them next to the Pyzum × BPT 5204 entry, so I cannot confidently attribute them to this variety. Recorded as unattributed. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
- Field-trial or multi-location results for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Naveen × Kataktara (per Indian Farming), which conflicts with the supplied parentage Sale 6 (4TH SRR DSBWYT-40). Flagged for verification. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
- QTL or marker studies for this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, which the source says has developed 42 rice varieties. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Station: The TRC code suggests the Tripura Centre, but no source explicitly links this variety to it. This is an inference only. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43621-026-02968-6

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, email and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute address found (Manipur Centre, Imphal, 795 001), taken from the article's author affiliation, not the variety's station. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-12/Indian%20Farming%20July%202025%20Special%20Issue.pdf
- Tripura Centre address (Lembucherra, West Tripura, 799210) from a study that used NEH Tripura Centre material. Institute-level only. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43621-026-02968-6

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2025). Improved cultivars of rice for different [title truncated in retrieved text]. Indian Farming -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
- Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses and conference papers naming this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety was returned. The search returned seed material for other varieties, which was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released for aerobic conditions of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka, and also Tripura and neighbouring NE states. The supplied list omits Tripura. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
- Release year conflict: the source says 2021, while the record says 2020-11-09. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-12/Indian%20Farming%20July%202025%20Special%20Issue.pdf

NAME NOTE
- The Seednet name "TRC 2015-5 (IET 26178) Aerobic Dhan-1" was not returned by any search, and no seednet.gov.in page was retrieved. All evidence above refers to the variety_name form ("NICRA Aerobic Dhan-1/TRC 2015-5"). The code IET 26178 did not appear in any source.

drought.details: TRY 3 is identified as a drought-tolerant rice variety. It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and has shown tolerance under induced drought stress conditions (55 DAS). It is listed among disease-resistant and drought-tolerant varieties.

heat.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to heat stress, evaluated at the seedling stage. It is recognized among genotypes tolerant to heat stresses for adaptation strategies under climate change. It helps escape terminal heat stress.

salinity.details: TRY 3 is identified as a salt-tolerant genotype, specifically recommended for saline tracts. It has been screened for salinity tolerance at the seedling stage and found tolerant in salt stress conditions. It is tolerant up to an Exchangeable Sodium Percentage (ESP) of 32.

flood.details: TRY 3 is stated to be tolerant to flood conditions. It is mentioned in the context of climate-resilient flood-tolerant varieties.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to sheath rot.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to stem borer and leaf.

agronomic_details.stability: Its multi-stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) suggests good stability across challenging environments, though specific stability trials are not detailed.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for irrigated conditions, direct sown rainfed conditions, and semi-deep water cultivation. It is suitable as a Thaladi crop and for Navarai season.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: BROAD LEAVES, CLEFT LIGULE, RELATIVELY SPARSELY PLACED SPIKELETS. Semi tall (130 cm).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials have been conducted at various locations including Trichy, Ramanathapuram, KVK Tirur, and KVK Tindivanam. It has been evaluated for abiotic stress tolerance at the seedling stage against salt, cold, and heat, and for submergence tolerance and sodic conditions.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Tripura Toria-1 (CSC minutes name) / Tripura Khara-1 (Seednet name, crop listed as PADDY (DHAN))

NAME AND CROP CHECK
- No search result mentions "Tripura Toria-1" or variety code TRC T-1-1-5-1. The only Tripura variety match is "Tripura Khara-1", which the Seednet record lists as paddy. The sources below for Tripura Khara-1 therefore refer to a rice variety, not a toria variety. Under the strict-relevance rule, I have kept them only under the Seednet name and paddy crop, and flagged each one.
- Searches were run for the toria name and the Seednet name. The toria results were about other toria varieties (PT-303, TS-38, TS-46, Sushree, Anuradha) and were discarded. The Seednet-name results were about rice.
- Search budget was exhausted after 4 searches, so seed availability was not searched.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for Tripura Toria-1 (toria) under drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence.
- Tripura Khara-1 (paddy, Seednet name): the ICAR Tripura Centre release report lists it among nine rice varieties released in 2014 but gives no stress-tolerance traits -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/6910
- Discarded, not confirmed as the same variety: an Indian Farming (2025) list describes "Tripura Khara Dhan-1" as released in 2014 for drought-prone shallow lowlands, with drought QTLs qDTY2.2 and qDTY4.1 in an IR 64 background. The near-identical name is not confirmed as this variety -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Tripura Toria-1 or Tripura Khara-1.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Tripura Toria-1 (toria) in trials.
- Discarded: toria trials at Namsai (Arunachal) and Jorhat (Assam) tested TS-67, M-27, TS-36, TS-38, TS-46, Jeuti, Sushree and Anuradha, none of which is this variety -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-10-2020/Taba%20Nem,%20et%20al.pdf ; https://www.allresearchjournal.com/archives/2015/vol1issue9/PartB/1-8-120-423.pdf
- Discarded: Tripura rice assessment in Sepahijala used Gomati and Tripura Chickon, not Khara-1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384066050_Assessment_of_high_yielding_rice_varieties_for_their_growth_and_yield_performance_in_Sepahijala_district_of_Tripura

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for Tripura Toria-1 or Tripura Khara-1. The Khara Dhan-1 QTL note above is for a similarly named, unconfirmed variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Tripura Khara-1 (paddy, Seednet name): the 2014 ICAR Tripura Centre release meeting report lists it among the nine rice varieties presented by Dr S. P. Das (Senior Scientist, Plant Breeding). This names him as presenter, not confirmed breeder -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/6910
- The same report says the 16 varieties were approved by the State Varietal Release Committee chaired by the Principal Secretary of Agriculture, Government of Tripura, and released by ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Tripura Centre, Lembucherra (15 September 2014) -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/6910
- Tripura Toria-1 (toria): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Tripura Centre, Lembucherra, Debendrachandra Nagar-799210, Tripura -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/indian-council-of-agricultural-research-icar-tripura-no ; https://www.indiacustomercare.com/meghalaya-indian-council-agriculture-research-icar-no
- Official website: https://icarneh.tripura.gov.in/ . Listed general email: jd.tripura[at]icar[dot]gov[dot]in (also icartripura.jd[at]gmail[dot]com) -- https://icarneh.tripura.gov.in/
- Head of Centre: Dr. Burhan U. Choudhury, HoRC and Principal Scientist, phone 8131074848, email Buhan.Choudhury@icar.gov.in (typo as printed); other listed addresses Burhan.Choudhury@icar.org.in and burhan.choudhury[at]icar[dot]org[dot]in -- https://icarneh.icar.gov.in/Profile/Tripura.html ; http://www.icarneh.ernet.in/Profile/Tripura.html ; https://www.indiacustomercare.com/indian-council-of-agricultural-research-icar-tripura-no
- Plant breeding scientist (institute-level contact, not variety-specific): Dr. Rahul Kumar, Scientist (Genetics & Plant Breeding), phone 8958626086, email Rahul.Kumar5@icar.org.in -- https://icarneh.icar.gov.in/Profile/Tripura.html ; http://www.icarneh.ernet.in/Profile/Tripura.html
- Parent institute (Umiam, Meghalaya): Director Dr. G. Kadirvel, phone 0364-2999450, director.icar-neh@icar.org.in; postal address Umroi Road, Umiam, Meghalaya, PIN 793103; phone (0364) 2570257 -- http://www.icarneh.ernet.in/contacts.html ; https://www.babrone.edu.in/vinstituteD.php?id=i_id000135
- Conflict: other pages name different directors for the parent institute (Dr. Sandeep Ghatak in https://www.indiacustomercare.com/meghalaya-indian-council-agriculture-research-icar-no; Dr. V K Mishra in https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-research-complex-neh-region). Verify before use.
- An older Agartala address (Quarter No. V/3, Agartala Capital Complex, Pin 799006; phone 91 381-2865201) is listed at https://www.indcareer.com/tripura/agartala/icar-research-complex-neh-region-tripura and may be outdated.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for Tripura Toria-1 or Tripura Khara-1 in peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses or KrishiKosh. Not searched on KrishiKosh directly; search budget was used on the topics above.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Not searched (search budget exhausted). No evidence gathered for NSC, Tripura state seed agencies, KVK, SAU or private dealers.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tripura (Tripura Khara-1, paddy): the 2014 release was approved by the Tripura State Varietal Release Committee -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/6910
- Tripura Toria-1 (toria): No evidence found for a recommendation.

RECORD NOTES FOR THE CURATOR
- The CSC release year (2018-08-10) differs from the 2014 ICAR Tripura Centre release date for Tripura Khara-1. Check whether the CSC entry and the Seednet entry are the same variety.
- The toria crop and paddy crop conflict must be resolved against the CSC minutes before this record is used.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: variety_name is "US 312" (CSC minutes). seednet_variety_name is "US-316". No Seednet listing for US-316 or US 312 was found, so every finding below refers to the commercial "US 312" (SeedWorks hybrid) name, not to a Seednet record.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Listed as blast-resistant, with tolerance to sucking pests (commercial listing; no trial data) -- https://www.agriculture-xprt.com/products/us-agriseeds-model-us-312-hybrid-rice-seeds-853682 ; https://www.bighaat.com/products/us-312-hybrid-paddy-rice
STRESS TOLERANCE (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence): No evidence found. Hybrid notes say avoid extreme low or high temperatures at panicle initiation and flowering (general agronomy, not a variety-specific rating) -- https://www.agriculture-xprt.com/products/us-agriseeds-model-us-312-hybrid-rice-seeds-853682

DISEASE AND PEST: Blast resistance is claimed -- https://www.agriculture-xprt.com/products/us-agriseeds-model-us-312-hybrid-rice-seeds-853682 ; disease resistance claimed for the related "US 312 Gold" research paddy (no test data) -- https://www.somaniagro.com/products/us-312-gold ; sucking-pest tolerance listed -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/us-312-hybrid-paddy-rice

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Maturity 120-125 days, semi-dwarf (about 105 cm), large panicles, long slender grains, acceptable cooking quality, potential yield about 2.8-3 t/acre under normal conditions -- https://www.agriculture-xprt.com/products/us-agriseeds-model-us-312-hybrid-rice-seeds-853682 ; US 312 Gold: 125-130 days, mid-duration, long bold grains -- https://www.somaniagro.com/products/us-312-gold ; seed-rate and nursery practice (6 kg presoaked seed, 21-25 day seedlings, one per hill) -- https://www.agriculture-xprt.com/products/us-agriseeds-model-us-312-hybrid-rice-seeds-853682
Multi-location or field trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. Parentage not found (CSC record also says "Not specified"). The hybrid status (SeedWorks hybrid) is from commercial listings only.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developed by SeedWorks (SeedWorks International Pvt. Ltd./Seed Works International Limited); the listing says extensive hybrid research by SeedWorks led to its release and notification for irrigated tracts of several states -- https://www.agriculture-xprt.com/products/us-agriseeds-model-us-312-hybrid-rice-seeds-853682 ; company listing as Seed Works International Limited, Malkajgiri, Telangana -- https://www.indiamart.com/ms-seed-works-international-pvt-ltd/paddy-seeds.html
Lead breeder name(s) and station: No evidence found.
Year of release: No evidence found (CSC year recorded as NaT; no notification year found).

CONTACT DETAILS: No individual breeder contact found. Company-level location only: Seed Works International Limited, Malkajgiri, Telangana (no address, email or phone found) -- https://www.indiamart.com/ms-seed-works-international-pvt-ltd/paddy-seeds.html
Official institute contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for US 312 in peer-reviewed journals, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers. Search results were unrelated (for example, the Sri Lankan red rice Bw 312 is a different variety: https://reference-global.com/download/article/10.4038/ta.v168i3.59.pdf ), so none is listed here.

SEED AVAILABILITY: Commercial sellers list US 312 hybrid seed: BigHaat online -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/us-312-hybrid-paddy-rice ; SeedWorks/Indiamart listing -- https://www.indiamart.com/ms-seed-works-international-pvt-ltd/paddy-seeds.html ; Somani Agro lists US 312 Gold -- https://www.somaniagro.com/products/us-312-gold
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales: No evidence found. Seednet gazette index did not show a US-316 entry -- https://seednet.gov.in/SeedGO/Index.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES: Listing says the hybrid is released for irrigated tracts of "many states" but names none -- https://www.agriculture-xprt.com/products/us-agriseeds-model-us-312-hybrid-rice-seeds-853682 ; recommended_states_raw is "Not specified" and no state notification was found.

Limitations: The search budget ran out after the first batch of four queries. The planned follow-ups (IET 19513 variety-code search, SeedWorks breeder/contact search, and dealer/seed-availability search) were not completed, so the breeder, contact, and Seednet gaps may be fillable with further searching. Commercial pages are not official sources and their performance claims are unverified.

drought.details: The variety Uttar Ganga (IET 28840) was proposed and discussed in the context of breeding for multiple biotic and abiotic stress tolerance, including drought. Its development utilized Nilachal, a parent associated with stress and heat stress tolerance, with an aim for resistance to drought.

heat.details: Uttar Ganga was developed using Nilachal, a parent specifically linked to heat stress tolerance.

salinity.details: The variety IET 28840 (Uttar Ganga) was proposed in a discussion that also included saline tolerant varieties, but its specific salinity tolerance level is not explicitly stated.

flood.details: No specific information regarding the variety's tolerance to general flooding was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Uttar Ganga is expected to possess disease resistance, as its development, using Nilachal as a parent, aimed to create cultivars resistant to diseases. Discussions around its proposal mentioned the objective of developing varieties with resistance to specific diseases like bacterial blight (referencing genes like Xa1, Xa3, Xa4, xa5) and general disease resistance. Nilachal is also cited for its role in disease resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Uttar Ganga (IET 28840) was listed in the context of proposals for multiple pest resistant rice varieties. Its development, using parent Nilachal, aimed for resistance to pests.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VL 7620 (rice / PADDY (DHAN))

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "VL 7620", so one set of searches covered both. The four searches were: "VL 7620 rice variety", "VL 7620 rice breeder developed by Vivekanand Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan", "VL 7620 rice research paper", and "VL 7620 paddy seed availability". No search returned a page naming VL 7620 as a rice variety. Results for other VPKAS varieties (VL Dhan 159, VL Dhan 160, VL Barik Dhan, VL Dhan 88) and an LSU (Louisiana) variety table that lists "7620" as a column entry were discarded as other varieties or other programmes. No Seednet portal page was reached.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no stress-tolerance data for VL 7620. The only "7620" match was a Louisiana State University variety table, which is a different programme and was discarded. -- https://www.lsuagcenter.com/~/media/system/a/2/9/a/a29a7881dfbe72a0d19e1caad7a1d97a/pub2270_ricevarieties2017_finalpdf.pdf (discarded)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page linked VL 7620 to disease or pest reaction. Results on blast and sheath blight concerned LSU varieties and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for VL 7620 were returned.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage or pedigree for VL 7620 was returned. The parentage field in the record is "Not specified", and no source supplied it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution-level only: the variety is listed as ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, but no page ties VL 7620 to it. -- https://ccafs.cgiar.org/partner/vivekananda-parvatiya-krishi-anusandhan-sansthan
Lead breeder: No evidence found. A ResearchGate profile for Lakshmi Kant lists him as Research Director at VPKAS, but its breeding interests are wheat and maize, and nothing links him to VL 7620, so he is not attributed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Lakshmi-Kant-3
The VPKAS other-variety pages (VL Dhan 159, VL Dhan 160, VL Barik Dhan, VL Dhan 88) show the institute's rice programme but are not evidence for VL 7620.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level website: http://www.vpkas.nic.in/ -- https://ccafs.cgiar.org/partner/vivekananda-parvatiya-krishi-anusandhan-sansthan (listed with location "India, Almorah")
Institute location as found: Almora, Uttarakhand -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395348090_List_Agri_Institutes
Official email, phone, and full postal address: No evidence found. The ResearchGate keyword list contains the string "Almora-263", which is probably a postal code but is not confirmed as an address; treat it as unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Lakshmi-Kant-3
Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, AICRP or ICAR report, or KrishiKosh thesis mentioning VL 7620 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The OSSC (Odisha State Seeds Corporation) varieties list and the IFFDC seed availability page do not include VL 7620. The retailer and marketplace pages returned were also unrelated. -- https://ossc.nic.in/Marketing/AvailabilityofSeeds ; https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. VL 7620 is not named in any returned page, so no notified states or zones can be recorded. The record's "Not specified in table" entry remains unverified.

Searches were limited to four, so the Seednet portal, the CSC release minutes, the KrishiKosh repository, and the VPKAS site were not checked directly. Those are the next places to look for VL 7620 details.
